stories.summary: Anant Singh Daughter Wedding: बिहार के मोकामा से विधायक अनंत सिंह की बेटी शिवांगी की शादी को लेकर उनके पैतृक गांव नदवां में भव्य तैयारियां की गई हैं। शिवांगी की शादी ऋषिकेश कुमार के साथ हो रही है। इस शादी में शामिल होने के लिए कई बड़े नेता और खास मेहमान पहुंच रहे हैं। उत्तर प्रदेश के पूर्व सांसद और बाहुबली नेता बृजभूषण सिंह भी पटना पहुंचे। उन्होंने अनंत सिंह के साथ अपने पुराने रिश्ते का जिक्र किया। शादी में मेहमानों के लिए 25 बीघे में पंडाल बनाया गया है। करीब चार लाख लोगों के खाने का इंतजाम किया गया है। वहीं, हेलीकॉप्टर से आने वाले मेहमानों के लिए तीन हेलीपैड भी तैयार किए गए हैं।

stories.title: 2 Bangkok gold smugglers arrested with ₹1.30 crore haul:Gorakhpur Police exposes duo after they file false robbery complaint
stories.summary: Gorakhpur Cantonment police arrested two members of a gang involved in smuggling gold from Bangkok on Wednesday. Around 960 grams of gold, valued at approximately ₹1 crore 30 lakh, was recovered from the accused. Cash worth ₹2 lakh was also recovered. The accused had filed a false report with the police about a robbery on 22 November in an attempt to seize the smuggled jewellery. An investigation into the report exposed the entire operation. The arrested accused have been identified as Ashutosh Shukla of Jharkata in the Gola police station area and Sunil Mishra of Hata Bazaar in Gagaha. After strict questioning of the accused, Cantt police registered an FIR against 10 people under serious sections on Wednesday (25 Nov). The case names both accused, Sunil Mishra and Ashutosh Shukla, along with Ajay Yadav, Deepak Tiwari, Krishnakant, Chandan Tiwari, Ayush alias Nikhil and Priyanshu Tripathi, among others. Police are conducting raids to arrest the accused who are absconding. City SP exposes gang at press conference City SP Nimish Patil briefed the media about the gang at a press conference held at 2:30 p.m. at the White House in the police lines. He said police arrested two members of the gang near Mohaddipur crossing late on Monday night. Two gold chains, a gold bangle and ₹2 lakh in cash were recovered from them. The accused had misled the police by giving false information about a robbery so that the gold could be disposed of. Interrogation revealed the entire operation During interrogation, Ashutosh Mishra and Sunil Mishra said that several people like them work for Deepak Tiwari, a resident of Mukhlispur in Bansgaon. Deepak Tiwari lives in Lucknow with his brother, Mukesh Tiwari. The gold smuggling operation is carried out through Deepak Tiwari. Ashutosh said that on 22 November 2026, he came to Gorakhpur from Lucknow via Kolkata with his associate Ajay Yadav, carrying Deepak Tiwari's gold, two chains and a bangle. They planned to go via Gorakhpur Student Union Crossing to Ghantaghar to sell the gold, but after seeing a large police presence at the crossing, he falsely informed the police that he had been robbed. The police believed their account and began investigating, during which he handed all the gold to Ajay Yadav and left the scene. Both accused said they had gone to Ghantaghar on 24 November to sell the chains and bangle. When they arrived, they found that it was Tuesday and were unable to sell the gold because the market was closed. When asked about the ₹2 lakh recovered from them, both said they had gone to Prayag Bullion Traders in Ghantaghar to sell the gold. They already knew the owner. The shop was closed, but they met him outside. After examining the gold, he gave them ₹2 lakh, which they divided equally between themselves, taking ₹1 lakh each. They said they would receive the full payment after the market reopened.

The seriously injured dog was taken to hospital for treatment. After battling for life for two days, the dog died. It is alleged that the dog had bitten a goat. Angered by this, the boys attacked it. Police have registered a case in connection with the incident and are searching for the accused. Beaten for biting a goat According to Deepanshu Verma, a resident of Bhikhampur, the incident took place at 11:42 am on 22 November. Six to eight boys surrounded the dog and beat it brutally. They seriously injured it by driving a metal rod into its eye. The injured dog was admitted to the Jeev Ashray Centre, where it received treatment for two days. It died at 12:19 pm on Tuesday. Police identifying suspects from video People in the neighbourhood had recorded a video of the incident, which has now emerged. Police are using the video to identify the suspects. One of the suspects is reportedly named Narayan. The identities of the other suspects are being established. Police have registered a case following a complaint from local residents. Deepanshu has demanded a fair investigation and strict action against all the accused. Inspector Mahanagar said that after registering the case, the accused were being identified.

stories.title: Meerut hostage-taker breaks down, pleads for forgiveness:Says, ‘I made a mistake, forgive me’; had threatened, ‘I won’t let you be with anyone else’
stories.summary: A man accused of holding a 24-year-old woman hostage at a hotel in Meerut was arrested after an encounter on Wednesday. After his arrest, Salman was seen crying and apologising to police personnel. He was heard saying, “Sir, I made a mistake. Please forgive me. I won’t do it again.” Salman is a resident of Shahpur Jainpur in the Rohta police station area of Meerut. A case has been registered against him following the woman’s complaint. Earlier on Wednesday, the SSP visited Hotel Square, inspected the premises and got the hotel vacated. It was subsequently sealed. How was Salman arrested? SSP BBGTS Murthy said a complaint had been received at Sadar Bazaar police station alleging that a man named Salman had held a Dalit woman hostage and sexually assaulted her. Based on the complaint, a case was registered under the relevant sections and legal proceedings were initiated. He said police received information on Wednesday that the accused was hiding near an under-construction underpass close to Nahar Narhera village in the Lohia Nagar police station area. Teams from Lohia Nagar and Sadar Bazaar police stations reached the spot and cordoned off the area. According to police, the accused opened fire at the police team after finding himself surrounded. When the police tried to catch him, he climbed onto a nearby bridge and attempted to flee. During the chase, he slipped and fell from the bridge. Both his hands were injured. He was taken to hospital for treatment. See three pictures related to the hotel incident Girl ran out of hotel screaming for help It was around 1.30 pm on Tuesday. A girl ran out of Hotel Square in the Abu Lane market in the Sadar Bazaar area, shouting for help. A young man came running after her, grabbed her by the hair, lifted her in his arms and tried to take her back inside the hotel. Hearing her screams, people nearby rushed to the spot. Seeing the crowd, the accused left her and ran inside the hotel. People tried to catch him, but hotel employees stopped them. A commotion continued for quite some time. Meanwhile, the accused managed to escape from the hotel's third-floor terrace. According to police, the man had held the girl hostage inside the hotel and threatened her with a knife. He would tell her, “If you cannot be mine, I won't let you be anyone else's either. I will kill you.” After receiving information, police reached the spot and took the woman to the police station. The accused, Salman, is married. Girl worked with Salman at a company According to police, the girl, a resident of Ghaziabad, met Salman, who belongs to the Kankarkhera police station area of Meerut, around a year ago. Both worked at a private company. They started talking and gradually began meeting each other. Recently, the girl's marriage was fixed. She then quit her job, and the two stopped meeting. Salman tried several times to meet her, but she refused. Around two days ago, the girl came to Meerut to visit a friend. Salman learnt about this. On the pretext of helping her find a job, he called her and took her to Hotel Square, where he locked her inside a room. Eyewitness says hotel employees helped the accused escape Eyewitness Aman said the girl came out of the hotel in a distressed condition. Her clothes were dishevelled, and she was screaming for help. A man named Salman was with her and was trying to forcibly take her away. When they rushed to the spot, the accused left her and ran inside the hotel. Hotel employees stopped people from entering Aman said they ran inside the hotel to catch the accused, but the employees stopped them. They said they would bring him downstairs themselves. Meanwhile, the accused jumped from the third-floor terrace onto a neighbouring house and escaped. Two people chased him, but could not catch him. The hotel employees then shut the rear door. Later, when they questioned the woman, she told them that Salman had kept her locked in a hotel room throughout the night and had not allowed her to leave. He had also threatened her with a knife. They then informed the police. Police seal hotel SP City Vinayak Gopal Bhosale said a case had been registered based on the woman's complaint. On Wednesday morning, the SSP visited the hotel, inspected the premises and got it vacated. Hotel Square was then sealed. SSP BBGTS Murthy said the hotel was sealed primarily to preserve evidence at the crime scene. This would prevent anyone from tampering with the evidence until the investigation was completed. Hindutva leader demands encounter Sachin Sirohi, national president of the All India Hindu Suraksha Sangathan, demanded a ‘half encounter’ of the accused. He said the SSP himself had confirmed that Salman had opened fire at the police. Despite this, no ‘half encounter’ was carried out. He alleged that the police took pity on Salman after he sustained injuries to his hands and legs. He called the police action condemnable and said the police had failed to teach such an accused a lesson.

He said, "The pairing of the two boys used to fail after the election results were announced, but this time it has already failed before the election." Yogi said that while meetings were being held between the two parties over seats, candidates were being announced on the other side. "What could be a greater insult than this?" he asked. A political contest to outwit one another is under way between the two parties. The condition of Congress, the country's oldest political party, is the result of its negative thinking. The people are repeatedly rejecting these parties. The Chief Minister was speaking at the ABP Conclave. He accused the SP of practising dynastic politics and not respecting the sentiments of Ram devotees. He said, "'Radhe-Radhe' is only the beginning; the time for 'Ram naam satya' is drawing near for the SP." Yogi says SP should apologise to Ram devotees On Akhilesh's visit to Ayodhya and questions related to Sanatan Dharma, Chief Minister Yogi said that riding two boats was always dangerous. He said visiting Ayodhya was a good thing, but the Samajwadi Party should also apologise to Ram devotees. He said that if this good sense had prevailed in the 1990s, there would have been no need to open fire on Ram devotees. Rejecting speculation about differences among the NDA's alliance partners, the Chief Minister made it clear that all the allies, including the Nishad Party and the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party, were united and would contest the elections together. PDA described as 'Parivar Development Authority' The Chief Minister took a swipe at the Samajwadi Party's PDA slogan, describing it as the "Parivar Development Authority". He alleged that the party's politics is limited to its own family. 'Strict action against those challenging the law will continue' Responding to the Opposition's allegations concerning bulldozer action and encounters, the Chief Minister said that women's safety and respect for traders were the government's top priorities. Strict action against those challenging the law will continue. On the possibility of sitting legislators being denied tickets, he said that in the BJP, the parliamentary board takes the final decision after the election committee's recommendation, and that the party works to bring people together. He described Prime Minister Narendra Modi as the BJP's universally accepted leader and ideal, as well as a symbol of India's global stature. Responding to a question about the chief ministerial face, he said that the lotus symbol was supreme for the BJP. CM hits back at Akhilesh's 'Infiltrator' remark During the programme's rapid-fire round, the Chief Minister responded to various words. He described India as the 'World Spiritual Powerhouse', Uttar Pradesh as having 'Unlimited Potential', Lord Ram as the 'embodiment of dharma' and the BJP as 'Nation First'. The CM compared Rahul Gandhi to a rocket that is launched but fails to take off successfully. Asked about performing his mother's last rites on the day she died and receiving Prime Minister Modi, he said, "This is the duty of an ascetic." Hitting back at Akhilesh Yadav's 'infiltrator' remark, the Chief Minister said that he is a resident of undivided Uttar Pradesh and has been serving in Gorakhpur since 1992 under the Nath sect's tradition. Speaking in the context of Uttarakhand, he said that the waters of the Ganga, Yamuna and Saryu originate in Devbhoomi Uttarakhand. The state's soldiers protect the country's borders, and therefore there should be a sense of gratitude towards Uttarakhand. He said he did not need any certificate for his ascetic faith or identity. Claim that Uttar Pradesh's economy has grown threefold Yogi claimed that Uttar Pradesh had transformed from a 'BIMARU' state into an engine of development. Since 2017, the state's economy, per capita income and budget have grown more than threefold. He said that the state previously had factories manufacturing illegal country-made pistols and bombs, but now revolvers, rifles and BrahMos missiles are being manufactured. The state has received investment proposals worth ₹50 lakh crore, and 36 sector-based policies have been formulated to attract investment. According to the chief minister, Uttar Pradesh accounts for 55% of the country's mobile phone production and 60% of electronic component production. The MSME and ODOP schemes are providing employment to 3.25 crore people. He said that housing-related disputes involving 4 lakh homebuyers had been resolved through dialogue between builders and buyers. Target of 10.5 lakh appointments Yogi said that around 9.75 lakh appointment letters had already been issued to young people. The government's target is to raise this figure to 10.5 lakh by 26 January. Warning that the safety of women, traders and investors would be ensured, he said that those who cast an evil eye on daughters, traders and women walking on the streets had only two places to go-jail or hell. Speaking about the political leadership and the BJP's preparations for the election, the Chief Minister named Prime Minister Narendra Modi as his role model. He said he was an ordinary party worker and would fulfil whatever responsibility was assigned to him.

stories.title: Mock aircraft crash alert at Lucknow airport:250 personnel lead rescue operation as passengers are evacuated amid flames
stories.summary: A rescue and relief exercise simulating an aircraft accident was conducted at Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport in Lucknow on Wednesday. A crash scene was created after a simulated landing failure. As soon as the alert was sounded, fire engines, ambulances and rescue teams reached the site. The exercise covered everything from extinguishing the fire to evacuating passengers. Around 250 officers and employees took part. During the full-scale Aerodrome Emergency Exercise 'Sahas-2026' held at the airport, various agencies jointly assessed their preparedness to deal with an emergency. The exercise was conducted from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. See 4 pictures... Crash scene recreated after simulated landing failure A crash scenario was created during the exercise after the aircraft's landing failed. As soon as the information was received, air traffic control, the firefighting team, CISF and the medical team became active. Firefighters extinguished the blaze. The rescue team practised evacuating passengers from the aircraft. The process of taking the injured to hospital by ambulance was also tested. 250 personnel took charge Airport administration, CISF, NDRF, SDRF, Uttar Pradesh Police, the Fire Department, district administration and medical teams took part in the exercise. Personnel from the Sarojini Nagar Fire Station, Dial-112 and Air Force Station Bakshi Ka Talab also participated. Medical teams from Chandan Hospital and OP Chaudhary Hospital were present. Fire tenders, ambulances, rescue vehicles and modern firefighting equipment were used. Their deployment was used to assess the availability of resources during an emergency and coordination among the agencies. Preparedness assessed against international standards 'Sahas-2026' was conducted in accordance with ICAO and DGCA standards. The exercise reviewed the emergency response plan, communication systems, crisis management and rescue operations. It also assessed how quickly all agencies could respond together in the event of an accident. Exercise conducted after NOTAM issued, flights remain normal The airport administration had issued a NOTAM in advance for the exercise. A mock drill was conducted at the scheduled time. Regular air operations were not affected. Flights continued to operate normally during the exercise, and passengers faced no inconvenience.

stories.title: Mother daughter murdered in Ghazipur:Bodies found inside house with throats slit, gate locked from outside
stories.summary: The bodies of a 35-year-old woman and her eight-year-old daughter were found inside their house in Ghazipur at around 8 am on Wednesday. Both had been killed with a sharp weapon. The mother and daughter were alone at home at the time of the incident, and the main gate was locked from outside. The deceased were identified as Jaymoon Nisha (35) and her daughter, Aiman Nisha (8). After receiving information about the double murder, police reached the spot and began an investigation. The incident took place in Dharwan village, under the Nandganj police station area, about 25 km from the district headquarters. See 2 pictures... Read the full case... Mohammad Anirullah, the brother of Qasimabad resident Zaibun Nisha, said he had called his sister on Tuesday, but her mobile phone was switched off. When he contacted neighbours on Wednesday morning, he was informed that the house was locked. He then sent his sisters, Zubeida Khatun and Shabana Khatun, to the spot. They broke open the lock and found Zaibun Nisha's blood-soaked body lying on the floor inside. Her daughter's body was found lying on the bed. Both had marks on their necks caused by blows from a sharp weapon. Dispute over demand to rent land Anirullah has accused Parvez alias Sonu, a resident of the village, of the murders. He said the accused had threatened his sister in the past as well. He had been asking the family to rent out land to him, which had led to an ongoing dispute. According to the brother, a complaint had been lodged earlier over the threats, but a settlement was reached later. Despite this, the threats continued. The family suspects that the murders were committed due to this enmity. Her brother said that Jaibun Nisha's husband, Gulfaam, is a resident of Meerut and that the couple had separated eight years ago. Jaibun Nisha had built a house in Nandganj and lived there with her eight-year-old daughter. SP reaches the scene and conducts investigation Superintendent of Police Vinay Kumar Singh reached the scene after receiving information about the double murder. He inspected the site and spoke to the family members. The SP said the family members had accused an acquaintance of carrying out the crime. The police are investigating the case from all angles. Evidence is being collected from the scene, and steps are being taken to send both bodies for post-mortem examinations. The SP has said that the incident will be solved soon.

stories.title: SC quashes CBI, ED probe order in Rahul’s assets case:Sends matter back to Allahabad HC, directs it to make Gandhi a party
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside an Allahabad High Court order directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to probe allegations of disproportionate assets against Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, Bar and Bench reported. A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana sent the matter back to the High Court for fresh consideration. It also directed the High Court to make Gandhi a party to the case and give him an opportunity to be heard before passing any orders. High Court had ordered CBI, ED to verify allegations In May, the Allahabad High Court directed the CBI and ED to verify claims made by BJP worker S Vignesh Shishir, who had sought an investigation against Gandhi and other members of his family. The High Court later asked the CBI to file a fresh affidavit detailing the progress of its inquiry. On July 20, a Bench of Justice Brij Raj Singh and Justice Rajesh Singh Chauhan expressed dissatisfaction with the agency's response, saying it did not adequately explain the investigation's progress. The Bench also observed that the ED had taken the required steps and could proceed further if the investigation revealed material warranting action. Gandhi challenged High Court directions in Supreme Court Gandhi challenged the High Court's directions before the Supreme Court. He argued that Shishir had no locus standi to file the petition and had not disclosed his credentials. Gandhi also questioned how confidential proceedings in the matter had been reported in newspapers. On August 17, the Supreme Court flagged that the High Court had passed orders without hearing Gandhi. It directed the High Court to defer the proceedings and questioned why the Congress leader had not been given an opportunity to present his side. The Supreme Court has now set aside the High Court orders and remanded the matter for a fresh hearing. Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal appeared for Gandhi. Separate case alleges Gandhi holds British passport In a separate petition pending before the Allahabad High Court, Shishir has sought criminal action against Gandhi, alleging violations of citizenship laws. He has claimed that the Congress leader holds a British passport in addition to his Indian passport. The High Court had initially ordered the registration of an FIR against Gandhi in the case. However, the judge later withheld the order and recused himself after Shishir made certain social media posts related to the matter. The case remains pending before the High Court.

stories.title: UP transfers 10 IPS officers, including 6 women:Mavis Talk shifted to Lucknow; 18 additional SPs also transferred
stories.summary: Major police reshuffle in UP ahead of Assembly elections: 10 IPS, 18 Additional SPs transferred; several women officers among those moved A major reshuffle has taken place in the Uttar Pradesh Police ahead of the Assembly elections. The government has transferred 10 IPS officers and 18 Additional Superintendents of Police (ASP). Officers from several police commissionerates have also been moved. Of the 10 IPS officers, six are women, while five of the 18 Additional SPs are women. Puneet Dwivedi, who was awaiting posting, has been appointed ACP in the Lucknow Police Commissionerate. Neetu has been transferred from Varanasi to the Noida Police Commissionerate. Shiva Singh has been moved from Kanpur to Agra, Amit Kumawat from Lucknow to Ghaziabad, and Kiran Yadav has been shifted to the Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) headquarters in Lucknow. Pushkar Verma has been transferred from Prayagraj to Fatehgarh, Aditya from Agra to Badaun, Shaivya Goyal from Noida to Ghaziabad, Bhavre Diksha Arun from Shahjahanpur to Meerut, and Mavis Talk from Sonbhadra to Lucknow. The IPS officers transferred include Additional SP- and Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police-rank officers from the 2020, 2021 and 2022 batches. Mamta Kuril transferred from Aligarh to Muzaffarnagar The list of 18 Additional SP transfers includes Kumar Ranvijay Singh, Additional SP (City), Moradabad, who has been appointed Additional SP (Rural), Azamgarh. ASP Anoop Kumar has been transferred from Mau to Sonbhadra. Devendra Singh-1, who was serving as Deputy Commandant of the PAC in Mirzapur, has been appointed Additional SP (Rural), Shahjahanpur. Indu Prabha Singh has been appointed Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police in Lucknow. She had earlier been transferred to the Kanpur Nagar Police Commissionerate. Mamta Kuril has been transferred from the post of ASP (Crime), Aligarh, to ASP (Traffic), Muzaffarnagar.

stories.title: Yogi to inaugurate Kashi Tamil Sangamam on November 28:1,400 delegates will reach Namo Ghat in 7 groups
stories.summary: The fifth edition of the Kashi Tamil Sangamam, which connects the cultural heritage of North and South India, will begin in Kashi on 28 November. The event, which will continue until 12 December, will be inaugurated by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Organised by the Union Ministry of Education, the main ceremony will be held at Namo Ghat. This time, around 1,400 representatives from Tamil Nadu will arrive in Kashi in seven groups. This year's theme is 'Tirukkural Pailavom', meaning 'Let us practise Tirukkural'. Through the theme, the teachings related to ethics, morality and the values of life in Tirukkural, the famous classical work of Tamil literature, will be conveyed to students and young people across the country. 1,400 representatives to arrive in seven groups Representatives from Tamil Nadu have been divided into seven groups: students, teachers, writers and media professionals, people associated with the agricultural sector, professionals and artisans, women, and spiritual leaders. Each group will have around 200 participants. During the eight-day visit, the representatives will also travel to Prayagraj and Ayodhya, along with Kashi. They will visit religious, cultural and historical sites there. Students from 1,000 educational institutions will also join This time, students from 1,000 higher educational institutions across the country will also be included in the event. Students interested in the Tirukkural will be selected from each institution on the basis of merit. The selected students will receive online training in the 22 scheduled languages and English. This will be followed by a month of research and academic activities. Students will have to prepare a four- to 10-page article or research note on the Tirukkural. They will also have to give a one-hour presentation at their institution. Eligible students who fulfil the prescribed conditions will be awarded a scholarship of ₹10,000. They will experience Kashi's religious and Tamil heritage During their stay in Kashi, the representatives will visit major religious and historical sites, including the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Sarnath, BHU, Ramnagar Fort and Bharat Mata Temple. The programme will also include the Ganga Aarti, a dip in the Ganga, academic discussions and cultural events. Sites associated with Tamil heritage have also been given a special place in the itinerary. The delegates will visit the ancestral home of poet Subramania Bharati, Kedar Ghat and Kashi Math, known as 'Little Tamil Nadu'. An academic interaction will be held at the Tamil Department of Banaras Hindu University. The delegates will then visit the Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj and the Shri Ram Temple in Ayodhya.

stories.title: Imran Masood warns, 'We won't be trampled underfoot':Says, 'Rahul's 'magic' helped Akhilesh win 37 seats, otherwise parties got just 5 each'
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Congress working president Imran Masood is extremely unhappy with Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. After the Samajwadi Party (SP) announced candidates for five seats, Masood openly criticised the party. In a warning tone, he said, We are ready to make every possible compromise for the alliance, but we won't be trampled underfoot. Masood also said it was Rahul Gandhi's “miracle” that Akhilesh won 37 seats in 2024. Otherwise, he said, the SP had won only five seats each when it contested elections in an alliance in 2019 and 2014. Without naming him directly, Masood also targeted Akhilesh Yadav. He said Rahul Gandhi was the only guarantee of defeating the BJP and that no one else in the country could defeat the party. Read the exclusive interview… Q: What do you have to say about the SP announcing five candidates while seat-sharing talks are still underway? Imran Masood: It is their decision. It is their party, and they are free to make decisions for it. They can release the list in whichever way they want. What can I say about that? But when it comes to an alliance, things cannot work like this. You say one thing during discussions and do something else. That is not right. Q: The SP has given a ticket to one of its sitting MLAs. What is wrong with that? Imran Masood: Why are they sitting MLAs? I joined you in 2022 with two MLAs, and both were sitting MLAs. I held discussions based on your promises and helped you win both seats. After that, what happened during my own election does not need to be explained. Despite everything, I won those two seats by margins of 40,000 and 47,000 votes. If we are talking about strengthening the alliance, then it should function like an alliance. You simply said that you would start with 26 seats. We did not even ask you for seats. Are we beggars? Will you now decide on your own where we should contest? We are not here to let you make all the decisions for us. Q: Will the talks remain stalled or reach a conclusion? Imran Masood: I don't know. Look, there should be seriousness in every matter. Talks on the alliance were underway in Delhi. What were those discussions about? We held marathon meetings for two days. Why did we do all that? If you want to announce candidates like this, you might as well announce them for all 403 seats. What difference does it make? Q: Akhilesh Yadav says this is the first list of 26 candidates. Imran Masood: We did not ask you for 26 seats. Why are you announcing them? We never asked you to give us these 26 seats. We did not give you any list. If you are announcing your own list, then select candidates from it. When did we give you these seats that you have announced them? Q: What will be your stand on the two Saharanpur seats where the SP has fielded candidates? Imran Masood: I will work according to whatever my party tells me. But we have to protect our identity and our party. We have repeatedly said that we are ready for every possible compromise. But that does not mean you can crush us. That is not acceptable. Q: It has been said that you will field candidates on all seven seats in Saharanpur. Imran Masood: I have not said anything like that so far. But let me ask you something. In 2022, there was a lot of talk about forming the government. People kept saying the government was being formed. We were also drawn into the alliance. The SBSP joined, along with several other parties. The Rashtriya Lok Dal was also there. Yet, you could not go beyond 111 seats. It was Rahul Gandhi's miracle that you reached 43 seats. That alliance was Rahul Gandhi's. Otherwise, there was an alliance in 2019 as well. The SP and BSP had contested together. Where did you stand then? You could win only five seats. You won only five in 2014 as well. If we assess all these things, you cannot claim that we do not have people capable of working on the ground. In this country, Rahul Gandhi is the only guarantee of defeating the BJP. There is no other guarantee in the country from anyone who can claim to defeat the BJP. Q: What do you think is the future of the alliance? Imran Masood: I don't know what its future will be. I am not an astrologer who can predict the future. I simply don't know what will happen. Q: Will your next scheduled meeting take place after this decision by the SP? Imran Masood: What is the point of holding those meetings? The meeting will take place in Delhi, while the list will be announced from Lucknow. We did not even discuss the matter in the meeting, and you will simply announce a list and say that you have given us 26 seats. What does that mean? You were giving 35 seats to the RLD. This kind of behaviour is deeply insulting. Q: Is this your personal anger or the Congress's anger? Imran Masood: What am I? I am the Congress. This is an insult to the party and its workers. What do you mean by 26 seats? We are not asking you for seats. You want to give us all the seats you have lost and then tell us that our strike rate is not good. Well, we are not going to function according to your wishes.

stories.title: Suresh Gautam appointed new BSP district president:Party changes 6 district presidents in 11 months in Gorakhpur, some lasted just 7 days, others 100
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) has repeatedly changed its district president. In the past 11 months, the party has entrusted six leaders with this responsibility. It has now changed the district president once again and handed the reins to a new face. Jaikaar Prasad, who was appointed district president on 17 August, has been removed from the post and given responsibility as divisional co-ordinator. Suresh Kumar Gautam has been appointed the new district president in his place. The appointment order was issued on the night of 24 November. Suresh Kumar Gautam has previously served as district president. He has also been responsible for four districts as the chief divisional co-ordinator. He is considered a senior leader in the party. The repeated changes have also left workers confused. Some removed after seven days, others after 100 days Gorakhpur has been a strong political base for the BSP in eastern Uttar Pradesh. However, for some time now, the party has been unable to settle on stable leadership for its organisation here. The repeated changes of district president are creating a situation of instability within the organisation. On 20 January, Ghanshyam Rahi, who had previously served as district president twice, was given the responsibility for a third time. But just seven days later, he was removed and Hari Prakash Nishad was appointed district president. On 12 June, Santosh Kumar Jigyasu was given the responsibility in place of Hari Prakash Nishad. Within two months, Santosh Kumar Jigyasu was appointed chief mandal coordinator. On 4 August, Rishi Kapoor was made district president for the second time, but he was removed on 17 August and Jaikar Prasad was handed the reins. Now, around 100 days later, Jaikar Prasad has also been removed. First, know when and to whom the responsibility of district president was given Jigyasu became district president immediately after returning from expulsion Santosh Kumar Jigyasu was the Bahujan Samaj Party's district president during the 2022 Assembly elections. He was also holding the same responsibility during the 2023 municipal elections. He was expelled from the party for allegedly campaigning against the party's candidate in Ghaghasra Nagar Panchayat. He returned to the party on 12 June 2026. He was appointed district president on the same day. However, around two months later, he was given the responsibility of chief divisional coordinator. Experts say: Repeated changes are affecting the organisation Senior journalist DBB Mishra said district presidents are not changed so frequently in any political party. In the Bahujan Samaj Party, the same old faces are repeatedly being given a chance. The district president is the organisation's highest-ranking post in a district. Appointments to the post should be made after careful consideration. According to him, changing district presidents six times in 11 months points to immature decision-making. Such changes close to elections could affect the organisation. Traditionally, the BSP has appointed district presidents from the Dalit community. A district president should be given a tenure of at least two years to strengthen the organisation. Who is Suresh Kumar Gautam, the BSP's new district president? Suresh Kumar Gautam is a long-time BSP worker. He had also served as district president before 2007. In addition, he has been responsible for four districts as the chief divisional coordinator. He is a resident of Sisai village in the Pali block of the Sahjanwa Assembly constituency. His village lies on the border of the Sahjanwa and Campierganj Assembly constituencies. Suresh Gautam says he will work with party workers to bring the BSP to power. Learn about the leaders appointed as district presidents... Ghanshyam Rahi Ghanshyam Rahi, who belongs to the Scheduled Caste category, has been associated with the Bahujan Samaj Party for a long time. He has served as a councillor of the Pipraich Nagar Panchayat and has also held the responsibility of zonal coordinator. He was appointed district president three times. His third term lasted only seven days. He is currently overseeing the party's work in Gorakhpur district as divisional in-charge. Hari Prakash Nishad Hari Prakash Nishad, a resident of the Pipraich Assembly constituency, has been involved in student politics. He has also served as a district panchayat member. In the Bahujan Samaj Party, he has held the responsibilities of zonal coordinator, chief zonal coordinator and chief divisional in-charge. He is currently overseeing the work of the Backward Classes Bhaichara Committee. Santosh Kumar Jigyasu He is a resident of Ghaghsara Nagar Panchayat in the Sahjanwa area. He was expelled for campaigning against the party candidate in the 2023 municipal elections. He was appointed district president upon his return to the party on 12 June. Rishi Kapoor Rishi Kapoor is originally from Gorakhpur. He began his political career in student politics, after which he joined the BSP. He has remained with the BSP ever since and was appointed district president in 2023. The 2024 Lok Sabha election was held under his supervision. He was given the responsibility of district president for a second term on 4 August, but his responsibility was changed 13 days later. Jaikar Prasad Thirty-nine-year-old Jaikar Prasad is originally from Madaई Tola in Bansgaon block. He has been active in the BSP since 2007. He began his political journey as a booth president. After this, he took charge as the sector in-charge, assembly constituency in-charge, assembly general secretary and district in-charge. He was appointed district president on 17 August. He was removed around 100 days later. Suresh Kumar Gautam Suresh Kumar Gautam has been appointed the new district president. He is a long-time BSP worker. He had served as district president before 2007. As the chief divisional coordinator, he has been responsible for four districts. He is a resident of Pali block in the Sahjanwa Assembly constituency. His village, Sisai, lies on the border of the Sahjanwa and Campierganj Assembly constituencies. He said he would work with party workers to bring the BSP to power.

stories.title: Pratapnagar-Barauni special train to run from today:Train to pass through Gorakhpur with 19 coaches as railways respond to post-Chhath rush
stories.summary: The Railways has decided to run an additional festival special train between Pratapnagar and Barauni to manage the rush of passengers after the Chhath festival in Gorakhpur. Train number 09159, the Pratapnagar-Barauni Festival Special, will operate as a one-way service on November 25. It will pass through Gorakhpur. The train is expected to provide relief to passengers travelling across Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. According to the Railways, the train will depart from Pratapnagar at 11:50 pm. The next day, Thursday, it will reach Vadodara at 12:10 am, Godhra at 2:47 am, Ratlam at 7 am, Nagda at 7:50 am, Kota at 10:45 am, Sawai Madhopur at 12:12 pm and Gangapur City at 1 pm. It will then reach Idgah Agra at 4:25 pm, Tundla at 5:35 pm and Kanpur Central at 11 pm. Continuing its journey, the train will reach Aishbagh at 12:58 am on Friday, Barabanki at 2:25 am, Gonda at 3:40 am and Basti at 4:55 am. Train to reach Gorakhpur at 6:55 am The train will arrive in Gorakhpur at 6:55 am on Friday. From there, it will reach Narkatiaganj at 11:35 am, Muzaffarpur at 4:35 pm and Samastipur at 5:45 pm. It will finally reach Barauni at 8 pm. The journey from Pratapnagar to Barauni will take more than two days. Train to have 19 coaches The special train will have a total of 19 coaches, including 10 sleeper coaches, one general second-class sitting coach, six general coaches and two SLRD coaches. This will provide more travel options for passengers travelling with sleeper and general tickets. The Railways said the special train was being introduced in view of the additional rush of passengers after the Chhath festival. It will make travel easier for passengers at major stations along the route.

stories.title: Imran Masood praises Mayawati, says she can turn things around:‘She just needs to step out’; responds to possibility of an alliance with BSP
stories.summary: Congress MP Imran Masood has expressed anger over the Samajwadi Party's first list of candidates for the UP Assembly elections. He said, "We are not beggars waiting to get something from Akhilesh. You announced candidates without discussing it with us, so why are we even holding talks?" Speaking at a TV channel's programme, he also praised Mayawati. Imran Masood said: "If Behenji (Mayawati) steps out of her room, the political picture of the state will change completely." When asked whether Congress would form an alliance with the BSP, he said the decision rested with Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, not him. He added that a mission and movement had lost momentum simply because Behenji remained confined to her room. There was no doubt that she was a major political leader in Uttar Pradesh, but he did not know what had happened to her after 2012. She had shut herself inside her room to such an extent that she no longer stepped outside. The seat-sharing deadlock between the two parties has been intensifying. Against Congress's demand for 125 seats, the SP submitted a list of just 26 constituencies. Moreover, before further discussions could take place, the SP released its first list of five candidates at 10 pm on Tuesday. It included two seats in Saharanpur that Congress had also claimed. Earlier, Akhilesh had written on X: "We have started with the first 26 winnable seats. Talks will move forward through mutual understanding and cooperation." stories.title: Pollution rises as Kashi turns colder, mercury at 19°C:AQI crosses 100 at all four stations after Dev Deepawali, with Maldahiya recording highest pollution
stories.summary: The weather has started changing in Varanasi, with falling temperatures bringing colder conditions. At the same time, rising air pollution has become a concern. The city's minimum temperature was recorded at 19°C on Wednesday morning. Winds blew at 5 kmph, while humidity stood at 60%. The city's Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 264, falling in the poor category. According to meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh, temperatures are likely to continue falling over the coming days. Haze may increase during mornings and nights over the next week, making the cold more intense. However, sunshine during the day may provide some relief. AQI crosses 100 at all four monitoring stations after Dev Deepawali Air quality in Kashi was affected by the lamps and fireworks during Dev Deepawali celebrations. AQI readings crossed 100 at all four air quality monitoring stations in the city. Maldahiya recorded the highest AQI at 153, followed by Bhelupur at 149, BHU at 139 and Ardali Bazar at 119. Air quality was satisfactory on November 22, pollution rose the next day According to data from the Sameer app, Varanasi recorded an AQI of 54 on November 22. For the first time in November, air quality had reached the satisfactory category. However, pollution levels rose again the very next day. Data from previous years also shows a recurring rise in pollution around Dev Deepawali. The AQI was recorded at 97 in 2023, 155 in 2024 and 128 in 2025. This year's post-festival rise in pollution has once again raised concerns over air quality in the city.

stories.summary: Dev Deepavali was celebrated with great enthusiasm and grandeur in Varanasi, the city of religion and spirituality. On this auspicious occasion, the Ganga Seva Nidhi organised a special Maha Aarti at the world-famous Dashashwamedh Ghat. As evening set in, 21 priests performed the grand aarti of the River Ganga together amid Vedic chants and the sound of conch shells. Lakhs of devotees and domestic and international tourists gathered at the ghat and were mesmerised by the spectacle. The entire ghat was decorated like a bride with thousands of earthen lamps and colourful lights. Chants of 'Har Har Mahadev' filled the city with a devotional atmosphere. stories.title: 2,000 guests to attend Rinku Singh-Priya Saroj wedding in Lucknow:PM Modi invited; Akhilesh, Rahul among VVIPs; functions at Ramada hotel
stories.summary: Cricketer Rinku Singh and Samajwadi Party MP Priya Saroj will get married on December 4 at Hotel Ramada in Lucknow. Around 2,000 guests from across the country have been invited. The list of VVIP guests includes Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, former Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav, Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and MP Priyanka Gandhi. Bollywood star Shah Rukh Khan has also been invited. Members of both families will arrive at the hotel on December 3. All wedding functions, including the mehendi ceremony and other rituals and pujas, will be held at the venue. Priya Saroj will wear jewellery sourced from her local market in Pindra for the jaimala ceremony. She will also wear artificial jewellery to complement her lehenga. See three pictures... SP chief Akhilesh Yadav likely to attend with family SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has been invited by Priya Saroj and is expected to attend with his family, including his wife Dimple Yadav, daughters and son. Priya Saroj also invited Rahul Gandhi through Priyanka Gandhi. Rinku Singh personally handed invitation cards to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Invitations sent to 90 MPs and MLAs Apart from them, around 8–10 Union ministers and nearly 90 MPs and MLAs have been invited by Priya Saroj and her father, Tufani Saroj. Those invited include Union Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari, Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Kamlesh Paswan. Congress Rajya Sabha MP Rajeev Shukla is also expected to attend. UP leaders and young cricketers to attend Rinku's fellow cricketers will also start arriving from December 3. They include Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Tilak Varma, Suresh Raina, Praveen Kumar, RP Singh, Piyush Chawla and Kuldeep Yadav, among others. Bhojpuri artists, including Samar Singh, are also expected to attend. Arrangements have been made for around 2,000 guests in total. Famous Banarasi sarees purchased for Priya The wedding menu will be entirely vegetarian, with arrangements ranging from soups to desserts. Priya Saroj is getting her clothing collection from New Delhi, while some shopping has also been done in Lucknow. Famous Banarasi sarees have been purchased from Varanasi. The jewellery has been sourced from Pindra's local market, PC Jewellers in Delhi and Mohammed Zubair in Varanasi.

stories.title: Mercury dips to 9.5°C in UP, Hardoi coldest:Muzaffarnagar also shivers as nights and mornings set to get colder
stories.summary: Cold conditions have intensified in Uttar Pradesh due to snowfall in the hills. The mercury has dropped below 10°C. Over the past 24 hours, Hardoi recorded the lowest temperature at 9.5°C, followed by Muzaffarnagar at 9.8°C. On Tuesday morning, dense fog covered 15 cities, including Lakhimpur, Sitapur, Ballia, Sambhal, Bijnor and Muzaffarnagar. Visibility in Lakhimpur dropped so much that objects beyond 25 metres could not be seen on the roads. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said that wind patterns have changed after the impact of the cyclone originating in the Bay of Bengal subsided. Westerly winds are now gaining strength. As a result, minimum temperatures may drop by 3–5°C over the next week. This will make nights and early mornings colder. According to Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, Temperatures are falling due to cold and dry winds. Fog has also increased. However, clear skies are allowing good sunshine during the day. But the mercury drops rapidly after sunset. Light rainfall is possible at isolated places tomorrow. Farmers advised to take precautions while sowing and irrigating Rabi crops With the possibility of rainfall in November, farmers have been advised to remain cautious while managing Rabi crops. In particular, those sowing wheat, gram, peas and mustard in eastern UP should ensure proper drainage in their fields. Waterlogging in low-lying fields can damage crops. Farmers should avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields where rainfall has already provided sufficient moisture. Sowing and irrigation decisions should be based on weather conditions and soil moisture. BJP has 4 options to resolve UGC row:How will it address upper-caste resentment while reaching out to Dalits and OBCs?
stories.summary: One thing has become clear to the BJP: on the UGC issue, the entire upper-caste (Savarna) community—namely Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Kayasthas, and others—is not only angry, but this will also cause substantial losses in the elections. This is the reason why, during the state executive committee meeting in Lucknow on 30–31 October, state in-charge Vinod Tawde stated that the UGC controversy would be resolved before the announcement of election dates. The question is, how will it be resolved…? Sources indicate that the party is considering four options. What are these four options? What are the pros and cons of each option, and based on this, which path might the BJP choose? We will explore this in today's UP Explainer… But first, let us understand how the apprehension of electoral loss due to the UGC issue was confirmed…? The resentment of the upper castes over the UGC issue is well known, yet the BJP had assumed that it would not become an electoral issue, believing that the upper castes would eventually have to align with the BJP anyway. However, discussions regarding electoral losses began emerging across various surveys, feedback sessions, and brainstorming meetings. Subsequently, the MLC election results put the final stamp on this concern. The BJP received around 36,000 fewer votes than the SP. Moreover, slogans such as 'UGC Roll Back' and 'Withdraw the UGC rules, then talk' were written on thousands of ballot papers. Although the Election Commission rejected the votes on these ballot papers, these aggressive sentiments among educated youths made the BJP realise that this issue could disrupt calculations in the Assembly elections. Now, learn what options the BJP has to deal with this… The Supreme Court stayed the new UGC rules on 29 January 2026 and directed that the 2012 rules remain in force until further orders. That is, on an interim basis, the old system remains applicable. The government will submit in court that a balanced system can be created by making necessary amendments to the 2012 rules. Advantages: Disadvantages: Where the electoral catch lies: The BJP may get relief among its traditional upper-caste supporters, but there will remain a risk of damage to its social justice image among Dalit and backward classes. This is slightly different from the first option. Instead of strongly defending the new rules in the Supreme Court, the government will acknowledge their flaws. Seeing the apprehension of discrimination against the upper castes if the new rules are implemented, it will allow them to be struck down by the Supreme Court. Advantages: Disadvantages: Where the electoral catch lies: This could be a politically convenient route for the BJP. A direct message of relief will go to the upper castes, while the direct responsibility for scrapping the rules will not fall on the BJP government. However, the opposition may attempt to set a narrative portraying the government as anti-Dalit and anti-backward class. Under the UGC's regulatory process, the government itself withdraws or repeals the new rules. Advantages: Disadvantages: Where the electoral catch lies: This will end the anger of the upper-caste community in one stroke, but Dalit and backward castes will open a new front of protest. The SP will publicise this as an attack on the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak — Backward, Dalit, Minority) community. This is the most balanced option. The UGC should review both the old and new rules and issue a fresh circular. This should retain provisions to prevent caste-based discrimination while ensuring there is no scope for injustice against students of any category or misuse of the rules. Advantages: Disadvantages: Where the electoral catch lies: This could be the biggest balancing act for the BJP. Through this, it can claim that it neither snatched away the rights of any section nor ignored the apprehensions of any group. However, there is no guarantee that framing the rules afresh will satisfy all social sections. Which path will the BJP choose…

stories.title: Will Azam hand over his political legacy to daughter-in-law?:Five previous attempts failed, SP may field her in 2027 Assembly elections
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan walked out of jail after 365 days, but he will still be unable to contest elections. For the first time, he may be seen campaigning for his daughter-in-law. The Samajwadi Party (SP) is almost certain to launch her political career by giving her a ticket. The seats under consideration are Rampur Sadar and Swar, both considered strongholds of the Azam family. Azam's daughter-in-law is not entering politics all of a sudden. She has made five attempts in the past, but her political entry did not materialise due to political or family reasons. Now that Azam Khan and his younger son Abdullah cannot contest elections, it has become clear that his daughter-in-law, Sidra Adeeb, may not just campaign for the family in the 2027 Assembly elections but could emerge as its candidate. On five occasions between the 2022 Assembly elections and the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, speculation intensified that Sidra Adeeb Khan would contest an election. Her name came up each time, but she had to step back because Azam Khan did not give his consent. However, the equations are different this time. First, let us look at the occasions when she tried to contest elections. 1. 2022 Assembly elections Speculation began as early as November 2021 that Sidra could contest from the Rampur Sadar seat. She had told the media, “If my father-in-law, Azam Khan, asks me to contest, I have no objection.” However, Azam Khan later decided to contest from Rampur Sadar himself while he was in jail. This ended Sidra's claim to the seat. 2. Rampur Lok Sabha by-election The Rampur Lok Sabha seat fell vacant after Azam Khan became an MLA. Sidra's name came up again during the by-election in June 2022. However, instead of getting a family member a ticket, Azam Khan fielded his close aide Asim Raja. Asim lost the election. 3. Rampur Sadar Assembly by-election Azam Khan lost his membership of the Assembly after being sentenced to three years in the hate speech case. A by-election was subsequently held for the Rampur Sadar seat in December 2022. Sidra once again came forward to contest, but Azam Khan secured the ticket for Asim Raja. Asim lost again. 4. Swar Assembly by-election After Abdullah Azam's Assembly membership was cancelled in March 2023, discussions began about fielding Sidra from the Swar seat. The matter reached Akhilesh Yadav, but once again, family members did not agree. The SP then gave the ticket to Anuradha Chauhan, who also lost the election. 5. 2024 Lok Sabha elections There was speculation that Azam Khan's elder daughter-in-law would be the party's candidate for the Lok Sabha elections. The party was preparing to give her a ticket from Rampur, but according to sources, Azam Khan and the SP leadership could not reach an agreement over the candidature. The party eventually fielded Mohibullah Nadvi. Sidra may contest from these Assembly seats... Rampur has five assembly seats. The Azam family has a strong hold over three of them: Rampur Sadar, Swar and Chamraua. If Sidra Adeeb is to contest the election, the party may consider one of these seats. However, the Rampur Sadar seat slipped out of the SP's hands in the December 2022 by-election, when the BJP's Akash Saxena won. Before that, Azam Khan himself had been elected MLA from this seat 10 times. In the 2019 by-election, his wife, Dr Tazeen Fatima, also became an MLA from the same constituency. Swar is Abdullah's traditional seat The Swar Assembly seat has traditionally been held by Azam Khan's younger son, Abdullah. Abdullah won the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections by large margins. After his Assembly membership was cancelled, Shafiq Ahmed Ansari of Apna Dal (S), an NDA ally, won the seat in the May 2023 by-election. No member of the Azam family has contested from Chamraua No member of the Azam family has contested an election from the Chamraua seat. However, owing to Azam Khan's influence, the SP's Naseer Ahmed Khan is the MLA from this constituency. ‘People will vote for the daughter-in-law in Azam's name’ Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans says the SP lost the Rampur seat in the 2022 by-election and will want to win it back at any cost this time. He says, “If Sidra Adeeb, Abdullah Azam or Dr Tazeen Fatima contests, they will get votes in Azam's name. Party workers will also believe that Azam Khan himself is contesting the election.” The impact will not be limited to Rampur. It could also be seen in Bareilly, Moradabad, Amroha and Pilibhit, where there is a sizeable Muslim population. Siddharth Kalhans says that if a member of the Azam family contests the election, it could also put an end to speculation about differences between the SP and Azam Khan. It would send a message to Muslim voters that Azam Khan's family is with the party.

stories.title: Electricity to be stored in water like a battery:UP and MP to jointly store 500 MW; both states to get supply for 6 months each
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh have jointly procured 500 MW of pumped storage capacity, in the country's first such unique initiative in the field of power management. Considering their different seasonal electricity requirements, the two states will store electricity through water. At present, electricity is stored only through batteries. Under the arrangement, Madhya Pradesh will use this capacity from November to April, while Uttar Pradesh will use it from May to October. This will allow a single energy storage project to be used throughout the year. It will also spare both states the additional investment required to develop separate energy storage systems. E-reverse auction process completed MP Power Management Company Limited (MPPMCL) has completed the e-reverse auction process for the agreement. This is an online bidding process for purchasing electricity, in which the company offering the lowest rate is selected. The lowest rate received in the online auction, which lasted around four hours, was ₹1.3487 crore per megawatt per year. This includes the cost of losses incurred while storing and retrieving the electricity. The company said this rate is lower than that of other such projects. Agreement to run for 40 years, benefit to come from higher electricity demand The agreement between the two states for purchasing electricity will be for 40 years. Under it, a facility to store 500 megawatts of electricity will be provided. Electricity can be stored for up to six hours, and supplied continuously for up to four hours when required. When electricity demand is low, surplus power will be used to pump water up to an elevated reservoir. When demand rises, the water will be released downhill to generate electricity. This arrangement will help address the shortage of electricity in the evening, when solar power generation declines while consumption rises. The stored electricity will be useful at such times. It will reduce the need for both states to buy electricity from elsewhere at high prices. Solar and wind power can also be utilised more effectively. Could become a model for other states as well Under this agreement, both states have taken their electricity demand periods into account. Madhya Pradesh will benefit from this facility for six months, followed by Uttar Pradesh for the next six months. This will allow the same project to be used throughout the year. This arrangement could also set an example for other states. It will help reduce the cost of electricity and ensure adequate power is available when needed. What is pumped storage? Pumped storage can be understood as a large battery for electricity. It uses water to store electricity. In simple terms, when there is surplus electricity, water is pumped uphill and stored. When electricity is needed, the water is released downhill to generate power. However, it generates slightly less electricity than the amount consumed to pump the water upwards. Typically, 70 to 85 per cent of the electricity can be recovered.

stories.title: UP women affected by violence to get ₹15 lakh compensation:Government to provide legal aid too, Yogi Cabinet changes 11-year-old policy
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government will provide financial help of up to ₹15 lakh to women and girls who are victims of serious crimes and violence. The Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, approved the 'Rani Lakshmibai Women and Child Honour Fund Rules, 2026' on Wednesday (November 18). Under the new rules, victims will receive financial help ranging from ₹1 lakh to ₹15 lakh, depending on the seriousness of the crime. Earlier, the maximum compensation was ₹10 lakh. New system to replace 2015 scheme Until now, financial assistance was provided to women and girls who were victims under the 'Rani Lakshmibai Women's Honour Fund Rules, 2015', which came into force on 6 February 2015. The government has decided to replace these rules, which are nearly 11 years old, with the new Rules, 2026. The new system has been prepared in line with the compensation scheme of the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) and the new criminal laws. What has changed in the old and new rules Compensation amount increased- The 2015 rules provided for compensation ranging from ₹1 lakh to ₹10 lakh, depending on the severity of the crime. Under the new rules, the maximum amount has been increased to ₹15 lakh. Scope of the scheme expanded- Under the old scheme, assistance was mainly provided to women victims of offences covered under nine selected sections of the IPC. The new rules include children as well, and the scheme has been renamed the 'Rani Lakshmibai Women and Children's Honour Fund'. It has been aligned with NALSA's compensation scheme. Emphasis on immediate assistance- The new guidelines emphasise providing victims with timely financial and medical assistance. However, the process of providing immediate interim relief on the basis of a preliminary medical report and confirmation of the incident should be verified only after examining the original guidelines. Victims of which crimes will benefit? Under the new guidelines, financial assistance will be provided to women and minor girls affected by serious violence and sexual offences. The cases covered mainly include: The amount of assistance will be determined according to the severity of the crime Not every victim will receive the same amount. Financial assistance will be determined based on the seriousness of the crime, the need for treatment, and the physical and mental harm suffered by the victim. In generally serious cases, assistance will start at ₹1 lakh, while in severe cases, the amount may go up to ₹15 lakh. In addition, victims will be provided free treatment, reconstructive surgery if required, and legal assistance. The approved amount will be transferred directly to the bank account of the victim or her legal guardian.

stories.title: BJP leader’s Fortuner stolen by interior designer in Prayagraj:Made duplicate key, walked with a limp to avoid suspicion
stories.summary: An interior designer stole a BJP leader's Fortuner in Prayagraj with the help of a friend. He first got a duplicate key made and then stole the car when he got a chance. To avoid being caught, he pretended to walk with a limp while stealing the vehicle. The incident took place around midnight on October 23-24 and was captured on CCTV cameras. During the investigation, police found that the accused had taken the car from Prayagraj to Maharashtra via Rewa. They changed the original number plate and put a fake one on the vehicle. They were preparing to sell it. The Civil Lines police and Surveillance Cell arrested both accused from Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, on Tuesday and recovered the Fortuner. On Wednesday, they brought the two accused to Prayagraj. The case is being investigated by the Civil Lines police. BJP leader's car was parked outside the hotel BJP leader and district vice-president of the OBC Morcha, Piyush Jaiswal, had his Fortuner stolen around midnight on 23-24 October. His car was parked outside the Royal Stay Inn hotel on Myor Road. When the car could not be traced despite an extensive search, he filed a case at the Civil Lines police station. Driver arrived to have the car washed, and the conspiracy was hatched According to the police, the mastermind behind the theft was Mohammad Ishtiyaq, alias Mohammad Shah. He is originally from Rasoolabad in Shivkuti, Prayagraj. He used to work in interior designing in Maharashtra. It emerged during questioning that on 9 October, BJP leader Piyush Jaiswal's driver, Mohammad Azam, had gone to Civil Lines to get the car washed. Ishtiaq arrived there during this time. The two spoke, and a plan to steal the car was made. After this, Ishtiaq, Azam and another associate together had a duplicate key made for the car. 23 October was fixed as the date for the theft. As planned, Ishtiaq first went to Maharashtra. Azam also stopped driving the car so that no one would suspect anything. On the appointed date, Ishtiaq returned to Prayagraj. The two then stole the Fortuner at night using the duplicate key. Changed His Gait to Mislead Police A notable aspect of this theft was that the incident was captured on CCTV. The footage showed the man who stole the car walking with a limp. Based on the footage, the police began investigating and tried to identify the thief. During questioning, Ishtiyaq said he had deliberately pretended to limp. His aim was to mislead the police so that the investigation would be diverted based on the identity and appearance of the man seen in the footage. Car taken from Prayagraj to Maharashtra via Rewa After stealing the car, the accused did not keep it in Prayagraj. They drove it to Rewa via Naini, Chheoki, Meja and Koraon. From there, they went to Maharashtra. On the way, they removed the car's original number plate and replaced it with a fake one. The two were then planning to sell the car in Maharashtra. The Civil Lines police and Surveillance Cell teams traced both accused during the investigation. Acting on an informer's tip-off, the police arrested Mohammad Ishtiaq and Mohammad Azam from the MIDC Ground in the Taloja police station area of the Navi Mumbai Commissionerate. The stolen Fortuner was also recovered from their possession. See the entire incident in 4 pictures He had mortgaged his Fortuner against a loan During police questioning, Ishtiyaq also explained why he committed the theft. He said he had worked in interior designing in Maharashtra. In 2020, when work came to a halt during the coronavirus pandemic, he moved to Rasoolabad in Prayagraj. He then began working while living there. During this period, he lost a substantial amount of money in share trading. Due to financial hardship and debt, he also had to mortgage his Fortuner car for ₹5 lakh. Meanwhile, he met Azam. Azam was the driver of BJP leader Piyush Jaiswal. Ishtiyaq knew that Azam had a direct connection with the car. Taking advantage of this, he planned to steal the BJP leader's Fortuner. Civil Lines police station in-charge Ramashray Yadav said the police identified the arrested accused as Mohammed Ishtiaq alias Mohammed Shah (45), a resident of Rasoolabad, Shivkuti, and Mohammed Azam (29), a resident of Bailey village under Cantt police station. The search for another accused involved in the crime is under way. Both have been sent to jail.

stories.title: Minister Nishad stages highway blockade in Maharajganj:Demands SC reservation for his community, calls Pankaj Chaudhary
stories.summary: Nishad Party national president and Cabinet Minister Sanjay Nishad took to the streets with his supporters in Maharajganj at around 4.30 p.m. on Wednesday evening, demanding Scheduled Caste (SC) reservation for the fishing community. After the conclusion of a convention and march organised at Abhinav Vidya Mandir Inter College in Uditpur, in the Farenda tehsil area, he began a sit-in on the Gorakhpur-Sonauli National Highway. This disrupted traffic on both lanes of the highway for around two hours. Long queues of vehicles formed on both sides of the road. Constitutional rights issue raised at convention A Constitutional Security Rights Mega-Conference and March was organised at Abhinav Vidya Mandir Inter College. The event raised demands for the constitutional rights of the fishing community, social justice, political representation and reservation for Scheduled Castes. At the event, Sanjay Nishad said that the fishing community had been struggling for a long time for its constitutional rights and reservation. He called on the community to take forward the fight for its rights with greater strength. Sit-in began with protesters occupying both lanes After the mega-conference ended, Sanjay Nishad reached the Gorakhpur-Sonauli National Highway with his supporters and party workers. He began a sit-in protest on both lanes of the road. The sudden blockade of the highway led to queues of vehicles forming on both sides. Commuters faced difficulties. Sanjay Nishad said he would continue sitting in protest with the workers until the government accepted their demands. Protest ended after talks with Pankaj Chaudhary After the protest continued for around two hours, Sanjay Nishad spoke to BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary. He then decided to end the sit-in with the party workers. Traffic on the highway was restored after the sit-in ended. Following the protest over the demand for reservation, the issue of the constitutional rights of the fishing community has once again come into focus.

stories.title: ₹6 lakh paid to shooters to kill husband:Man shot in right hand; 5 arrested in Lucknow, including cop lover
stories.summary: A woman in Lucknow allegedly paid ₹6 lakh to have her husband killed. The shooters opened fire on him, but he survived the attack. Police have arrested five people, including the woman's lover, in connection with the case. According to the police, the wife, Aashi Mishra, and her lover, Nitin Rana, a Uttar Pradesh Police constable, were involved in the plan to kill her husband, Anurag Shukla. They allegedly paid ₹6 lakh for the job. Anurag was shot near Purnia Chauraha on 28 October. The bullet hit the upper part of his right arm, but he survived. Nitin Rana was among those who took the contract. Mayank Vashishtha, Shubham Sharma and Shivam Rajput were also allegedly involved. Police arrested the four men in Meerut and Aashi Mishra in Lucknow. Another accused, Mayank Rajput, is still absconding. They met at a library; affair had been ongoing since 2022 DCP North Amit Kumar Anand said Nitin Rana is a constable from the 2019 batch of the Uttar Pradesh Police and is currently posted at the Reserve Police Lines in Lucknow. He met Aashi Mishra in 2022 while preparing for competitive examinations at Maa Public Library in Kapurthala. She is a resident of Faizullaganj. The two subsequently became involved in a relationship. Aashi married Anurag Shukla, a resident of Daudnagar's Vishnu Vihar Colony, in 2025. He is employed as a sales manager at Kotak Mahindra Bank. Nitin and Ashi remained in contact even after the marriage. Nitin had also given Ashi a SIM card registered in his name, which they used to talk to each other. She plotted her husband's murder after he spoke to other women During questioning, it emerged that after the marriage, Ashi had checked her husband's mobile phone. She discovered that Anurag spoke to other women. She complained to Nitin about this. The two then planned to eliminate Anurag three months ago. Nitin contacted his acquaintance Shubham Sharma and others. A contract killing was arranged for ₹6 lakh. Some of the money was also paid in advance. Two days of reconnaissance, then gunfire in Purnia According to the DCP, the accused came to Lucknow on 26 October to carry out the conspiracy and conducted reconnaissance of Anurag's activities and the routes he used to travel. Then, at around 10:30 pm on 28 October, Mayank Vashishth and Manoj Rajput opened fire at Anurag near the gate of the Central Building at Purnia Crossing. The bullet hit his right hand. However, Anurag survived. All four accused arrested in Meerut Following the incident, the police identified the accused with the help of CCTV footage, mobile surveillance and other technical evidence. The SWAT-surveillance team of the DCP North and Aliganj police conducted a joint operation and raided a location near Maliyana railway crossing in Meerut's Transport Nagar area. Mayank Vashisht, Shubham Sharma, Shivam Rajput and constable Nitin Rana were arrested there. Ashi Mishra was apprehended in Lucknow. All the arrested accused are residents of Baghpat. According to the police, the accused threw the country-made pistol used in the incident somewhere along the way. The police are trying to recover it. Manoj Rajput, who was involved in the firing, is still absconding. Raids are being conducted to arrest him.

stories.title: UP panchayat elections delayed by 6 months:Government extends pradhans' term, approves 30 Cabinet proposals
stories.summary: Panchayat elections in Uttar Pradesh have been postponed by another six months. The state Cabinet has approved an ordinance related to the panchayats. Under the new arrangement, existing village heads will be appointed as administrators after their terms end. The tenure of the OBC Commission has also been extended. This arrangement will remain in place until the panchayat election process is completed. A total of 31 proposals were presented at the Cabinet meeting. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Suresh Khanna said that 30 proposals were approved, while one was dropped. Why have the panchayat elections been postponed? Several reasons are believed to be behind the delay. These include preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections, the OBC reservation process, the revision of voter lists and possible dissatisfaction among party workers. The Assembly elections are due in 2027. Holding panchayat elections before them could divert the government's and the party's attention from Assembly poll preparations. Local party workers could be unhappy with the distribution of tickets in the panchayat elections. This could affect the party's preparations for the Assembly elections. The panchayat election results could give an idea of the political mood in the state and influence parties' strategies for the Assembly polls. Completing the OBC reservation process is another important reason for the delay. The tenure of the OBC Commission has been extended for this purpose. Revising voter lists and completing other election preparations could also take more time. Other key Cabinet decisions Deep Tech U Hub to be set up in Noida, ₹281.03 crore approved The Cabinet has approved ₹281.03 crore for setting up a Deep Tech U Hub at IIT Kanpur's Noida campus. A budget of ₹100 crore will be provided for the project in the current financial year. The Central Government will not provide any funds for it. The construction work is expected to be completed within 24 months. Suresh Khanna said the project aims to promote new ideas, support start-ups and create more job opportunities in the state. Land in Agra to be given to Sports Department for stadium The Cabinet has approved the transfer of land in Uganpura gram panchayat in the Bah area of Agra to the Sports Department for building a stadium. The land is currently registered in the name of the Youth Department. The stadium will provide local and upcoming players with a place to showcase their talent. Cooperative college to be built in Rahman Kheda The Cabinet has approved the allocation of 4.51 hectares of land in Rahman Kheda, Lucknow, to an institution under the Cooperation Department. A cooperative college will be built on the land to promote education, research and training in this field. The institution will also offer courses related to artificial intelligence (AI). A hostel and a hall with a capacity of 1,000 people will also be built there. The aim is to prepare skilled professionals in the field of cooperation. Changes to rules related to waqf properties The Cabinet has approved changes to the rules related to waqf properties. This will help put the arrangements linked to the Ummeed portal in place. Land arrangements for Kashi Vishwanath Corridor The Cabinet has also approved a proposal related to land arrangements for the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor. Other key decisions The Cabinet has approved a proposal to provide compensation to farmers affected by the Jewar Airport project. Proposals to promote the semiconductor and deep-tech sectors in the state have also been approved. These aim to attract investment and create jobs in new technology fields. A proposal related to the operation of 102 and 108 ambulance services has been approved. A logistics cluster will be developed near the Purvanchal Expressway. It will have facilities for storing and transporting goods. The Cabinet has approved a residential project on the site of the old police lines in Agra. A yoga centre will be built in Baghpat. Changes to the rules of the Women and Child Honour Fund have been approved. The Cabinet has approved a proposal to take technical help from IIT-ISM Dhanbad for mining-related work.
