stories.title: Fire breaks out in Lucknow slums:Plastic items fuel blaze, 10 fire engines deployed to control it
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in the slums of Aishbagh, under the Bazar Khala police station area in Lucknow, at around 4 pm on Wednesday. Thick black smoke from the fire could be seen from nearly 4 km away. After seeing smoke rising from the area, people alerted the fire brigade. The fire spread quickly, causing panic among residents. Four fire engines reached the spot and started efforts to control the flames. The fire is reportedly flaring up again and again because a large amount of plastic items is stored in the slums. Check out pictures below : Area thrown into chaos by raging flames According to eyewitnesses, smoke began rising from the shanties at around 4 p.m. People initially tried to put out the fire, but the flames began spreading rapidly. The fire brigade was then alerted. Four fire engines at the scene As soon as the information was received, four fire engines reached the spot. Firefighters are working to bring the blaze under control. The presence of plastic materials is making it difficult to extinguish the fire, and the flames are repeatedly intensifying.

According to official party information, the committee will hear and investigate complaints of indiscipline against the party's elected representatives, office-bearers and workers. Key names included in the committee The new disciplinary committee formed by the BJP includes five senior organisational leaders as members: How will this committee function? Under the party's rules, if a complaint of indiscipline or anti-party activities is received against any elected representative, office-bearer or worker, the committee will hear the case. After hearing the parties concerned, the committee will prepare its inquiry report, on the basis of which a final decision will be taken on further action against the leader or worker found guilty.

He also addressed a public meeting in Chauri Chaura. Akhilesh Yadav attended a tribute meeting in Devkahi held on the 10th death anniversary of former BJP leader Vinay Kumar Singh Binnu. stories.title: 600 couples to get married under government scheme in Varanasi:Brides to receive ₹64,000 each; events to be held across all blocks
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government will organise mass marriage ceremonies for 600 couples across all eight development blocks of Varanasi under the Chief Minister's Mass Marriage Scheme. The ceremonies will be held from November 21 to the first week of December. Under the scheme, ₹64,000 will be transferred directly to the bank account of each bride. The newly married couples will also receive household items to help them start their new lives. District Social Welfare Officer Girish Chandra Dubey said preparations had been completed for the ceremonies. The programme will be held in Sevapuri, Harhua, Arajiline, Pindra, Baragaon, Cholapur, Kashi Vidyapeeth and Chiraigaon blocks. Block-wise marriage schedule Sevapuri: November 21 – 80 couples Harhua: November 25 – 80 couples Arajiline: November 26 – 80 couples Pindra: November 26 – 80 couples Baragaon: November 26 – 80 couples Cholapur: November 29 – 80 couples Kashi Vidyapeeth: December 3 – 30 couples Chiraigaon: First week of December – 90 couples What will brides receive? Apart from the ₹64,000 grant, each couple will receive household items, including five sarees, a steel dinner set, a pressure cooker, a trolley bag, an iron, a ceiling fan, a blanket and a mattress. The items will help the couples set up their homes. The scheme aims to support families who cannot afford the expenses of their daughters' marriages.

stories.title: 23 rare turtles found in 13 bags at Varanasi station:2 women carrying children arrested for smuggling them from Sultanpur to West Bengal
stories.summary: A joint team of the Government Railway Police (GRP), Railway Protection Force (RPF) and Central Intelligence Bureau (CIB) recovered 23 rare turtles from Banaras railway station. The turtles were packed in 13 bags and bundles. Two women travelling with their children were detained in connection with the case. The incident took place on Tuesday night when the women were found sitting in the station's closed parking area near the second entrance. They had two children with them, one around 1.5 years old and the other around three years old. Several bags and bundles were kept beside them. According to RPF post in-charge Rajesh, police teams were patrolling the station due to the festive season when they noticed the women. When asked about their names and addresses, they did not give any information. The team became suspicious and took them to the GRP outpost. During a search of their bags, the team found 23 rare turtles. According to the Forest Department, the turtles were being taken from Sultanpur to West Bengal through Varanasi. Their estimated market value is more than ₹3 lakh. They had arrived in Banaras by bus from Sultanpur The RPF in-charge said that when the women's bags were searched, 23 rare tortoises of different sizes were found. All of them had been packed into 13 bags and bundles. The women, who were arrested, identified themselves as Manisha, a resident of Pakri under Hanumanganj police station in Sultanpur district, and Sapna, a resident of Pakri under Hanumanganj police station in Sultanpur district. Both women also have children, whom they were going to take along while travelling. Sold in West Bengal for more than ₹3 lakh Regional Forest Officer Rajkumar Gautam, who reached the spot after receiving information, said 23 turtles had been seized at Varanasi's Banaras Junction. All these turtles were being prepared for transportation from Sultanpur to West Bengal via Varanasi. He said, "We reached here after receiving information from police officers." These are all rare turtles. They are taken to West Bengal and sold at high prices. Their international value is more than ₹3 lakh.

stories.title: Akhilesh's Gorakhpur roadshow grabs attention:2-foot dancers, selfie crowds and laptop-waving supporters steal the show
stories.summary: From a two-foot-tall SP worker surrounded by people wanting selfies to supporters dancing to drum beats and waving laptops while riding horses, Akhilesh Yadav's Gorakhpur roadshow on Wednesday saw people come up with different ways to grab attention. A large crowd gathered to welcome the Samajwadi Party chief. Riding on the PDA Rath, Akhilesh received a warm welcome at several places, while SP flags, hoardings and cutouts covered the streets. 2-foot-tall SP worker becomes selfie attraction Chand Babu, a two-foot-tall Samajwadi Party worker from Bhadohi, reached Gorakhpur airport to welcome Akhilesh. As soon as people spotted him, they gathered around to shake hands and click selfies. The crowd grew so large that he eventually had to leave the spot. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Chand Babu said he had travelled around 266 km from Bhadohi to welcome the party chief. Calling himself the party's "smallest soldier", he said he followed every order given by Akhilesh. He also said his family had followed socialist ideas for generations. "My grandfather and great-grandfather were socialists, and we will remain so throughout our lives. This time, Akhilesh Yadav will become the Chief Minister. The entire public is with him," he said. Supporters wave laptops and welcome Akhilesh with a huge garland Supporters came up with other ways to show their excitement. One person had Akhilesh's name written on his body, while another arrived on a horse and waved a laptop in the air. Shubham also wore a T-shirt with "2027 ke Sattadhish" written on it. At Kudaghat crossing, two cranes lifted a huge garland to welcome Akhilesh. The SP chief had his PDA Rath stopped as supporters raised slogans. Seeing their enthusiasm, he climbed onto the roof of the bus and waved at the crowd. Red-cap supporter dances to drum beats Another young supporter grabbed attention by dancing on the road. Wearing a red cap with "Yuvjan Sabha" written on it, he started dancing as soon as the drums began playing. He raised his hands and moved to the beats with full energy. People stopped to watch and cheer him, while other SP supporters also joined in. Two-foot-tall Shubham surprises Akhilesh with his dance Shubham, another two-foot-tall dancer, also became a talking point during the roadshow. Wearing a T-shirt with Akhilesh Yadav's picture on it, he danced enthusiastically on the road. His energetic moves made people stop and clap. Even Akhilesh was surprised by his performance. Akhilesh holds first Gorakhpur roadshow since 2024 polls This was Akhilesh's first visit to Gorakhpur for a political programme since the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. His roadshow passed through Gorakhpur City, Gorakhpur Rural and Chauri Chaura assembly constituencies. Later, addressing a public meeting in Chauri Chaura, Akhilesh paid tribute to Babu Bandhu Singh and the martyrs of the Chauri Chaura incident. He also thanked people for the support they showed during the roadshow.

stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath launched a joint training programme of the National Security Guard (NSG) and Uttar Pradesh Police in Lucknow on Wednesday. During the programme, NSG commandos conducted a mock drill in front of the Chief Minister. They showed how they would respond to a terrorist attack inside a building. The commandos arrived by helicopter and used ropes to reach the building's roof. They then entered through the windows and took down the terrorists one by one. They also rescued the hostages safely. An NSG dog also took part in the operation and helped the commandos. After the drill, the dog, Johnny, presented a bouquet to CM Yogi and saluted him. The aim of the joint training programme is to improve coordination between the NSG and Uttar Pradesh Police. Police personnel will be trained to handle situations such as terrorist attacks. stories.title: Nephew kills gym trainer in Agra:Repeatedly attacks his face with a stone, leaving his jaw and eyes disfigured
stories.summary: A gym trainer was killed by his brother and nephew in Agra on Tuesday. On Wednesday, a video linked to the murder emerged. It shows the nephew repeatedly striking the gym trainer on the head with a stone. The accused kept hitting the gym trainer until his eyes and jaw were dislodged. His teeth broke and were scattered on the road. After the murder, the accused tried to throw the gym trainer, covered in blood, into a drain. When people raised an alarm, the accused fled. New Agra police station has registered a case against the accused. First, read the full case Dispute over 120 square yards of land Shahid, alias Guddu Pehalwan, a 49-year-old resident of Suresh Nagar, was a gym trainer. He was currently running a grocery shop near his home. He was one of four brothers. Shahid's son Ajaan said there was 120 square yards of land behind their house. His father had an ongoing dispute over the land with his elder brother, Afsar alias Lala, and younger brother, Bunty Qureshi. "We had already won the case in court. Despite this, both brothers continued to harass us," he said. On Monday morning, uncle Afsar and uncle Bunty reached the land with other people. The accused arrived carrying a door and a door frame. They began construction on the land. My father, Shahid, objected. When the accused refused to stop, my father went to New Agra police station. The police then reached the spot and stopped the construction. At 8:30 a.m. on Tuesday, another dispute broke out over the land. The women from both sides confronted each other. As the dispute escalated, Shahid left to lodge a complaint at the police station. His friend Dilshad was with him on the scooter. Surrounded 150 metres from home, killed in a stone attack Shahid had reached a point about 150 metres from his home when the accused surrounded both of them on the way. The accused pulled Shahid off his scooter and knocked him to the ground. They kicked and punched him and tried to drag him into a drain. Shahid then confronted the accused. Meanwhile, Mehtab and Aftab, the two sons of Afsar alias Lala, attacked Shahid with a stone. Shahid fell on the road as soon as the stone hit him. Mehtab then picked up a large stone from the road and began repeatedly striking Shahid's face. The accused struck him four times with the stone in 17 seconds. Shahid's jaw was fractured, his eyes protruded and his broken teeth were scattered across the road. When people raised an alarm, the accused fled the scene. Shahid's friend ran home and informed his family. His family took Shahid, who was covered in blood, to the police station. From there, they first took him to the district hospital and then to a private hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Now read what the video shows In the 17-second video, the accused, Guddu Pehalwan, is seen attacking the victim with a stone four times. People are seen standing and shouting, trying to stop him. But he did not stop. The people continued standing and recording the video, but no one had the courage to stop the accused. After the murder, the accused fled the scene. Shahid is survived by three sons, Azaan, Faiz and Zaid, and a daughter. His father, Raheesh, died in 2016. Meanwhile, Nazneen lost consciousness after her husband was murdered. ACP Hariparvat Bajrang Prasad said an FIR had been registered on the complaint of Shahid's friend, Dilshad. A team has been deployed to arrest the accused.

stories.title: Akhilesh says government is scared, shuts down internet:Holds 20-km roadshow in Gorakhpur, says city feels like Europe
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav arrived in Gorakhpur on Wednesday for his first political programme in the city since the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. He held a roadshow on the PDA Rath, passing through Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's stronghold and receiving a warm welcome from supporters at several places. The roadshow passed through Gorakhpur City, Gorakhpur Rural and Chauri Chaura Assembly constituencies. The BJP and its allies held power in all three seats. Akhilesh also addressed a public meeting in Chauri Chaura. A large number of supporters gathered to see him. Amrita Yadav, a student who attended the roadshow, said she was a big fan of Akhilesh and liked everything he said. She added that she was not old enough to vote yet, but would support her parents when they cast their votes. She also raised slogans in support of the SP chief. Another supporter, Muskan Yadav, said she had come to see Akhilesh and hoped the Samajwadi Party would form the government in 2027. She said a change in government would bring many changes and that she expected a new direction under Akhilesh's leadership. Taking a dig at the current government, she said it had done nothing during its term. Roadshow held on PDA chariot The Samajwadi PDA chariot had arrived in Gorakhpur on Tuesday night. Akhilesh boarded it at Gorakhpur airport at 12 noon on Wednesday and left for Devkahi. On the way, he passed through AIIMS, Gurung Tiraha in Kudaghat, the Engineering University and Sooba Bazaar. Supporters welcomed him at several places. The chariot began its journey in the Gorakhpur City Assembly constituency before entering Gorakhpur Rural and Chauri Chaura. Akhilesh greeted people from inside the chariot and also stepped out to acknowledge their welcome. Akhilesh pays tribute to martyrs In Devkahi, Akhilesh attended a programme marking the 10th death anniversary of former BJP leader Vinay Kumar Singh Binnu. He also unveiled a statue of martyr Bandhu Singh and paid tribute to him and the martyrs of the Chauri Chaura incident. Addressing the gathering, Akhilesh thanked people for the support they had shown during the roadshow. At the end of his speech, he took a dig at the government over the internet shutdown, saying it was scared and had therefore stopped internet services. Visit aimed at reaching upper-caste voters Akhilesh's visit also focused on upper-caste voters, particularly Kshatriya and Brahmin communities. He attended the programme held on the death anniversary of former BJP leader Binnu Singh. Binnu Singh's brother, Tappu Singh, had received around 30,000 votes as an independent candidate in the 2022 Assembly elections. The Samajwadi Party was preparing to bring him into the party and hoped to gain support among Kshatriya voters in Chauri Chaura and nearby constituencies. Akhilesh also visited Tiwari Hata, the residence of Samajwadi Party national secretary Vinay Shankar Tiwari, son of former minister Harishankar Tiwari, in Dharamshala Bazaar. He stayed there for around 30 minutes. The visit was seen as an attempt to reach out to Brahmin voters. Visit also seen as a challenge to Nishad Party Akhilesh's programme in Chauri Chaura was also seen as a political challenge to the Nishad Party. Its national president Dr Sanjay Nishad's younger son, Er. Sarwan Nishad, represented the constituency and had won the seat on a BJP ticket. The Samajwadi Party aimed to strengthen its position in the constituency by bringing Tappu Singh into its fold. Through the programme, it also sought to expand its support in nearby Assembly constituencies.

stories.title: 'Akhilesh can neither attend nor organise a Katha':Dhirendra Shastri says he would hold one if he ever develops faith
stories.summary: Pandit Dhirendra Shastri took a swipe at Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav in Pratapgarh. He said, "He is a very good person; we are not his opponents. We would only say that he should also come and listen to the discourse. In any case, such a time will not come when he can listen to or organise our discourse. But if faith ever awakens within him, we will conduct a discourse for him without hesitation." In Kunda, MLA Raghuraj Pratap Singh (Raja Bhaiya) is organising a Ram Katha by Bageshwar Dham seer Dhirendra Shastri. After completing the discourse on the first day, Tuesday, Dhirendra Shastri appeared before the media and answered their questions. On his comment about Krishna, he said, "My statement was given a political colour. Confusion was spread. Krishna is in our very name." Today, Wednesday, is the second day of the Ram Katha. Earlier in the morning, Dhirendra Shastri went to bathe in the Ganga. He then offered prayers at Haudeshwar Nath Temple. Raja Bhaiya is the patron of this temple. Mahant Raju Das of Hanumangarhi was present with him. Read Pt Dhirendra Shastri's question-and-answer session with the media Question: Akhilesh Yadav has been attacking you more aggressively. Why is that? Answer: There must be something about us that is causing this. As for the question of whether my religious discourse is cheap or expensive, understand that we are not selling a commodity; religion is not a business. If it were a business, it would be cheap. Religion is a matter of faith. There are many wealthy people who want to organise my religious discourse. If they approach us as though they are buying the discourse, we will not go; if they do it out of faith, we will go along just the same. Question: Several Opposition leaders besides the Samajwadi Party chief are also upset with you. What do you have to say? Answer: We do not offer lengthy explanations because we have set out to do our work, so it is natural that all kinds of things will be said. Under the Constitution, religious discourses cannot be stopped. If they are stopped, prayers at mosques will also be stopped. Prayers in churches will also be stopped. If that happens, the system will be disrupted. Hindus are awakening, followers of Sanatan Dharma are awakening and responding assertively. Question: You are holding religious discourses in Uttar Pradesh and benefiting politicians? Answer: Those who listen to, deliver and organise a discourse benefit from it. Not only them, but sound-system providers, television channels and news organisations also benefit from it. As for the fact that this is an election year, that is not the case; we hold discourses throughout the five-year term. We conduct these discourses not for elections, but for Sanatan Dharma. Question: You said that there is a need for another Partition. Why? Answer: There has not yet been a complete Partition. Some people had been left behind because they were afraid in India. It is such a safe country, yet if they are still afraid, they should leave. Some Hindus want to come from Pakistan; they should be allowed to come. The Hindus who have already come to India should be granted citizenship here. This is my view: if someone wants a complete Partition, it should happen. Question: Did you divide Ram and Krishna in your discourse? Answer: It is impossible to understand a 30-second excerpt from a three-hour discourse after it has been edited. People cut out that portion and circulated it in that form. The confusion will disappear once you listen to the entire discourse. It was given a political colour. It had nothing to do with denigrating God in any way. After all, how could someone narrating the discourse denigrate Krishna-especially someone who has Krishna in his own name? What happened during the discourse on the first day? Read on In fact, on 5 November, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav had demanded the cancellation of Dhirendra Shastri's discourses scheduled to be held in Pratapgarh, Gonda, Jhansi, Lucknow and Agra.

stories.title: Chandrashekhar's ex-girlfriend from Indore to contest against him:Accused him of sexual exploitation; performed a ritual at Baglamukhi Temple
stories.summary: Dr Rohini Ghavari, the former girlfriend of Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad who accused him of sexual exploitation, arrived in Nalkheda in Agar-Malwa on Tuesday night. She visited the Maa Baglamukhi Temple and performed a havan ritual. Rohini said she had come to seek the goddess's blessings for victory in her court case and justice. She also said she would contest the election from the Hastinapur Assembly seat against Chandrashekhar Azad. However, she has not yet clarified whether she will contest on a political party's ticket or as an independent candidate. Also met Digvijaya Singh and Kailash Vijayvargiya Rohini returned to India from Switzerland around eight months ago. Since then, she has met former Chief Ministers Digvijaya Singh and Kamal Nath, as well as state minister Kailash Vijayvargiya, in Delhi and Bhopal. These meetings sparked speculation about her possible entry into politics. Who is Rohini Ghavari, and what is the dispute with Chandrashekhar? Dr Rohini Ghavari is from Indore. Under the Madhya Pradesh government's fellowship scheme, she got an opportunity to study in Switzerland. She completed her PhD there. During this period, she met Bhim Army founder Chandrashekhar Azad. Rohini alleges that Chandrashekhar concealed the fact that he was married, promised to marry her and sexually exploited her. According to her, Chandrashekhar began distancing himself from her after he was elected MP from Nagina. Rohini had also lodged a complaint with the Women's Commission in this matter. Meanwhile, Chandrashekhar and his supporters had an FIR registered against Rohini. Rohini has also been consistently voicing her views against Chandrashekhar on social media. Indications of entering politics While studying in Switzerland, Rohini also founded an NGO called 'Janpower'. After returning to India, her meetings with political leaders and now her announcement that she will contest the election have intensified speculation about her political future.

stories.title: Azam walks out of jail, son says ‘Tiger is back':Spends a year behind bars; 600 supporters gather outside Dasna jail
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan walked out of jail exactly a year after being sent behind bars. As soon as he saw Azam, his son Adeeb said, “The tiger is back. Today is like Eid for us.” As soon as Azam came out of jail, supporters and media personnel surrounded him. Azam said, “I have always said the same thing. A Muslim built a temple of education, and this is his punishment.” He then left for his home in Rampur in a Scorpio SUV. More than 600 supporters were present outside the jail. They raised slogans of “Long live Azam Khan”. Azam was sent to Rampur jail on November 17, 2025, in a case related to two PAN cards. He thus spent an entire year behind bars. Earlier, at around 4.30 pm on Wednesday, the release order for Azam reached Dasna jail in Ghaziabad. He was released after the paperwork was completed. It may be recalled that Azam had also walked out of Rampur jail on October 31, but the Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested him immediately. He had been lodged in Dasna jail since then. Earlier on Wednesday morning, the ED approached the Supreme Court challenging Azam's interim bail. The agency sought an urgent hearing in the case. The judge reprimanded the ED, saying, “What is the hurry? Let Azam remain out on bail. It is not the end of the world.” Azam's case to be heard again in Supreme Court on Thursday The Enforcement Directorate (ED) approached the Supreme Court on Wednesday morning challenging Azam's interim bail. It sought an immediate hearing in the case. However, the court has scheduled the hearing for Thursday (November 19). The court may either overturn the Allahabad High Court's order or uphold it. If the High Court's order is overturned, Azam may have to return to jail. Meanwhile, the Vigilance Department has registered an FIR against Azam in Lucknow in connection with the Haj House case. He could also be arrested in this case. However, the department will need approval from the state government before making the arrest. Akhilesh says the government wronged Azam Khan and his family Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav expressed happiness after Azam Khan was granted interim bail. He said Azam Khan had received justice from the court. The government had wronged Azam Khan and his family for several years. Akhilesh said, "We have been saying from the first day that the cases registered against Azam Khan are false and that the government's action is wrong. The government's intentions are not right. Several things have come to light today through the court's observations. We have complete faith that justice will be delivered by the court." Minister Jaiveer Singh says being granted bail and being cleared of the charges are two different things Uttar Pradesh government minister Jaiveer Singh said the government respects the court's order. Under the constitutional system, courts and other institutions independently take decisions within their respective powers. When the court has granted bail, what comment can the government make on it? The order will be followed. The minister said that being granted bail does not mean being cleared of the charges. The two are different matters. The cases will now be heard in court. The final decision will come only after the trial is completed. Could Azam's release cause trouble for the BJP? Read ... Azam Khan has been sentenced to 10 years in the PAN card case, while Abdullah Azam has been sentenced in the PAN card and fake birth certificate cases. Both have also been disqualified as members of the Legislative Assembly. Under Section 8(3) of the Representation of the People Act, a person sentenced to two years or more cannot contest elections for six years after completing the sentence. This disqualification is not removed merely by being granted bail. A stay on the sentence from a higher court is necessary to contest an election. However, Azam's release before the 2027 Assembly election could prove significant for the Samajwadi Party. Understand its political impact in 3 points... 1. He will become the SP's star campaigner Despite being unable to contest elections, Azam Khan can campaign for the SP. His speeches in Muslim-dominated seats in western Uttar Pradesh are expected to boost the morale of party workers. 2. Countering Owaisi's challenge Azam's return may help the Samajwadi Party prevent Muslim votes from splitting. The party will regain its old and outspoken face to take on the challenge posed by Asaduddin Owaisi's AIMIM. 3. Organisation to be strengthened in western UP Azam has had influence in western UP, including the Rampur and Moradabad divisions. His return may help fill the vacuum in the party's minority leadership created by his absence. Akhilesh may assign him responsibility for coordinating the party's seats in western UP. What will be the BJP's next move? After Azam's release, the BJP may target the Samajwadi Party on law and order and corruption issues. According to senior journalist Jaigam Murtaza, Azam's release could reactivate the SP's local organisation in Rampur and the surrounding districts. This could affect the political contest in the 2027 election.

stories.title: Who was Binnu Singh? Akhilesh to visit and pay tribute:He campaigned against Mahant Avaidyanath and contested against Union minister's father
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav is visiting Gorakhpur today, 18 November, on his first political tour of the district in connection with the 2027 Assembly elections. He will pay tribute to late Vinay Kumar Singh 'Binnu' on his 10th death anniversary at Devkahi in the Chauri Chaura Assembly constituency. At the same event, Ajay Kumar Singh, Binnu Singh's brother, will be inducted into the SP. Ten years have passed since Binnu Singh's death, but he is once again in the spotlight because of the SP chief's programme. Binnu Singh had been a combative politician from the outset. Binnu Singh, who began his political career in student politics, once campaigned against Yogi Adityanath's guru, Mahant Avedyanath, in a Lok Sabha election. In the 1990s, he contested an Assembly election against late Om Prakash Paswan. Om Prakash's elder son, Kamlesh Paswan, is currently a minister in the Union government. Entered student politics and secured a victory Binnu Singh was regarded as a dynamic leader from his youth. In the 1980s, he entered the fray in the student union election at Gorakhpur University and succeeded in winning. In the 1989 election, he joined the Janata Dal. At the time, the Janata Dal had given Rampal Singh a Lok Sabha ticket, while the BJP had supported him. Binnu Singh was very close to Rampal Singh. During this election, he openly campaigned against Mahant Avaidyanath, who was contesting on the Hindu Mahasabha banner. However, Mahant Avaidyanath succeeded in winning the election. After this, Binnu Singh joined the BJP. In the 1993 election, the BJP gave him a ticket from Maniram. The seat was considered Mahant Avaidyanath's traditional constituency. Late Om Prakash Paswan had been elected BJP MLA from here in 1991. In 1993, he was again staking his claim. However, Om Prakash Paswan contested this election as an independent. The BJP fielded Binnu Singh against him. However, late Om Prakash Paswan won the election by a huge margin. He received more than 59% of the votes. Janata Dal's Shambhu Sharan, who came second, received 18.89% of the votes, while Binnu Singh received only 13.34%. Binnu Remained Active in the BJP After this election, he remained continuously active in the BJP. He was considered very close to senior BJP leader Kalraj Mishra. Meanwhile, his family also became associated with Gorakhnath Temple. Ajay Kumar Singh Tappu, Binnu Singh's brother, told a media organisation that his family had donated land and provided other assistance for Gorakhnath Temple and Madan Mohan Malaviya University of Technology (MMUT). His family is said to be descended from martyr Bandhu Singh. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also regularly speaks about martyr Bandhu Singh on various platforms. Brother Sought BJP Ticket; Entered Fray as Independent After Being Denied Ajay Kumar Singh Tappu is Binnu Singh's younger brother. He is a contractor by profession. He also runs a hotel in Mohaddipur. He has educational institutions as well. Binnu Singh died in November 2016. After his death, Tappu Singh gradually became active in politics. In 2022, he sought the BJP ticket but was not given one. Tappu Singh then contested the election as an independent. Following this, he was expelled from the party. Contesting as an independent, Tappu Singh received around 30,000 votes. He has decided to contest the election this time as well. When there appeared to be no possibility of getting a BJP ticket, he approached the Samajwadi Party. The SP is expected to field Tappu Singh from Chauri Chaura.

stories.title: 8 special trains to run from Lucknow to- Mumbai:6 new services introduced, trips of 2 trains increased
stories.summary: North Eastern Railway has decided to operate eight special trains in view of the rising rush on trains after Diwali and Chhath. One additional trip each has been added to two trains already in operation, while six new special trains will be run. They will operate between 18 and 22 November. This will provide relief to passengers travelling from Gorakhpur, Chhapra and Mau to Delhi, Mumbai and Udhna. One additional trip each added to two trains One additional trip of the Lokmanya Tilak Terminus-Gorakhpur Special (01041/01042) will operate. Train number 01041 will depart from Lokmanya Tilak Terminus on 19 November. On the return journey, train number 01042 will depart from Gorakhpur on 21 November. Similarly, one additional trip of the Hadapsar-Gorakhpur Special (01457/01458) has also been scheduled. Train number 01457 will depart from Hadapsar on 20 November, while train number 01458 will depart from Gorakhpur on 22 November on the return journey. Special trains also for Chhapra and Delhi In addition, the Chhapra-Anand Vihar Terminal Special (05057/05058) and Gorakhpur-Delhi Special (05051/05052) will operate on 19 and 20 November. According to the railway, trains are experiencing additional crowding as passengers return after the festival. Special trains have therefore been arranged.

Fog blankets UP, speed limits reduced on expressways:Bareilly records lowest temperature; 'Akvan' storm to intensify cold and fog
stories.summary: Snowfall in the hills has intensified the cold in Uttar Pradesh. Dense fog is affecting the state during the morning and night hours. Visibility has dropped so low that objects beyond 10 metres are barely visible on roads. Due to the fog, speed limits have been reduced on expressways. The speed limits on the Agra-Lucknow, Purvanchal, Bundelkhand, Gorakhpur Link and Ganga Expressways have been set between 50 and 80 kmph. Cars will not be allowed to exceed 80 kmph, buses 60 kmph and goods vehicles such as trucks 50 kmph. On Wednesday morning, fog covered 15 cities, including Gorakhpur, Deoria, Jaunpur, Mau and Kushinagar. Roads remained deserted. Over the past 24 hours, night temperatures have dropped to around 10°C, while temperatures in 20 districts fell below 15°C. Bareilly was the coldest city, recording 11.1°C. Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, said the impact of Cyclone 'Akvan', which formed over the Bay of Bengal, is now moving from south to north. As a result, cloud cover, cold conditions and fog are expected to intensify over the next 24 hours. Bay of Bengal storm to change the weather According to the meteorologist, temperatures may remain normal or below normal for the next two to three days. After that, the direction of the winds is likely to change under the influence of Cyclonic Storm 'Akwan', which has formed in the Bay of Bengal. This could lead to a rise of 2 to 3 degrees Celsius in temperatures. For now, the chill will intensify in the morning and at night, while sunshine during the day will keep the weather relatively pleasant. It is a score that indicates air quality and helps us understand whether the air around us is clean or polluted. The AQI measures the levels of pollutants present in the air. stories.title: BJP leadership accepts lapse over UGC issue:Party chalks out election strategy in Mathura; youth and women to be key focus
stories.summary: Discontent over the UGC's new regulations was raised at the BJP's two-day meeting in Mathura. The central leadership said the government had also acknowledged that there had been some lapses in drafting the regulations. These would be rectified. The meeting was told that the UGC matter is currently pending before the Supreme Court. However, the government will organise the entire process. The central leadership assured the meeting that no law or regulation would be implemented that could ruin anyone's future or cause injustice to anyone. In September, protests were held at several places in Uttar Pradesh over the UGC's new regulations. Upper-caste groups, in particular, had targeted the BJP government. The protesters were put in touch with Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak. The agitation ended only after they were assured that their demands would be conveyed to the central government. The BJP fears that upper-caste voters may shift towards the Samajwadi Party in the 2027 Assembly election. For now, the central leadership has made it clear that the government does not intend to discriminate against any section. Any shortcomings in the rules will be addressed so that everyone's interests can be taken into account. Read about the issues on which the BJP has prepared a strategy to corner opposition parties.... On 16 and 17 November, the BJP held a two-day state planning meeting at the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Research Centre in Parakham, Mathura. This was national president Nitin Nabin's fifth visit to Uttar Pradesh. He had earlier visited the western, Awadh, Kashi and Gorakhpur regions. Will remind young voters of the Samajwadi Party government's failures According to the BJP leaders who attended the meeting, young people who are preparing to vote for the first or second time today were very young during the Samajwadi Party government before 2017. They have seen only BJP rule at the Centre since 2014 and in the state since 2017. The party believes it is important to inform these new voters about the law-and-order situation, recruitment controversies, the Jawaharb​​agh incident and issues related to women's safety during the earlier period. Only 25% of young people who received tablets were voters Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath shared an important statistic about the electoral roll at the meeting. He said tablets had been distributed in Lucknow to young people above the age of 18 under the Swami Vivekananda Youth Empowerment Scheme. When they were asked how many of them were voters, only 25% of the young people raised their hands. Chief Minister Yogi directed office-bearers to ensure that 100% of the young population is enrolled in the electoral roll. He said the electoral roll for the panchayat elections should be compared with the Assembly electoral roll so that no eligible voter is left out. Speculation Over Organisation, Leadership and Tickets Put to Rest BJP national president Nitin Nabin made it clear at the meeting that there is no crisis whatsoever regarding the organisation, leadership or government in the state, while emphasising that the organisation is paramount. The public has faith in the work of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. 'Nationalism' and new slogans to counter caste politics Nitin Naveen told party workers, "Opposition parties are trying to divide society along caste lines, but the youth and women must be kept united around the issue of nationalism rather than caste. The SP, BSP, Congress and the third front-none of them is an ally, so an aggressive strategy will have to be adopted towards all of them." Suggestions for slogans were also sought from office-bearers at the meeting to give momentum to the election campaign. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak suggested around a dozen slogans, with 'Uttar Pradesh Will Answer' emerging as the most prominent. MLC Santosh Singh and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Suresh Khanna also presented election slogans. A special team comprising former and current office-bearers will now be formed to prepare a roadmap for taking these issues and campaigns to the ground. The meeting discussed the party's action plan for the next three months. It also covered strengthening the organisation, increasing party activities and improving coordination with the NDA's allies. Tribute Also Paid to Ashok Singhal The meeting began with the garlanding of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay's statue. This was followed by a floral tribute to the portrait of late Ashok Singhal, former international president of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), on his death anniversary. National General Secretary (Organisation) BL Santosh, National General Secretary Vinod Tawde, Smriti Irani and Harish Dwivedi were present at the meeting. In addition, more than 50 senior leaders, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, attended.

stories.title: Foreign birds hunted and served at UP hotels:Poacher tells Bhaskar on camera, 'We supply meat to politicians and officials'; hotels offer on-demand delivery
stories.summary: Foreign migratory birds travelling nearly 6,000 km to India to escape deadly temperatures of -40°C are falling into a death trap in Uttar Pradesh. Protected migratory birds are being hunted in more than 10 districts of the state. Their meat is reportedly sold at hotels for up to ₹3,000 per kg. Customers are told that eating this meat increases physical strength and virility and keeps the body warm during winter. A shocking revelation emerged from a sting operation by Dainik Bhaskar, which found that hunters allegedly enjoy the protection of local politicians, police personnel and forest department officials. In return, they supply them with bird meat. To expose the network of hunters and the alleged nexus between politicians and officials in UP, an investigation was conducted in Sant Kabir Nagar, Siddharthnagar, Maharajganj and Bahraich districts. We received information that large-scale hunting was taking place in UP districts bordering Nepal. With the help of a source, a Bhaskar reporter reached a hunter named Azim alias Battery. We were told that hunters operated in the forests of Badhara Ghat and Chetia in the Bansi area. Posing as a buyer, we reached Badhara Ghat, where the hunter negotiated a deal with us. Reporter: I need foreign bird meat, every week or even every month… Azim: We can arrange it. Just place your order, whatever quantity you need. We will deliver it. Reporter: How much will it cost if we buy a larger quantity? Azim: The rate is the same, ₹1,700. We will also roast or clean and cut the meat properly. If we supply it as it is, we could get caught. Reporter: How much can you provide at a time? Azim: We can give you up to 5 kg at a time. We will prepare it so that nobody finds out. Reporter: Hunting these birds is prohibited and the rules are strict. How do you manage to hunt them in forests with guns? Azim: Forest department officials trouble us a lot, so we keep them on our side too. We have to give them some meat as well. Many people are in contact with us. Reporter: How do you catch foreign birds? Azim: We set traps and catch several at once. Come along and we will show you how they are caught. Reporter: I need more birds. Arrange things by managing the department officials. Azim: Just inform us in advance. We can arrange as many as you want. ‘We supply meat to Raja Sahab; he gets us out of trouble’ After confirming that hunting was taking place openly, the question was how hunters managed to escape the police, local residents and politicians. Azim also had an answer. He said they supplied foreign birds to 'Raja Sahab' of Bansi. Whenever they got into trouble, they would ask him to call senior police officers. Reporter: The forest is an open area. Surely everyone must know what is happening? Azim: We know 'Raja Sahab'. Reporter: So, he also helps you? Azim: Yes. Sometimes, when we get caught, he calls the police station or police outpost. Reporter: Don't the police demand money? How would they let someone go just like that? Azim: No. Once Raja Sahab says that we are his men, that's enough. We also make arrangements for food and drinks. Reporter: How do you know Raja Sahab? Azim: We have known him for a long time and keep visiting him. We work in his orchard and even catch monkeys for him free of cost. Ten days later, the reporter returned to Badhara Ghat village in the Bansi area. We wanted to find out where the hunters kept so many birds after catching them. After a lengthy conversation, the hunter became convinced that we would place a large order and took us to a dilapidated-looking house. Feathers were scattered all around the outside of the house. There were bloodstains on the walls. Besides Azim, four other associates were present inside. At the reporter's request, a minor boy showed us 12 to 15 birds kept in five large separate sacks. They were alive and tied with ropes. Among them were Chaha, Surkhab and Patera birds. Reporter: I need more birds. Do you also supply them alive? Azim: Yes, we can. How many do you need? We keep the birds alive by tying them up. If their wings are left free, they will fly away. Reporter: These are foreign migratory birds, right? Azim: This is a Surkhab. It sells for a very high price. We will give it to you. Cook it separately; it is an excellent bird. Its meat is tender. Hold it and check; you won't find any bones. It is not sold openly. Some hotels serve it only to regular customers. The price can go up to ₹3,000 per kg. Reporter: What species is this other bird? Azim: This is Patera, and the other one is Chaha. Reporter: Why are they called that? Azim: Today, you can eat Chaha. I also have foreign Tikiya species of birds. Reporter: What is special about this one? Azim: It lives among water hyacinths and is a large bird. We caught it from a pond. Reporter: The police won't catch you, will they? Azim: We have no fear of the police. We supply them with meat. The hunter had prepared a price list for the birds: Surkhab meat: ₹3,000 per kg Lalsar meat: ₹2,500 per kg Tikiya meat: ₹650 per kg Chaha meat: ₹500 per kg Patera meat: ₹550 per kg Hunter says prices are non-negotiable; claims hunting requires hard work When the reporter asked for a lower price in exchange for a bulk order, the hunter refused. He said these birds arrive only once a year and that Lalsar and Surkhab are particularly difficult to find. They sell for ₹2,500 to ₹3,000 per kg. Hotels also have to place orders in advance because the meat is very expensive. He added that if we bought a larger quantity for hotels, he could offer a slightly lower rate, and we could sell it for up to ₹3,000 per kg. He also claimed that catching these birds required considerable effort. Hunters do not use guns to catch foreign birds During the sting operation, we also learnt about other hunters operating like Azim. Such hunting is reportedly taking place in several districts, including Pilibhit, Sant Kabir Nagar, Bahraich, Maharajganj, Prayagraj, Kanpur, Unnao, Hapur and Varanasi. These birds are found along the Ganga and in wetlands, lakes and ponds. Hunters reportedly use three methods: - Method 1: Hunters carry guns but do not use them. Instead, they lay spring-loaded traps to catch the birds. They sew the beaks and eyes of two or three Siberian birds with thread and tie them up. A rope is attached to the trap, which the hunter holds while hiding nearby. When a flock of Siberian birds lands on the trap, the hunter pulls the rope, trapping the birds by their long legs and claws. - Method 2: Hunters tie the legs of one or two Siberian birds with ropes and place them in water. This attracts other birds to the pond. Once the birds arrive, hunters catch them. They generally choose the morning hours for this. - Method 3: Some hunters put chemicals into ponds to kill fish, causing them to float to the surface. Foreign migratory birds then gather around these ponds, making them easier to hunt. When asked why they did not simply shoot the birds, the hunter said catching them alive helped preserve more meat, whereas shooting them resulted in greater wastage. Hunting peaks between November and February In Siberia, Russia, Mongolia and Central Asia, temperatures drop to between -20°C and -40°C from November to February. Thick layers of ice form over rivers and lakes, making it difficult for these birds to find food. These birds travel 4,000 to 6,000 km to reach India. After spending the winter here, they return to their countries in March and April. Hunting of these birds increases significantly during this period. Poaching can lead to up to seven years in prison - Non-bailable offence: Hunting, killing, selling the meat of or keeping protected migratory birds at home is a non-bailable offence. Rare and endangered migratory birds listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act receive the highest level of protection, on a par with tigers and elephants. - Strict punishment: Under Section 51 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, a first-time offender can face imprisonment ranging from three to seven years and a fine of ₹25,000 to ₹5 lakh. The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) is active in preventing illegal hunting and trade. During winter, special teams monitor lakes and wetlands through patrols and motorboats. In November 2018, the ministry launched a special action plan for the conservation of migratory birds under the Central Asian Flyway initiative. Protected lakes are also being developed as Ramsar sites. Number of migratory birds is declining Dr Yogesh Pratap Singh says birds from extremely cold regions migrate to the Terai wetlands of eastern UP. He says large-scale hunting due to administrative negligence is rapidly reducing their numbers. These birds play an important role in maintaining the balance of our ecosystem. Continuous hunting is making the birds feel unsafe. If the situation continues, they may stop visiting these areas permanently.

stories.title: NDA allies seek 4 times more seats:Claim ministerial constituencies too; BJP could face challenges if it contests fewer seats
stories.summary: The tussle over seat-sharing has begun within the NDA ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the BJP had allotted 32 seats to two of its allies, Apna Dal (S) and the Nishad Party. They won 23 of these seats. The RLD and SBSP, which were part of the Samajwadi Party alliance at the time, have now also joined the NDA. The four allies are now collectively demanding around 123 seats, nearly four times their combined allocation in the previous election. They argue that their support base and organisational strength have grown over the past four years. BJP National General Secretary and UP in-charge Vinod Tawde and state party president Pankaj Chaudhary are set to begin discussions with the allies to finalise a seat-sharing formula. The picture is expected to become clear by December. Here is a detailed breakdown of the allies' demands… RLD: Jayant eyes seats held by BJP ministers The RLD contested the previous election in alliance with the Samajwadi Party on 33 seats and won nine. After joining the NDA, the party has demanded 35 seats, spread from western to eastern UP. These include seats in Awadh and Purvanchal currently held by BJP MLAs. The Chhata seat in Mathura is particularly significant. Yogi government Cabinet Minister Chaudhary Laxmi Narayan represents this constituency. Giving up such seats could trigger resentment and rebellion within the BJP at the local level. This makes the RLD's demand one of the most complicated issues for the BJP. SBSP: Rajbhar insists on 17 seats allotted by SP The SBSP contested the previous election in alliance with the SP. It was allotted 17 seats and won six. Now aligned with the BJP, the party is demanding 25 to 30 seats. Its main condition is that it should get all 17 seats allotted to it by the SP in the previous election. It also wants a share of seats in other Purvanchal districts. Om Prakash Rajbhar claims that his party's presence will directly benefit the NDA in Purvanchal. Apna Dal (S): Demands more seats based on strike rate Anupriya Patel's party was the most successful NDA ally in the 2022 elections. It won 12 of the 17 seats it contested, emerging as the third-largest political party in the state. On this basis, Anupriya is demanding 30 seats this time, including the 17 it received previously. The additional seats include constituencies in Purvanchal and Bundelkhand where the BJP had lost. Nishad Party: Sanjay bets on seats lost by BJP Sanjay Nishad's party currently has five MLAs. For 2027, it is demanding 22 to 25 seats. Its proposed formula is that the BJP should allot it seats in addition to the constituencies it currently holds, particularly those where the BJP lost in 2022. Sanjay Nishad believes his party can perform better than the BJP in constituencies along riverbanks and those with a significant Nishad population. In the previous election, the party was allotted 16 seats. It contested 10 of them on its own symbol, a plate filled with food, and won six. On the remaining six seats, Nishad Party candidates contested on the BJP symbol and won five. How has the situation changed since 2022, and what could be the impact? In 2022, the BJP contested 376 of the 403 Assembly seats, leaving 27 for its allies. The BJP alone won 255 seats, comfortably above the majority mark of 202. However, the political picture for 2027 looks very different… BJP does not want smaller allies to grow stronger

stories.title: SP announces five candidates for Assembly polls:Names MP Iqra Hasan's brother from Kairana, a setback for Congress MP Imran Masood
stories.summary: For the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Samajwadi Party has sounded the election bugle first by releasing its first list of five candidates. Issued late on Tuesday night with the signature of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, the list seeks to work out the political equations in western Uttar Pradesh and Bundelkhand with the slogan, "This time, voting will be united in the name of the PDA." The SP announced two candidates in Saharanpur. On both seats, Imran Masood had been asserting the Congress's claim. Congress had also placed these seats in the non-negotiable category. Imran Masood had sought a total of five seats in Saharanpur, including Behat and Saharanpur, as well as Gangoh, Nakur and Rampur Maniharan. In 2022, the SP won two seats here-Behat and Saharanpur Rural. The SP has declared tickets for both its MLAs. Besides this, the SP has also announced the ticket of Naheed Hasan, brother of Iqra Hasan, who is currently an SP MLA. View the list...

stories.summary: Wedding celebrations have begun in the family of former Chief Minister Kalyan Singh. Ceremonies for the weddings of his grandsons, Uttar Pradesh minister Sandeep Singh and his brother Saurabh Singh, were held on Tuesday. At around 4 pm, the two brothers took part in a traditional wedding procession ceremony at Raj Palace on Marris Road in Aligarh. Their father, former MP Rajveer Singh, also known as Raju Bhaiya, danced with his sons. A video of the three dancing is going viral on social media. Both brothers mount horses after prayers The wedding ceremonies began with prayers and religious rituals. Sandeep and Saurabh mounted horses at the auspicious time. Raj Palace was filled with celebrations as drums played and music filled the air. Their father, Raju Bhaiya, was also seen dancing with his sons. See 3 pictures below : Mother Premlata, grandmother Ramwati Devi, both sisters, brothers-in-law, relatives and friends also took part in the ceremony. After the ghurchadhi ceremony, the entire family and close relatives left for Delhi. Sandeep Singh and Saurabh appeared in royal attire During the ghurchadhi ceremony, Minister Sandeep Singh was seen wearing a dark maroon sherwani with heavy embroidery. It featured intricate floral and vine motifs embroidered in white thread. He wore a pink sash around his waist, a cream-coloured safa on his head and embroidered juttis on his feet. His brother Saurabh Singh wore a light cream-coloured embroidered sherwani. It was paired with a pink sash and a border featuring golden gota-patti work. He wore a cream-coloured safa on his head, adorned with a kalgi-like embellishment. The wedding will take place at The Leela Hotel in Delhi on 26 November The two brothers will get married at The Leela Hotel in Delhi on 26 November. Sandeep Singh will take the seven rounds with his childhood friend Meghna Chaudhary, while Saurabh Singh will marry Antara Tyagi. Earlier, on 14 November, the two brothers got engaged in Talanagari, Aligarh. A grand venue had been prepared for the ceremony across around 100 bighas. Several prominent figures from politics and social life, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, attended the ceremony. The Prime Minister may also attend the ceremony A grand reception will be held on 27 November at The Jora, near Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Delhi. Prime Minister Narendra Modi may also attend the wedding ceremony, while several VVIPs and political figures are expected to be present. Political heavyweights, ministers, MPs and MLAs from the country and the state are also likely to attend the reception. Sandeep Singh is the MLA from Atrauli and the Minister of State for Basic Education in the state government. He is the grandson of former Chief Minister Kalyan Singh and the son of former MP Rajveer Singh. As a result, the weddings of the two brothers have become a topic of discussion not only as a family event but also in political circles.

stories.title: Why are seat-sharing tensions rising between Akhilesh and Rahul?:SP cites 2022, Congress 2024 polls; 3 formulas under discussion
stories.summary: Tensions over seat-sharing between the Samajwadi Party and Congress have started to rise ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. There are two main reasons for this. Congress is demanding 125 seats, while the Samajwadi Party has offered only 26. This has created a wide gap between the two parties. Both parties have different views on how to judge their electoral strength. The Samajwadi Party is looking at Congress's performance in the 2022 Assembly elections. Congress, however, says its position has changed after the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and it should not be judged by its earlier performance. Congress MP Imran Masood said, "We are not begging anyone. Congress is no longer the party it was in 2022." Leaders of both parties held a meeting for around three hours on Tuesday. After the meeting, Samajwadi Party general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav said that discussions were held on all 403 Assembly seats. He added that the talks would continue. The seat-sharing dispute is not just about the number of seats. It also reflects the struggle for a bigger role and leadership within the alliance. The Samajwadi Party wants to remain the alliance's largest partner, while Congress wants a bigger share based on its improved performance. Three formulas that could lead to an agreement... First: Congress gets 90 seats, with the SP fielding candidates in 35 According to SP sources, the party is prepared to offer the Congress 55 to 60 seats. In addition, it may offer the option of fielding its own candidates in 30 to 35 seats on the Congress symbol. This would allow the SP to field its strong candidates while increasing the number of seats allocated to the Congress. Second: Congress wants 100-125 seats, with its own candidates contesting 60-70 According to a leader associated with the Congress, the party wants 100 to 125 seats. It wants to field its own candidates in 60 to 70 of these seats. Samajwadi Party candidates could contest the remaining seats on the Congress symbol. Under this arrangement, the Congress would get an opportunity to strengthen its organisation and expand politically, while strong SP candidates could also find a place in the alliance. Third: Seat-sharing modelled on the Lok Sabha election In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the SP gave the Congress 17 of the 80 seats. This was a share of around 21.25 per cent. If the same ratio is applied to the Assembly election, the Congress would get around 86 seats. Under this formula, the Congress could stake a claim to at least 85 seats. The Congress wants at least one seat in every district, in addition to the Assembly constituencies falling under the Lok Sabha seats it holds. One thing is common to all three formulas: both parties want to field their respective strong candidates in the electoral fray. The dispute is over which party's candidate would be more useful to the alliance on which seat. SP's arithmetic: Congress gets 26 seats, party relies on its vote in 20 The list of 26 seats that the SP has given to the Congress includes two where the Congress won in 2022. Aradhana Mishra Mona won from Rampur Khas, while Virendra Chaudhary won from Pharenda. The Congress finished second in four seats-Mathura, Kheragarh, Jagdishpur and Kidwai Nagar. The SP's argument is that it has a strong vote base in the remaining 20 seats. According to Ram Gopal Yadav, the SP received between 60,000 and 70,000 votes in these seats in 2022, while the Congress received around 2,000 votes. The SP says the alliance could benefit if its strong candidates are fielded from these seats on the Congress symbol. The other aspect of this list is that Congress candidates forfeited their deposits on 16 of these 26 seats in 2022. In such a situation, the SP is presenting its proposal as offering the Congress more seats than its current strength in the Legislative Assembly. Of the 26 seats on the list, 10 were contested in 2022 by alliance partners that were with the SP. Of these, nine seats were held by the RLD, while the Pindra seat in Varanasi was held by Apna Dal (Kamerawadi). Congress believes it has a strong claim to the Assembly constituencies under its six Lok Sabha seats-Rae Bareli, Amethi, Saharanpur, Barabanki, Sitapur and Prayagraj. In addition, it wants at least one seat in every district. In other words, Congress is seeking not only a certain number of seats but also space to strengthen its political presence and expand its organisation across the state. Surprisingly, however, the list of 26 seats does not include Amethi and Rae Bareli. Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans says: Because of Rahul and Priyanka's active involvement, the Congress considers Rae Bareli and Amethi its political strongholds. The proposal did not include any Assembly seat from the area influenced by Saharanpur MP Imran Masood. No seat was left for the Congress in Lucknow either. The political implication could be that the Samajwadi Party does not want to give the Congress an opportunity to expand in areas where it seeks to build strength on the back of its senior leaders and organisation.

stories.title: Girl flees hotel in Meerut screaming ‘Help, help’:Man grabs her by the hair and pulls her back inside; escapes by jumping off the roof
stories.summary: Young woman ran out of a hotel in Meerut screaming for help. She was running away when a man caught her by the hair and tried to drag her back inside. Hearing her screams, people from the neighbourhood gathered at the spot. When they tried to enter the hotel, the staff stopped them. Meanwhile, the accused jumped off the hotel roof and fled. The incident took place in the Sadar Bazaar police station area. Man grabs woman by hair and tries to drag her back inside According to eyewitnesses, chaos broke out outside a hotel in the Sadar Bazaar area on Tuesday. A young woman ran out of the hotel, shouting for help. A man following her grabbed her by the hair and tried to pull her back inside. Seeing the woman being dragged, nearby shopkeepers and passers-by gathered at the spot. Some people tried to enter the hotel to rescue her, but the staff stopped them. Accused escapes by jumping off the roof As the crowd outside the hotel grew, the accused went to the rooftop and jumped down to escape. People then asked the woman what had happened. She said she had been held captive inside the hotel since Monday. She alleged that the man had kept her under his control at knifepoint. On Tuesday, she found an opportunity to get out and seek help from the public. Accused identified as a resident of Kankarkhera The woman identified the accused as Salman, a resident of Kankarkhera. After learning about the incident, Sachin Sirohi, national president of the Akhil Bharatiya Hindu Suraksha Sangathan, also reached the spot. He informed the police. Police arrived, questioned the woman and took her to the police station. Woman is from Ghaziabad At the police station, the woman told police that she was from Ghaziabad. She accused Salman of holding her captive in the hotel at knifepoint and forcibly keeping her under his control. Police are investigating the case based on her statement. They are also examining the circumstances under which she was kept at the hotel and the possible role of the hotel management. The search for the accused is underway, while the hotel's CCTV footage could also prove important to the investigation. The report is being updated…

stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri responds to Baba Ramdev calling him a hypocrite:Says he praised him 4 days ago, now criticises him; does not want to divide Hindu society
stories.summary: Bageshwar Dham head Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri has responded to Baba Ramdev calling him a hypocrite. He said the yoga guru had praised him from the stage just four days ago. "Perhaps he did not like something this time, so he said it. He does not feel uncomfortable about it," Shastri said. He added, "We will not respond to his words. He is our elder, senior and guardian. He has always shown us affection, and we have always respected him as our guardian. We accept both his criticism and his praise." Shastri said he could not disrespect saints. He added that his aim was to unite Hindu society, not divide it. He made these remarks while speaking to the media on Tuesday, the final day of the three-day Shri Hanumant Katha at Lamini Stadium in Pathankot. This is a developing story. More details will follow.

stories.title: Man stages his own death to avoid arrest:Blind youth killed, his Aadhaar card found near body
stories.summary: A man allegedly planned a murder to avoid arrest in criminal cases and frame his rivals in Shahjahanpur. He killed Rajpal, a visually impaired man, and cut off his head with a machete. He then threw the head in Badaun and left his own Aadhaar card near the body before fleeing. The accused had reportedly told Rajpal that he could cure his eyesight through rituals. He also involved a relative and the relative's friend in the plan by promising to turn brass coins into gold. Police said he carried out the murder to avoid the criminal cases registered against him and blame his rivals. Police arrested all three accused on the night of 23 November. On Tuesday, at around 1 pm, SP (Rural) Diksha Bhaware shared details of the case. The incident took place in the Kalan police station area, around 70 km from the district headquarters. Roamed around disguised as a holy man after being released from jail Five cases, including rape, have been registered against 50-year-old Vinod, a resident of Siuri village. He was released from jail on bail a year ago. He had been absconding ever since. Meanwhile, Vinod's wife and children had moved to Delhi. After his release from jail, Vinod roamed around disguised as a holy man and used occult rituals to lure people. Was looking for someone who lived alone Vinod's in-laws live in Chaudhera village, under the jurisdiction of Nigohi police station. Rajpal, 30, lived there. Rajpal's wife had put chilli in his eye around 10 years ago, causing him to lose his eyesight. After this, his wife left with their son. Vinod was thinking of a way to avoid a police case. He was looking for someone who had no family. This was why Vinod chose Rajpal as his target. He involved a relative and his friend in the conspiracy Vinod then began luring Rajpal. He told him that his eyesight could be restored through occult rituals. Convinced by Vinod's words, Rajpal agreed to undergo the rituals. However, Vinod feared that he would not be able to carry out the task alone. So he also involved his relative Vikas, who lived in Badaun, and Vikas's associate, Ompal. Promise to turn 15 brass coins into gold Vinod told his relative that he had 15 brass coins. He said the coins would turn into gold after a sacrifice. He would give all the coins to Vikas and Ompal. In addition, Vikas's aunt, who had left home, would also return. Greed prompted the two men to agree to sacrifice Rajpal. Head severed near the well, Aadhaar card placed beside the torso On the night of 14 November, the three reached a dry well in Siyuri. They called Rajpal there for a पूजा ceremony. Vinod then beheaded Rajpal with a billhook and crushed his face with a brick. Vinod placed his Aadhaar card near the torso. He then took the head to Badaun, around 50 kilometres away, and threw it into a river. Family falsely identified the body and had an FIR registered against nine people The torso was found in the well on 17 November. The villagers refused to accept that it was Vinod's body. On 18 November, Vinod's wife, Pooja, and son, Aditya, reached the village. They identified the body as Vinod's after seeing the thread tied around its leg. An FIR was registered against nine people, including the village head. Called his son to reveal that he was alive Meanwhile, Vinod bought a new SIM card and inserted it into Rajpal's mobile phone. Vinod then called his son and told him that he was alive. He revealed the entire plan to his family. Vinod told his family to go to the Chief Minister's public hearing to have their opponents sent to jail. This would put pressure on the police. Vinod's wife Pooja, mother Sumirta, brothers Nand Kishore and Kunwarpal, sons Alok and Aditya, and nephew Manoj then supported him. Surveillance and the deceased's mobile phone exposed the truth Meanwhile, when police showed the clothes from the body to Rajpal's villagers after receiving information that he was missing, his true identity was revealed. The police then placed Vinod and his family members' mobile phones under surveillance. As soon as Rajpal's mobile phone was switched on, the police traced its location and arrested Vinod and his two associates. The three accused were planning to flee from Budaun to Nepal. Seven family members involved in the conspiracy were also taken into custody. A billhook and a brick used in the murder were recovered from the accused. SP (Rural) Diksha Bhawre said: As the deceased was 30 and Vinod was 50, the police already suspected him. However, Vinod's wife and son blocked the road to put pressure on the police. The police have also added the names of seven family members to the FIR for their involvement in the conspiracy. All three accused have been sent to jail. Rajpal's head has not yet been found.

stories.title: Azam says he cannot be stopped from contesting polls:Rulers are cruel, and the entire country is living in fear
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party senior leader Azam Khan said on Tuesday in Rampur, "Who can stop me from contesting elections? My election symbol is the bicycle. The bicycle will contest, and the bicycle will win." Azam said he could not think of anything beyond the bicycle. "I do not want to think about cars, helicopters or planes," he said. Azam was released from Ghaziabad's Dasna Jail on interim bail on 18 November. Earlier, after being released from Rampur Jail on 31 October 2026, he was arrested in a case filed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). Read details below : Question: Will you contest the 2027 Assembly elections? Azam Khan: "Who can stop me from contesting elections? My election symbol is the bicycle. The bicycle will contest, and the bicycle will win." He said he could not think of anything beyond the bicycle. "People with small hearts and narrow thinking do not think about cars, helicopters or planes. They are doing their work, and we are doing ours. We are grateful to the High Court and Supreme Court judges," he said. Question: Are you afraid or worried about anything? Azam Khan: "People do feel afraid when the rulers are cruel. That is why people are silent and cannot speak their minds. They will express themselves on election day. It is not just me; the entire country is afraid." Question: But is there also fear of vote theft? Azam Khan: “There is fear. You were also worried about whether I would speak or not. Fear is something that exists in every heart.” Azam Khan says, 'One day, we will visit Nagina' Azam Khan was asked about the possible impact of a political alliance between Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad on Uttar Pradesh politics. In a joking tone, he said, "What are you talking about? One day, we will go to Nagina and tell the people there, as well as the people across the country." After his release from jail, several people have been visiting Rampur to meet the Samajwadi Party leader. These meetings are being linked to preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections and his future role in politics. Will Azam Khan be able to contest elections? According to legal experts, Azam Khan has been sentenced to jail terms ranging from 2 to 10 years in eight cases. Because of these convictions, he is currently not eligible to contest elections. Abdullla Azam has received relief in the fake birth certificate case, but he is also disqualified due to convictions in two other cases. Tanzeen Fatima can contest elections. However, considering her age and health, the names of Azam Khan's elder son, Adeeb, and daughter-in-law, Sidra, are also being discussed. According to senior Supreme Court lawyer Shariq Abbasi, getting bail alone does not make a person eligible to contest elections. The person must get a stay on the conviction from the court.

stories.title: Baba Ramdev softens criticism of Dhirendra Shastri:Describes him as a child and friend, a day after calling him fraud and hypocrite
stories.summary: Ramdev clarified his remarks about Dhirendra Shastri at a press conference in Haridwar on Tuesday. He said that Bageshwar Baba was like a child in front of him. He was also like his younger brother and disciple. Therefore, he had scolded him in his capacity as an elder over the things he found inappropriate and which had hurt him. Shastri had accepted his reprimand as an expression of affection. This also reflected his greatness. Ramdev said that a massive uproar had been going on for two days. He had also spoken to Dhirendra Shastri the previous day. He said he had been deeply hurt by the comments being made about their gods and goddesses. This was not part of the Sanatan tradition. There was no distinction among the gods. Discrimination being practised in the name of gods, castes and religions was dividing society. He said he was deeply saddened. Secondly, he had a serious question in his mind: Sanatan Dharma should not be associated with superstition or hypocrisy. This was because Sanatan Dharma was divine. Sanatan Dharma was scientific. The values of Sanatan Dharma were very lofty. The matter was trolled in a very wrong manner. My words should not have been taken this way. Now know what Ramdev had said earlier... 1. They do not know the Vedas, Upanishads or Constitution, yet claim to be Sanatanis Some people have neither read the Vedas, nor studied philosophy and the Upanishads, nor read the Puranas, the Ramayana or the Mahabharata. They do not know the Constitution or democracy either. They keep standing up and talking utter nonsense. They say, "We are Sanatanis; we will save Hinduism." Such people incite crowds with misguided ideas. He described such storytellers as frauds and hypocrites. 2. They exploit people by creating religious hysteria Some storytellers frighten people in the name of religion and possession by ghosts and spirits. They let their hair down, chant strange mantras and pretend to drive away ghosts. They then sprinkle water and claim that the problem has been resolved. This is a way of creating religious hysteria and exploiting people. He said women are the biggest victims of this hypocrisy. 3. Ram is great, Krishna is crooked... Repeated the same statement even after apologising Ramdev said, "Ram is great, while Krishna is crooked..." and then apologised. After apologising, he went there and bowed before Banke Bihari. Even after that, he is saying, "Krishna is indeed crooked!" You hypocrite, you have lost your senses! We are saying this deliberately: do not make such statements. No one has the right to make frivolous remarks in society. Everything has its own limits, discipline and protocol. 4. It is necessary to call out those who engage in hypocrisy, so I criticised them from the stage Do not compare deities. Even in jest or banter, do not disrespect or insult our divine incarnations. Who are we to compare deities, insult them or show them disrespect? How can we joke or banter about them? It is wrong. Even when someone says something like this personally, we try to explain it to them. If they still do not understand, we have to speak out from the stage. Otherwise, no one should say tomorrow that someone was engaging in hypocrisy while Swami Ramdev was present, and that Swami Ramdev did not stop him. That is why we have called it out from the stage here today. 5. We cannot engage in pretence and hypocrisy in the name of Sanatan Ramdev said that people should understand that deceit, ostentation and hypocrisy cannot be practised in the name of Sanatan. Such things are wrong and cause pain and distress within us. We are ascetics, so we will never make deranged remarks. Now, know which statement by Dhirendra Shastri sparked the controversy Shastri had said, "Your Thakurji is bent at 3 places" Dhirendra Krishna's remarks about Lord Krishna sparked a controversy. Comparing Lord Shri Ram with Lord Krishna, he said- 'Just look at even one picture of your Thakurji. Even when he stands, he is bent at three places. One foot over the other, he bends his waist and plays the flute with his neck tilted. Our Thakurji stands completely straight. Even his name is straight. Our Thakurji walks straight and looks straight too. Your Thakurji's name is crooked, he walks crooked and even stands crooked. Lifting a mountain is no great feat. A disciple of our God flew away with an entire mountain. Our God's abode is straight too-Ayodhya, while yours is Vrindavan!' Shastri said-Many people misunderstood what I said However, as the controversy grew, Dhirendra Shastri released a video clarifying his remarks. He said, "Many people misunderstood what I said. We ourselves are devotees of Thakurji and Braj. Whenever we pray to Thakurji, we ask that we be allowed to live in Braj." He said, "We also narrate the Shrimad Bhagwat Katha and sing the praises of Thakurji. We had no intention of differentiating between Lord Ram and Lord Krishna." In fact, Dhirendra Shastri had commented on Lord Krishna during the Shriram Katha being held in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh. After a video of the remarks emerged on 10 October (Sunday), the saints of Mathura expressed their displeasure. They had asked Dhirendra Shastri to apologise. Dhirendra Shastri reached Vrindavan on 21 November and offered prayers at the Banke Bihari temple. He said, "I bow by rubbing my nose at the feet of the people of Braj." He also led chants of, "Victory to the Crooked Thakur Ji... Victory to Hanuman Ji with the crooked leg..."
