stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav offers prayers at gurdwara in Lucknow:Says Election Commission is adding 3 crore voters under pressure from CM
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav alleged that the Election Commission was planning to add 3 crore voters under pressure from the Chief Minister. He said, "The account numbers of the people whose votes are being added are also being collected. It is worth considering who these account numbers will be given to." Earlier on Tuesday, Akhilesh Yadav visited a gurdwara in Sadar, Lucknow, where he paid obeisance and sought the blessings of Guru Nanak Dev. He spent more than half an hour at the gurdwara, attended the satsang and listened to kirtan. Akhilesh said the Sikh community had made many sacrifices for the country, which would always be remembered. He added that the community had made India proud across the world. Check out pictures below : The committee presented Akhilesh with a sword and prasad On reaching the gurdwara, Akhilesh Yadav tied a yellow scarf around his head and bowed in prayer. During the visit, the gurdwara committee honoured him by presenting him with a sword and prasad. Akhilesh Yadav said that the Sikh community had brought glory to India across the world. The Sikh community had made a significant contribution to strengthening the country's unity and integrity. Guru Nanak Dev had always conveyed the message of peace, unity and brotherhood. 'BJP putting pressure on Election Commission' Akhilesh Yadav said that the public wanted elections to be held on time. It was the responsibility of the constitutional body to conduct free and fair elections, but questions were now being raised about the body itself. The BJP's preparation was focused on how to add 3 crore voters. On the one hand, EVM machines were being repaired. On the other, continuous pressure was being exerted on the Election Commission. Alliances are formed to secure victory Akhilesh Yadav said that the party's senior leaders are holding discussions. They are discussing each other's seats and considering how many seats the other party could win. It is difficult to say anything at this stage about seat-sharing. Alliances are formed so that we can win. We will work together on an arrangement that enables us to defeat our opponents. 'Government unable to bring investment to the state' Akhilesh Yadav said, "They know they are going to lose the village-head elections, which is why they are not holding them on time. They have no answer on inflation and are unable to provide employment. They are unable to bring investment. They cannot answer the people, and the Bharatiya Janata Party will lose on the very day the election date is announced. We are the ones who are going to defeat them." Akhilesh Yadav said that the other party has to keep several allies happy. You must all have heard about a boat that does not know whether it will end up moored on this bank or the other. He claimed that Samajwadi Party candidate Sangram would win the Atroliya seat by a historic margin of votes.

stories.title: Stories of Kashi’s ghats to be available in 15 languages:Tourism Minister to launch service today, with broadcasts in French, German, Spanish and Japanese
stories.summary: Tourists and pilgrims visiting Varanasi will soon be able to explore the history of Kashi's 84 ghats without relying on guides. The Uttar Pradesh Tourism Department has linked all 84 ghats to a digital platform and developed the 'Varanasi 84 Ghats Audiobook-Audio Tour'. The GPS-based facility will allow visitors to listen to audio guides and read about the history, religious beliefs and cultural significance of each ghat in their preferred language. Tourism Minister Jaiveer Singh will launch the facility at Namo Ghat on Dev Deepawali. The department has completed preparations for the launch. The service will be accessible through the official UP Tourism mobile app and website. Separate options for walking tours and boat rides Individual audio chapters have been prepared for all 84 ghats, covering their historical, cultural, religious and mythological significance. Visitors will be able to choose between two modes: a walking tour and a boat tour. Those exploring the ghats on foot can select the 'walking tour' option, while visitors taking a boat ride on the Ganga can choose the 'boat tour' to listen to stories associated with the ghats. GPS to automatically play audio at each ghat The facility's main feature is its GPS-enabled smart system. As soon as visitors reach a ghat, the mobile app will detect their location and automatically play the corresponding audio guide. The audio will pause when they move away from the designated location and resume from the same point when they return. Visitors will also have the option to manually select any ghat and listen to its history and significance. Audio tour available in 15 languages To cater to domestic and international tourists, the audio tour has been developed in 15 languages. These include Hindi, English, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Gujarati, Kannada, Odia, Malayalam and Urdu. International visitors can also access it in French, German, Spanish, Japanese and Korean. Visitors will be able to download the complete audio tour before starting their trip. This will allow them to explore the ghats without requiring a continuous internet connection. People can explore Kashi's ghats from home The facility will also be accessible to people living outside Varanasi. Through the 'Enable Offline/Remote Tour' option, users from anywhere in India or abroad will be able to experience the ghats virtually. They can listen to stories and learn about the history and cultural heritage of Kashi's ghats from their homes. How to use the audio tour without logging in Visitors can access the facility by opening the official UP Tourism app on their Android or iOS smartphones. They will then need to select the 'Varanasi 84 Ghats Audiobook-Audio Tour' option, choose their preferred language and select either the walking or boat tour mode. After reaching a ghat, they can tap on 'Start Tour at Location' to begin the GPS-based audio guide. The service will also be available on the UP Tourism website. No account creation or login will be required.

stories.title: VIDEO | Leopard attacks man in Kanpur:Pounces as he enters field; 9 injured, people flee to save their lives
stories.summary: A leopard attacked villagers working in fields in Kanpur around noon on Tuesday, injuring nine people. Around 12 people initially entered the fields in an attempt to surround the leopard. Later, nearly 50 villagers gathered at the spot carrying sticks and clubs. During the operation, the leopard attacked them, leaving nine people injured. The injured were taken to hospital for treatment. Police and Forest Department teams reached the spot after receiving information about the incident. A search operation is under way to track down the leopard. The incident took place in Karan Kheda village, under the jurisdiction of Maharajpur police station. See 2 pictures.... Leopard attacks villagers attempting to surround it Villager Kishanlal said a leopard was spotted in the fields between 11 am and noon on Tuesday (24 Nov). After an alert was raised, villagers gathered at Ramsajeevan's marigold field. Around 12 people surrounded the animal from all sides, but it suddenly attacked them. After receiving information about the incident, nearly 50 villagers reached the field carrying sticks and began trying to corner the leopard. During this, the animal first attacked Ramkesh and then injured several others. Panic spread across the area as people ran for safety. Mohit Sharma, a resident of Madarpur, said he was harvesting cauliflower in a field when the leopard attacked him. Leopard also attacked villager who came to save his friend Injured Ravi Nishad said that he had gone to the field to pick marigold flowers. During this, the leopard attacked one of his friends. When he heard his friend scream and went to save him, the leopard attacked him as well. He somehow managed to escape from the spot with his life. Ravi said the leopard had also bitten and injured five or six other people besides him. 9 people injured, admitted to hospital The injured include Hariram Nishad (40), Ramkesh Nishad (18), Buddhi Nishad (50), Mohit Vishwakarma (18) and Sahil. Four other people were also injured. Sahil is a resident of Sikhtiya and had come to Karnakheda to stay at his maternal aunt's house. He suffered serious injuries. The injured were taken to hospital by their family members. On receiving the information, Sheikhpur outpost in-charge Anuj Patel and the Dial 112 team reached the spot. The police and Forest Department teams are conducting a search for the leopard with the villagers. Villagers urged to stay indoors The administration has appealed to villagers to stay in safe homes with their families and children. They have been advised not to go towards the fields alone and to work in the fields only in groups. Bhupendra Singh of the Forest Department said that Karnkheda village is situated along the river and is surrounded by forest. In such circumstances, a wild animal can emerge from the forest and enter the village. The Forest Department's rescue team has reached the spot and is conducting an operation to capture the animal.

stories.title: Fake oxytocin factory busted, 2 arrested in Dubagga:Accused mix phenyl, salt and powder; goods worth ₹2 crore seized
stories.summary: A joint team of the Special Task Force (STF) and Dubagga Police has busted an illegal factory manufacturing counterfeit oxytocin in Lucknow. Two men were arrested during a raid in Mohari Jehta village on Monday (23 Nov) night. Police seized fake oxytocin worth more than ₹2 crore, along with equipment and raw materials used in its manufacture. A vehicle allegedly used to transport and supply the counterfeit drug was also recovered from the premises. Two brothers arrested, fake oxytocin worth ₹2 crore seized According to police, the accused were preparing to fill the counterfeit oxytocin into bottles and ampoules before supplying it. The arrested men have been identified as Dildar and Irfan. The two brothers are residents of the Cattle Colony in Thakurganj. See 3 pictures... 3,700 bottles and 1.77 lakh ampoules seized During the raid, police recovered 3,700 bottles of 200 ml each and 1,77,800 plastic-packed ampoules of 2 ml each. The seizure also included 35 litres of liquid oxytocin, suspected powder, empty bottles, caps, rubber stoppers, packaging material and other equipment. A pickup vehicle was also seized from the premises. Police said materials used to manufacture and package counterfeit oxytocin were found at the site. Phenyl, salt and suspected powder found at factory Police recovered five-litre cans of phenyl, 36 packets of Tata Salt and suspected oxytocin powder from the premises. Investigators suspect that the accused were using these materials to manufacture counterfeit oxytocin. The STF and police are questioning the accused to establish where the counterfeit drug was being supplied and identify others involved in the operation. Case registered against two brothers A case has been registered against both accused at Dubagga police station under Case No. 360/2026. What is oxytocin, and why is it given to patients? Oxytocin is a hormone that is naturally produced in the body. It is also administered as an injection. In hospitals, it is mainly used during labour to induce uterine contractions and to stop excessive bleeding after childbirth. Using counterfeit medicine can pose a serious risk to patients.

stories.title: SP releases first list of 5 candidates for UP polls:3-hour seat-sharing talks with Congress end without deal; Congress seeks 125 seats, SP offers 26
stories.summary: The seat-sharing arrangement between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress in Uttar Pradesh appears to be heading for a deadlock. Akhilesh Yadav wants to offer Congress only 26 of the state's 403 Assembly seats, while Congress is sticking to its demand for 125 seats. On Tuesday, leaders of the two parties held a meeting lasting around 3 hours and 15 minutes at the residence of Congress MP Pramod Tiwari in Delhi. Discussions continued from 12.15 pm to 3.30 pm. SP announces five candidates for Assembly polls The Samajwadi Party released its first list of five candidates as seat-sharing talks cantinue with Congress. The SP announced two candidates in Saharanpur. On both seats, Imran Masood had been asserting the Congress's claim. Congress had also placed these seats in the non-negotiable category. Imran Masood had sought a total of five seats in Saharanpur, including Behat and Saharanpur, as well as Gangoh, Nakur and Rampur Maniharan. In 2022, the SP won two seats here-Behat and Saharanpur Rural. The SP has declared tickets for both its MLAs. Besides this, the SP has also announced the ticket of Naheed Hasan, brother of Iqra Hasan, who is currently an SP MLA. View the list... Before the meeting, SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav took a firm stance, saying, "I have given Congress a list of 26 seats from which it can field its candidates." SP MP Rajeev Rai also reiterated the same position. Congress MP Imran Masood objected to the SP's offer, saying, "We are not begging anyone. This is not appropriate for an alliance. Congress is much stronger today. It is no longer the same party it was in 2022." However, Akhilesh appeared to adopt a somewhat softer stance. In Lucknow, he said the objective of the alliance was to win the elections. The SP was ready to accommodate its allies by giving up seats and making adjustments, as this was a major political battle and the shared goal was victory. The second round of talks between the two parties has now concluded.After the meeting, leaders from both Congress and the SP appeared positive about the negotiations. Ram Gopal Yadav and Rajendra Pal Gautam said the alliance would be finalised within the next two days.

stories.title: 4 killed, including father and son, in Lakhimpur crash:Truck rams van, car crushed from 11 feet to 8 feet; 6 injured
stories.summary: A truck collided head-on with a van in Lakhimpur Kheri. Four people, including a father and son travelling in the van, were killed in the accident. Six people were injured. There were 11 people in the van. They were returning home after working all day. The collision was so severe that the van was completely mangled. The 11-foot van was reduced to 7-8 feet. The driver's cabin was crushed, and even the seat was torn out. The people remained trapped inside. The truck driver abandoned the vehicle and fled. Police reached the spot after receiving the information and sent the bodies for post-mortem examinations. They cut open the gate to pull the injured people out and took them to hospital by ambulance. The truck has been impounded and efforts are under way to locate the driver. The accident took place at 12.30 a.m. late on Monday night in the Sadar Kotwali area, around 12 km from the district headquarters. The deceased have been identified as Jagannath, 59, his son Pappu, 30, Ajay and Bahadur. Pictures of the accident- Now, let us understand the full case step by step- Mehwaganj outpost in-charge Bharat Singh said- The van was carrying more people than its capacity. Police are examining CCTV footage from the surrounding area. At present, the accident appears to have been caused by the van driver dozing off. However, the actual cause will be known only after the investigation.

stories.title: Suspected terrorist Ujaid arrested in Meerut:Was planning an attack on JK military airbase; probe reveals links to Pakistani handler
stories.summary: Security agencies arrested a suspected terrorist, Ujaid, in Meerut on Monday night over his alleged links with Pakistani handlers. He is accused of plotting an attack on a military airbase in Jammu and Kashmir and having connections with the Shahzad Bhatti gang. Investigators reportedly recovered several suspicious WhatsApp chats from his mobile phone. Ujaid was also in online contact with suspected terrorist Mohammad Sajid, who was arrested in Jammu and Kashmir on November 27, 2025. Suspect questioned by IB, ATS and other agencies During questioning, Sajid reportedly named Ujaid. Following his arrest, the Intelligence Bureau (IB), Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and other intelligence agencies questioned him. The investigation is under way. Ujaid is a resident of Baniyapara, under the Kotwali police station area. Suspect had been in contact with arrested terrorist for six months According to investigating agencies, Ujaid had been in online contact with suspected terrorist Mohammad Sajid for the past six months. Sajid was arrested in Jammu and Kashmir on November 27, 2025, while allegedly preparing to carry out a fidayeen attack on the Army. During questioning, Sajid reportedly disclosed Ujaid's name, following which police began searching for him. On January 18, 2026, Jammu and Kashmir Police raided Ujaid's house, but he managed to escape. Fearing further police action, his family locked the house and left. He was eventually arrested on Monday night. Suspect allegedly expressed willingness to carry out suicide attack According to sources, Ujaid discussed fidayeen attacks on social media and told Sajid that he was y to carry out a suicide attack. Police have recovered several chats related to these conversations from his mobile phone. Investigating agencies are examining the chats and other digital evidence. The investigation has also revealed that Ujaid was allegedly in contact with Pakistani handler Shahzad Bhatti. He is also accused of being part of a conspiracy to attack a military airbase in Jammu and Kashmir. After his arrest, the Intelligence Bureau (IB), Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and other intelligence agencies questioned him for several hours. Ujaid escaped during police raid on his house in January On January 18, the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Jammu and Kashmir Police raided the house of Ujaid Qureshi, a resident of Baniyapara in the Kotwali police station area, while searching for him. However, he was not at home at the time. The team pasted a notice outside the house before leaving. Some time later, Ujaid returned on a scooter but fled after seeing the notice. A video of the incident also surfaced. ATS suspects he was recruiting youths for terror activities According to the Uttar Pradesh ATS, Ujaid was active in a WhatsApp group where a conspiracy was allegedly being hatched to carry out a fidayeen attack on the Indian Army. The agency suspected that he was radicalising young people and recruiting them for terrorist activities. He was also suspected of being associated with an Al-Qaeda-linked sleeper cell. During the raid, the team detained his two brothers for questioning, but later released them. Case registered under Section 113 of the BNS A case was registered against Ujaid under Section 113 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). This section relates to terrorist activities. Investigating agencies were probing his alleged terrorist network, contacts and activities.

stories.title: Scorpio crashes into BJP MLA Sushil Singh’s convoy:Two Fortuners hit in Chandauli as MLA returns from Anant Singh’s daughter’s event
stories.summary: A speeding Scorpio rammed into two Fortuner SUVs in the convoy of BJP MLA Sushil Singh in Uttar Pradesh's Chandauli district. One of the Fortuners overturned, while both vehicles sustained damage. Three people travelling in the Scorpio were injured and taken to hospital. Four people, including the drivers, were travelling in the two Fortuners. Their occupants narrowly escaped injury. Four people were in the Scorpio, of whom three sustained injuries. MLA suspects conspiracy behind convoy accident The incident took place late on Monday night near Futiya and Jagdisarai villages in the Sadar Kotwali area. Sushil Singh, the BJP MLA from Saiyadraja, was returning from Mokama in Bihar with a convoy of 10 vehicles. He had gone there to congratulate MLA Anant Singh ahead of his daughter's wedding. The MLA was also travelling in the convoy when the accident occurred. He has raised the possibility of a conspiracy behind the incident. Two pictures related to the accident... Convoy vehicles hit at two locations The MLA's convoy was travelling from Chandauli to Varanasi. According to information, a speeding Scorpio collided with one of the convoy's Fortuners near Futiya village. After this, the driver tried to flee the scene. During this, the Scorpio collided with another Fortuner near Jagdisarai. One of the vehicles overturned in the accident. Some people also sustained minor injuries. Scorpio occupant admitted to hospital The injured youth has been identified as Pankaj Yadav, a resident of Manrajpur village in the Saiyadraja area. He was admitted to hospital in critical condition. Both Fortuners were also damaged in the accident. After receiving the information, police reached the scene and seized the Scorpio. Police are investigating the case. MLA Sushil Singh said, “He was present in the convoy at the time of the accident. His vehicle was not damaged. There is suspicion of a conspiracy behind the incident.”

stories.title: Former MP accused of rape in Gorakhpur:Woman alleges he had sex with her on promise of marriage, then blocked her number
stories.summary: A former MP from Purvanchal has been accused of rape and sexual exploitation in Gorakhpur. The woman approached the police station and created a scene, demanding action against him. Following this, Gorakhpur SSP assigned the investigation to Ramgarhtal police under the supervision of the Cantonment Circle Officer (CO). The complainant, a manager at a finance company in the Taramandal area, has alleged that the former MP established a physical relationship with her on the promise of marriage. Woman alleges former MP promised to marry her On Saturday, the woman created a scene at Ramgarhtal police station and insisted that a case be registered. In her written complaint, she alleged that the former public representative had taken her on a trip while he was in office. They stayed at a hotel, where he allegedly had a physical relationship with her after promising to marry her. She also claimed that he staged a marriage ceremony at a temple. However, she alleged that he has now been avoiding her requests to get married. When she pressed him on the issue, he allegedly threatened to kill her. Claims former MP blocked her number The woman further alleged that the former MP had blocked her mobile number. She claimed that people who live with him were also refusing to help her contact him. She reiterated that he had threatened to kill her and demanded police action. Police verifying photographs on her phone The woman showed police several photographs on her mobile phone, allegedly featuring her with the former public representative. She also showed a photograph of what she claimed was their wedding. Police are verifying the photographs found on her phone. Reports suggest that officers have also contacted the former MP, who reportedly said he was away on party-related work. Cantonment CO Arun Yash said the matter was being investigated and that further action would be taken based on the findings.

stories.title: 5 lakh devotees take holy dip in Ganga in Kashi:Crowds gather at 80 Ghats from 4 am; offer lamps and perform charity on Kartik Purnima
stories.summary: Varanasi witnessed a massive turnout of devotees on Tuesday on the occasion of Kartik Purnima. Large crowds gathered at around 80 ghats along the Ganga, including Dashashwamedh Ghat. Devotees began arriving as early as 4 am to take a holy dip. Despite the biting cold and dense fog, their enthusiasm remained undiminished. More than 5 lakh devotees had taken a holy dip in the Ganga by morning. After bathing, devotees offered water to the Sun God. They also performed charitable activities, chanted prayers, meditated and sang devotional hymns. Chants of 'Har Har Gange' and 'Har Har Mahadev' echoed across the ghats during the lamp-offering ceremonies. See the picture... Crowds gather from Dashashwamedh to Assi Ghat Dashashwamedh Ghat witnessed a steady stream of devotees from early morning. Heavy crowds were also reported at other prominent ghats, including Assi, Tulsi, Janki, Shivala, Dandi, Kedar, Darbhanga, Sheetla, Rajendra Prasad and Bhainsasur. After taking a holy dip in the Ganga, devotees offered lamps and worshipped the river. Religious rituals and prayers continued at various ghats throughout the morning. Holy dip and charity believed to bring eternal blessings According to religious beliefs, taking a dip in a sacred river before sunrise, offering lamps and performing charitable activities on Kartik Purnima hold special significance. It is believed that bathing in the Ganga on this day washes away sins and brings happiness and prosperity. The month of Kartik is considered sacred to Lord Vishnu. Devotees also worship Lord Vishnu and Goddess Tulsi on this occasion. Dev Deepawali is traditionally celebrated on Kartik Purnima. According to Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva killed the demon Tripurasura on this day, freeing the gods from his terror. To celebrate the victory, the gods lit lamps in Kashi and marked the occasion with a festival of lights. Police and river patrol teams remain on alert The administration and police made extensive security arrangements in view of the large crowds. As a security measure, people were prohibited from carrying belongings along the route from Godowlia Crossing towards Dashashwamedh Ghat. NDRF personnel continuously monitored the Ganga from boats. Police personnel, river police and women officers remained deployed under the supervision of Dashashwamedh ACP Vivek Kumar Tiwari and Station House Officer Santosh Kumar Singh. Special attention was given to crowd management at the ghats and the safety of devotees taking a dip in the river.

stories.title: Truck rams school bus on UP Expressway, killing 4:25 injured as children return to Kaushambi after picnic in Agra
stories.summary: Four children were killed and 25 others injured after a speeding truck rammed into a school bus from behind on the Lucknow-Agra Expressway in Uttar Pradesh’s Kannauj district. The bus was carrying 60 people, including 50 students. They were returning to Kaushambi after a picnic in Agra. Kannauj SP Vinod Kumar said the bus belonged to Oriental Public School in Kaushambi. It had left Agra at midnight on Tuesday. At around 6 am on Wednesday, the driver had stopped the bus on the expressway in the Tirwa police station area to allow the children to use the toilet. The accident happened during the stop. The impact was so severe that the rear section of the bus was badly damaged and several seats were dislodged. Several children were trapped between the seats. The truck driver is suspected to have dozed off at the wheel, possibly causing the crash. Please go through the live blog…to know the latest update on the Lucknow-Agra Expressway accident…

stories.title: Cold intensifies in UP as snowfall hits hills:Dense fog covers 15 cities; temperatures set to drop further next week
stories.summary: Snowfall in the hills has begun affecting the plains, with temperatures dropping across Uttar Pradesh. The cold is intensifying, accompanied by dense fog during the morning hours. On Tuesday morning, fog covered around 15 cities, including Prayagraj, Ballia, Deoria, Lakhimpur, Sambhal, Bijnor, Chandauli and Mau. On Monday, fog was particularly dense in Deoria and Sambhal, reducing visibility to just a few metres. Motorists faced difficulties due to poor visibility during the morning. According to Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, the impact of the cyclone over the Bay of Bengal has now ended. As a result, northerly and north-westerly winds have replaced easterly winds. These winds will gradually lower night temperatures, while dense fog is expected during the morning. The cold is likely to intensify further from next week. Night temperatures may fall by 3–5 degrees According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), winds are likely to turn westerly following the withdrawal of the cyclone's influence. This could lead to a fall of 3–5 degrees Celsius in minimum temperatures across the state over the next few days. This will increase the chill during the night and early morning hours. Moderate to dense fog is likely across most parts of the state, including the Terai districts. People are advised to take precautions against the cold, particularly during early mornings and late nights. Farmers advised to protect crops from cold and fog Wheat: Maintain adequate moisture in the soil during the early growth stage. Avoid waterlogging in fields. Mustard: Prolonged fog and moisture can increase the risk of white rust and other fungal diseases. Monitor crops regularly. Potato: Check leaves for signs of late blight. Consult agricultural experts if symptoms appear. Peas and gram: Excess moisture and waterlogging can damage roots. Ensure proper drainage in fields.

Pakistani Hindus visit India to attend Ram Katha:Say they cannot worship openly; women say they observe ghunghat because they don't wear burqa
stories.summary: At a grand pandal in Kunda, Pandit Dhirendra Shastri is narrating the Ram Katha. A sea of devotees has gathered, but the rows at the front of the VIP enclosure, illuminated by the pandal’s bright white lights, are attracting everyone's attention. On one side are women dressed in traditional Rajasthani-Sindhi attire, their faces covered with long veils. On the other are men sitting emotionally, with sandalwood tilaks on their foreheads and their hands folded in prayer. These are no ordinary devotees. They are Hindu refugees who left their homes and land in Pakistan's Sindh province and came to India. Invited specially by Kunda MLA Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya, these refugees travelled from Jodhpur in 10 buses. They have not only been given seats at the front of the Katha pandal but are also receiving royal hospitality at three large camps set up in a mango orchard behind Benti Raj Bhavan. These people are currently at the centre of the grand Ram Katha in Kunda. They say that although they used to worship in Pakistan too, they had to do so secretly. They are receiving such respect for the first time. Read the full report… Raja Bhaiya, the MLA from Kunda, visited Rajasthan in 2024. During his visit to Jodhpur, he met Hindu refugees. These people had fled Pakistan's Sindh province and moved to India in different years. They shared their suffering with Raja Bhaiya, saying that they had left behind their homes and everything they owned and were now somehow managing to make ends meet in India. Raja Bhaiya helped them. The initiative that began at that time has continued ever since. Several Pakistani refugees also live in Delhi's Majnu Ka Tila area. Raja Bhaiya met them as well. Later, the refugees' children celebrated his birthday. Pakistani refugees perform the role of hosts; Dhirendra Shastri conducts a havan Because of his affection for the Pakistani refugees, Raja Bhaiya had decided last year that whenever he organised a Ram Katha, he would invite them. On the first day of the Katha, they were brought from Jodhpur to Kunda in 10 buses. Three large camps have been set up in a mango orchard behind Raja Bhaiya's Benti Raj Bhavan, where they are staying. Their number is estimated to be around 500. A dedicated team has been assigned to look after them and make arrangements for their food and drinking water. For now, they have been kept away from the general public, and police personnel have also been deployed around the camps. The refugees were brought together at Benti Raj Bhavan, where a havan, prayers and purification rituals were performed. Pandit Dhirendra Shastri himself sat at the Yajna altar during the ceremony. The Bhaskar team was also present. Refugees say they left Pakistan for the sake of Sanatan Dharma Speaking to us, Heeralaal, who came from Pakistan, says, "We left Pakistan in 2018. We never imagined in our lives that we would get an opportunity to meet Bageshwar Baba. Our hearts are filled with happiness. The best part was that he performed a havan with us. It felt as if our souls had been purified. All our needs are being taken care of here." We asked him: Do you want to return to Pakistan now? Heeralaal says, "We want to get Indian citizenship. This country is good. We left Pakistan for the sake of Sanatan Dharma. We have the right to worship here, but we cannot do so openly there. We have to worship inside our homes out of fear. There is discrimination in children's education too. We send our younger daughters to school, but once they grow older, we are afraid to send them. You must be seeing on news channels what is happening to Hindus in Pakistan." Women say they have become accustomed to covering their faces The Hindu women refugees from Pakistan attending the Ram Katha had their faces covered with long veils. We asked one of the women why they were wearing veils. She said, "Muslim women in Pakistan wear burqas, so most Hindu women who step outside their homes also cover their faces with veils. This is done to keep their faces covered. So, out of habit, the women continued to cover their faces while listening to the Katha." Sita Devi, 40, says, "We are very happy to have come to Kunda. We had seen and listened to Bageshwar Dham on our mobile phones, but today we are seeing him in person for the first time. Nobody has ever invited us and given us front-row seats like VIPs before. I don't think we will ever get such an opportunity again." Speaking about the situation in Pakistan, she says, "We do not have any major problems there, but inflation is very high. People do not even have enough money to buy everyday essentials." Radha, who was sitting nearby, says, "We had come here 10 years ago as well. But wearing a veil is part of our culture and tradition, which is why we are wearing veils here in Kunda too." 'People are raped based on their religion, which makes us more afraid' At the Katha pandal, we met Akash and his family. It emerged that they had come to India on tourist visas in 2018 and never returned to Pakistan. They have not yet received Indian citizenship, but have started their education here. Akash says, "There is a lot of discrimination between Hindus and Muslims in Pakistan. People are raped on the basis of their religion. Nothing like that happens here, which is why we left our homes and land behind and came to India. However, we are facing some difficulties at the moment because we have to keep visiting police stations due to our arrival from Pakistan. Teachers at school treat us well, but the students studying with us do not consider us one of their own." Akash further says, "Some members of our family are still in Pakistan. We remain in touch with them. They say that if they get visas, they too will leave Pakistan and come to India. We feel safe here." Here are the VIP facilities being provided to the refugees Around 500 people who came from Pakistan are being provided with VIP facilities at the Ram Katha. Whenever they leave their camps and enter the main pandal, a special 'green corridor' is arranged for them. Volunteers form a security cordon on both sides, while the group moves straight towards its reserved seats in front of the stage, chanting 'Jai Shri Ram'. Amid the dazzling lights of the pandal and its devotional atmosphere, the expressions on their faces clearly reflect a sense of happiness and relief. Suresh, whom we met in the same row, appeared extremely happy. He says, "I am around 50 years old. I have never had the opportunity to attend such an event in my life. I can only thank Raja Bhaiya. "On 20 November, that is, tomorrow, after the Ram Katha concludes, we will visit the Sangam in Prayagraj. We will take a dip in the Ganga. After that, we will visit Baba Vishwanath in Varanasi and seek the blessings of Ram Lalla in Ayodhya. Then we will return to Jodhpur." Why is there a hurdle in getting Indian citizenship? Read this too Jodhpur, from where the refugees travelled to Kunda, is home to around 17,000 to 18,000 Pakistani Hindu migrants. They live in 21 different settlements across the city. These settlements are located in the Sursagar, Mandore, Kaliberi and Chokhan areas. Those who arrived in India 40 years ago have received citizenship. However, those who have not completed 40 years in the country have not received citizenship. The refugees said that most of them arrived after 2014, which is also creating difficulties in obtaining citizenship.

stories.title: Can BJP launch an Ayodhya-like movement in Mathura?:Three major challenges in Krishna Janmabhoomi case; 2027 could bring political gains as well as losses
stories.summary: Ram Temple movement gave the BJP recognition and political strength in the country's politics. During the decades-long movement, the RSS, VHP, saint community and BJP worked together. After the construction of the temple in Ayodhya, the BJP is now turning its attention to Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura. On 16–17 November, the BJP held its national brainstorming meeting in Mathura. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya said, "Ayodhya is ours; now it is Mathura's turn." He also challenged Akhilesh Yadav to visit Mathura and participate in kar seva. After the meeting, the slogan 'Radhe-Radhe, Kamal Khila De' (Radhe-Radhe, make the lotus bloom) echoed through the gathering. The question now is whether the BJP will launch a movement in Mathura similar to the Ram Temple movement. How much strength does the party have, and what challenges does it face? Will the Mathura issue only benefit the BJP, or could it also cause political damage? Read this in the UP Explainer… Ayodhya and Mathura are both centres of Hindu faith. There are claims that ancient temples at both places were demolished to build mosques. However, there are several differences in the land ownership claims and the present situation. Here is an explanation: The BJP and RSS have organisational strength on the ground as well as political power to pursue the issue. Compared with the 1990s, their circumstances, resources and networks are considerably stronger today. This can be understood through five points. A) RSS-BJP network Today, the BJP and RSS networks have reached almost every village and neighbourhood across the country. From panna pramukhs to mandal-level workers, the organisations have a trained workforce that can spread a message to millions of people within hours. During the Ram Temple movement, the BJP was in the Opposition and faced government restrictions. Today, the BJP has governments with a full majority at both the Centre and in Uttar Pradesh. This makes it easier to run a campaign. B) Krishna devotion is not limited to Braj The tradition of devotion to Lord Krishna is not confined to Mathura or the Braj region. There is a deep-rooted tradition of Krishna worship across Gujarat (Dwarka), Rajasthan (Nathdwara and Khatu Shyam), Maharashtra (Vitthal), Odisha (Jagannath Puri), Bengal, Manipur and southern India (Guruvayur and Udupi). Lord Krishna is not merely a religious symbol. He also has a strong connection with the large OBC community in north India, particularly the Yadav community. C) Role of saints and religious organisations Saints, Mahamandaleshwars, akharas and religious preachers have a direct influence on Indian society. Today, social media and television channels have expanded their reach to millions of people. If the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), Bajrang Dal, Akhil Bharatiya Akhara Parishad and prominent religious preachers from across the country come together on one platform and raise the demand, the issue could grow beyond a political party and become a major social and religious campaign. D) Experience of the Ayodhya movement The BJP and RSS have experience of the Ram Temple movement. They know how to connect a religious issue with the common person's sense of pride and identity. RSS-affiliated organisations are well versed in building public sentiment through Rath Yatras, Kalash Yatras, group Hanuman Chalisa recitations and devotional programmes, even without aggressive protests. Digital networks have made this process much faster than before. E) Unfinished religious agenda after Ayodhya The slogan 'Ayodhya is just the beginning; Kashi and Mathura are still left' has echoed among RSS and BJP supporters for decades. The construction of the Ram Temple has strengthened the belief among sections of society that even decades-old religious issues can be resolved. This provides a strong ideological foundation for taking up the Mathura issue. From a political and social perspective, the BJP has all the necessary elements to launch a movement in Mathura. However, the task will not be easy. The legal framework, ground realities and responsibilities of being in power in the Mathura case are different from those of the 1990s. The challenges can be understood through three major points. Challenge 1: Devotees do not yet show the same intensity of emotion as in 1990 Lord Ram Lalla remained in a tent for decades, creating deep anguish and anger among ordinary people. The situation in Mathura is different. Of the total 13.37 acres of land at the birthplace, a grand temple has already been built on 10.9 acres. Devotees can visit and offer prayers without restrictions. The Shahi Idgah mosque occupies 2.47 acres, which is the subject of the dispute. Today, along with religious faith, ordinary people also prioritise inflation, employment, education and basic facilities. Therefore, without strong public sentiment, it will not be easy to mobilise people for a movement that could continue for years. During the Ayodhya movement, the VHP and the Ram Janmabhoomi Nyas were working under central leadership. In Mathura, there are different akharas, saints and petitioners. It will not be easy to build a consensus on whether to wait for the court's verdict or launch a street movement. Keeping all organisations united behind the same timeline and strategy will be a major challenge. Challenge 2: The BJP was in the Opposition then, but is in power now For most of the Ram Temple movement, the BJP was in the Opposition. At that time, protesting against the government, organising Rath Yatras or courting arrest was politically easier. Today, the BJP is in power both at the Centre and in Uttar Pradesh. It also has a constitutional responsibility to maintain law and order. Therefore, a movement involving street clashes or vandalism is unlikely to be an option. The BJP faces a dual challenge. On one hand, it has to maintain the enthusiasm of its supporters. On the other, it must ensure law and order and maintain social harmony. Millions of devotees from India and abroad visit Mathura-Vrindavan every day. Any tension could not only raise questions about law and order in Uttar Pradesh but also damage the state's image as a destination for investment and tourism. Challenge 3: Places of Worship Act, 1991 The law states that the religious character of any place of worship as it existed on 15 August 1947 cannot be changed. Ayodhya was exempted from this law. However, Mathura was not given any such exemption. Arguments are underway in the Supreme Court over the constitutional validity of this law and its applicability to the Mathura case. Until a clear legal path emerges or Parliament makes changes to the law, any major movement will appear to be in direct conflict with the legislation. The Mathura issue could prove to be a double-edged sword for the BJP in the 2027 elections. It could strengthen the party's hold among its traditional voters. However, it could also invite allegations of promoting religious polarisation and diverting attention from ground-level issues. Potential benefits Potential disadvantages

stories.title: 'Men too deserve respect, safety and justice':Congress leader Rakesh Verma says, 'Name someone like King Dasharatha, and we will kill him'
stories.summary: Congress leader and former IAS officer Dr. Rakesh Verma said in Lucknow, "Because of Kaikeyi, Ram had to go into exile. A similar situation still exists. If there is someone like King Dasharath in today's time, tell us-we will kill #@%." Dr Rakesh Verma was a 1997-batch PCS officer. He was promoted to the IAS cadre in 2019. However, he also took voluntary retirement from it in 2020. He joined the Congress on 9 September. He attended the 'Silent Sentinel, Unspoken Emotions' programme in Gomti Nagar on Thursday to mark International Men's Day. Discussions on men's emotional health, family responsibilities, and their role in society were under way at the event. 3 key points made by Rakesh Verma 1. Raised questions about patriarchal society by citing Kaikeyi's example Dr Rakesh Verma, citing the example of Ram's exile, said that even King Dasharath could not prevent a major decision under Kaikeyi's influence. He questioned how society could always be called male-dominated when a woman was capable of wielding such influence. 2. Men's difficulties in divorce and child custody cases highlighted They said, "Men have to undergo lengthy legal proceedings and financial difficulties in divorce and child custody cases." They cited the example of their friend Anand Singh, who fought a case in the Supreme Court twice for custody of his children. 3. Claimed that crores were spent on the judicial process Rakesh Verma said, "Their friend Anand Singh spent around ₹4 crore, including lawyers' fees, in the custody battle. The legal process can exhaust a family's entire savings, and men should also receive fair justice."

stories.title: Car crashes into bike at 100 kmph, killing four:Vehicle flies 20 feet into the air and hits tree; victims had come from UP to attend wedding in Buxar
stories.summary: A speeding car hit a motorcycle from behind in Buxar on Thursday evening. In the collision, the car was thrown 20 feet into the air before crashing into a tree. Four people died in the accident. The accident took place near Sonpa village in the Rajpur police station area. It is reported that three people travelling in the car died on the spot, while the motorcyclist died during treatment at a hospital. The deceased have been identified as Irfan Ansari, 25, Arbaaz Ansari, 20, and Badal Kumar, 30, all residents of Bhataura village in Uttar Pradesh's Gahmar police station area. All three were travelling in the car. The motorcyclist has been identified as Arun Kumar, 22. Other people were also injured in the accident and have been referred for better treatment. According to information, the occupants of the car were travelling with a wedding procession from Bhautoura village in Uttar Pradesh to Bishanpur village in Bihar's Ramgarh police station area. During the journey, the car hit a motorcycle from behind near Sonpa village on NH-319A. The motorcyclist had travelled only around 50 metres after leaving a relative's house when the accident occurred. See the pictures of the accident... Car thrown into the air after collision According to eyewitnesses, the impact was so powerful that the car was flung around 20 feet into the air. It then crossed a water-filled ditch around 10 feet deep by the roadside before crashing into a tree. Chaos broke out at the scene after the accident. The car was travelling at 100 kmph Eyewitness Raviranjan Singh said the car was travelling at more than 100 kilometres per hour. Because of the high speed, the driver could not control the vehicle even after seeing the motorcycle and crashed into it from behind with great force. Three died at the scene, fourth succumbed to injuries in hospital Local residents took the injured to hospital after the accident. Rajpur police station in-charge Niwas Kumar said three people had died at the scene. The injured were taken to hospital, where one of the motorcyclists died during treatment. The matter is being investigated.

stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri depicted as Kansa in Mathura:Shown being struck by Lord Krishna; people say an apology will not save him
stories.summary: In Mathura, a poster depicted Bageshwar Dham head priest Pandit Dhirendra Shastri as Kansa, with Lord Krishna shown beating him. Every year, the Kansa Vadh Mela is held in Mathura's Rangeshwar area, featuring a variety of tableaux. On Thursday, the Mathur Chaturved Parishad's tableau depicted Dhirendra Shastri as Kansa. Mathur Chaturved Parishad president Rajan Pathak said, "There is no difference between Krishna and Ram. If you use abusive language about any god, do not assume that you can escape by apologising." At the Kansa Vadh Mela, children and elderly people beat an 18.5-foot-tall effigy with sticks. It is believed that when Lord Krishna and Balaram killed Kansa, the people of Braj were also present with them. This tradition has continued ever since. See 3 pictures... Read what Dhirendra Shastri had said about Lord Ram and Krishna Dhirendra Shastri had commented on Shri Krishna during the Shri Ram Katha being held in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh. A video of the remarks emerged on 10 October (Sunday). He had said: "Just look at even one picture of your Thakurji. Even when he stands, he is bent at three places. One foot over the other, bending at the waist in places, and playing the flute with his neck tilted. Our Lord, on the other hand, stands completely straight. Even his name is straight. Our Lord walks straight and looks straight as well. Your Lord's name is crooked, he walks crooked and stands crooked. Lifting a mountain is not a big deal. A disciple of our Lord made an entire mountain fly. Even the abode of our Lord is straight-Ayodhya; while your Lord's is Vrindavan!" Mathura's sadhus and saints expressed their displeasure over the statement and had demanded that Dhirendra Shastri apologise. However, as the controversy intensified, Dhirendra Shastri released a video clarification and said, "Many people misunderstood what I said. We are ourselves devotees of Thakurji and Braj." "We also narrate the Shrimad Bhagwat Katha and sing the praises of Thakurji. We had no intention of distinguishing between Lord Ram and Lord Krishna." What Dhirendra Shastri said in his clarification Pandit Dhirendra Shastri further clarified his statement, saying, "Just as the sakhis reproach Shri Ram, the gopis reproach Thakur Shri Krishna, poet Binduji Maharaj reproaches Thakurji, and Braj's saint Kokil Sai Ji reproaches Raghunath Ji, we too recited a verse in that spirit. It is a very popular verse by a saint: 'Playing the flute is just a game, but picking up the bow is not.'" We were explaining that very verse. However, instead of watching the full video, many people watched only half of it and branded us anti-Krishna. We are not anti-Krishna. Shri Krishna is our Thakurji. We ourselves repeatedly raise our voice for Krishna Janmabhoomi. His name is also part of our name. Our life exists because of him. Dhirendra Shastri said, "If our statement, explanation or sentiment has hurt anyone's feelings, we apologise. Please do not misinterpret our statement and present it in an exaggerated manner. We have not tried to divide society or God. Why would we divide God?" Ram and Krishna are one and the same. There is no difference between them. We said this emotionally. Even so, we ask all of you to understand our feelings. 'Playing the flute is a game; shooting a bow is not' Dhirendra Shastri had said, "Playing the flute is a game, but shooting a bow is not. All those of you seated here who worship Thakurji, today even your Thakurji is being hailed." He then pointed towards the artist playing the flute and said, "Listen, what does your Thakurji do? Play the flute? So playing the flute is hardly a big deal. Look, even this person here is playing it. Play it, play it. Go on, go on." After this, the flautist played a tune on the flute for some time. Dhirendra Shastri asked the people attending the religious discourse, "How many of you worship Lord Ram? Raise your hands. Yes! You people will be overjoyed today." ‘Grazing cows is a game; making monkeys dance is not’ Dhirendra Shastri had also referred to Lord Krishna herding cows and lifting a mountain. He had said, "People will say that our God herds cows. Anyone can herd cows. Herding cows is a game too; making monkeys dance is not." He then referred to Lord Krishna lifting Govardhan Hill. He had said, "You will say that our God can lift a mountain. Is that such a big deal? A disciple of our God flew away with an entire mountain." He was referring to Hanuman, a devotee of Lord Ram. Anger among Mathura's saints: read who said what- Dinesh Falahaari said- Even Ravana's arrogance did not last Dinesh Falahaari Maharaj, the petitioner in the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi temple-mosque case in Mathura, expressed his displeasure over Dhirendra Shastri's remarks. He said that Ram is Brahman and Shri Krishna is Yogeshwar. Our Krishna Kanhaiya is loved by the people of Braj. It is inappropriate to make remarks about him. Whether it is Dhirendra Shastri or anyone else, the people of Braj will not forgive him. Even Ravana's arrogance did not last, so who are you? Sadhvi says: Krishna is beloved by every resident of Braj Sadhvi Indulekha said that Shri Krishna is our revered deity. Dhirendra Shastri's remarks will not be tolerated at all. Krishna is beloved by every resident of Braj. Therefore, Dhirendra Shastri should apologise for his remarks. "Bageshwar Sarkar must apologise, or we will not remain silent" Pandit Rajesh Pathak said that no objectionable remarks about Shri Krishna could be tolerated, even in jest. History bears witness that whenever a sadhu, saint or storyteller has made an inappropriate comment about Shri Krishna, the people of Braj have opposed it. Bageshwar Sarkar's remarks will also be strongly opposed. If he does not apologise, the people of Braj will not remain silent. 2 years ago, Pandit Pradeep Mishra made remarks and later rubbed his nose on the ground Earlier, storyteller Pandit Pradeep Mishra had made controversial remarks about Radha Rani in Omkareshwar on 9 June 2024. He had said, "Radha Rani is not among Lord Shri Krishna's 108 chief queens and 1,600 wives. Radha's husband's name was Anay Ghosh, her mother-in-law's name was Jatila and her sister-in-law's name was Kutila. Radhaji was married in Chhata." He had also said that Radhaji was not from Barsana but lived in Rawal. Her father had a court in Barsana, which she visited once a year. Saints and people from Braj had protested after a sermon by Pradeep Mishra went viral. The sharpest reaction came from Premanand Maharaj. He said, "What do you know about Ladli Ji? What do you know at all? If you had spoken after consuming the dust from a saint's feet, such words would never have come from your mouth." After the controversy escalated, Pradeep Mishra visited the Barsana temple on 29 June 2024. He apologised at the temple for his remarks about Radha Rani's birth and marriage, rubbing his nose on the floor and offering a full prostration.

stories.title: Azam Khan reaches SP office, says 'I am still alive':Targets Owaisi with beard remark; says he does not like Hyderabadi biryani
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan reached the party's district office in Rampur on Thursday, the second day after his release from prison. He said, "Whatever happened to me was extremely bad. What worse could happen now? All the buildings that have been constructed here should also be demolished by bringing in bulldozers." Regarding the allegations against him, Azam Khan said, "I am still alive." Azam also took a dig at AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi. He said, "Hyderabadi biryani" is not liked in our area. People here prefer eating "pulao" and mutton biryani. He is a barrister, not a "maulana". Merely growing a beard does not make someone a "maulana", just as growing a beard does not make someone a "sadhu". Referring to Owaisi's rally in Rampur, he said, "My house was just four steps away. There was a free telephone. You could have asked my wife about my well-being. You could have paid a visit. That was not a prayer; it was medicine for my enemies." Read Azam's five major statements 1- In our organisation, positions and words have their own dignity Azam said that positions and words have their own dignity and propriety in our organisation. Referring to SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, he said that Yadav had been a Member of Parliament five times. He is the Chief Minister's son and has himself served as Chief Minister. Therefore, positions and words are accorded full respect in our organisation. 2- Congress is no longer what it used to be On the Congress-Samajwadi Party alliance, Azam said, "This is not the old Congress. The leadership today is different." However, he also said, "If any agreement has been reached between the two parties, it is a good thing." 3- The CBI's credibility has deteriorated severely Azam Khan said, "All constitutional institutions should safeguard their own dignity. The CBI's credibility has deteriorated severely. The agency should protect its reputation, because it is bringing disgrace to the country around the world." 4- Last time, it was an 'election of loot and plunder' Azam said that nothing happened in the election; rather, it was entirely an "election of loot and plunder". "I am its biggest victim myself. When Rampur was looted for the first time, police officers chased people with country-made pistols. Bolts were fastened on the outside of houses, and the police and PAC were deployed in the lanes to prevent people from voting." If the INDIA bloc had united and taken this issue seriously at the time, the election results in Kundarki, Sambhal, Haryana and Bengal would not have turned out this way. He alleged that the alliance leaders had not taken the incident seriously enough. 5-My membership was terminated and elections were held within 15 days Azam said that several cases had been filed against him, one of which was a "hate speech" case. His Assembly membership was terminated in this case. New elections were announced within just 48 hours, after which the elections were held within a period of one week to 15 days. However, the decision on his appeal came 15 days after that. Azam gets relief from Supreme Court, will remain out of jail SP leader Azam Khan will remain out of jail. The Supreme Court granted him major relief on Thursday. The ED had filed a petition in the Supreme Court challenging the interim bail granted to him by the Allahabad High Court. The court dismissed the petition within five minutes of the hearing beginning. It said, "This is an interim order, so we do not want to interfere in it. The High Court's observations will have no bearing on the final verdict." In fact, the Allahabad High Court granted interim bail to Azam in the money-laundering case linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust on 17 November. It said that the circumstances of the case showed that the action had been taken with malicious intent. Azam had been released from Dasna jail on Wednesday Azam was subsequently released from jail and reached Rampur at 10 p.m. on Wednesday night. On 31 October, the Enforcement Directorate arrested Azam just 40 minutes after he was released from Rampur jail. He had been lodged in Ghaziabad's Dasna jail ever since. Even before Azam reached home, a stream of supporters had gathered to meet him. The people present outside his residence said they had complete faith in the court. They hoped that Azam Khan would continue to receive relief in the future. Now read what Azam's supporters said Samajwadi Party leader Anuradha Chaudhary, who has contested the election from Swar-Tanda, said, "What greater happiness could there be than the Supreme Court dismissing the petition filed by the Enforcement Directorate regarding her bail? The people sitting in our country's institutions should think about the fact that they must not become anyone's slaves." 'We trusted the courts and will receive relief in the future too' Jeeshan Malik said, "We wholeheartedly thank the Supreme Court for its verdict. We had complete faith in the courts, and will continue to have it." Sulaiman said that he considered it a major relief for Azam Khan. "We had hoped that one day we would receive justice from the court, and today justice has been delivered to us." An elderly supporter said that the entire country was happy about Azam Khan's release and the Supreme Court's decision. Supporters have been enthusiastic since he returned home. Now, find out how the Supreme Court granted relief to Azam The judge reprimanded the ED, saying, "The sky would not fall." The Supreme Court had asked the High Court to decide the case expeditiously On 5 November, the Supreme Court sent Azam's petition to the Allahabad High Court and asked it to decide the matter of interim relief at the earliest. During the hearing, the High Court raised questions about the ED's arrest procedure. The bench of Justice Rajiv Gupta and Justice Devendra Singh said that the rules had not been followed when Azam was arrested at the prison gate. Azam was therefore ordered to be released on furnishing one personal bond and two sureties for the same amount. After coming out of jail, Azam said, "There will be a revolution, not an election" The Samajwadi Party leader was released from Dasna jail at 7 pm on Wednesday. As soon as he came out of the jail, he kissed his elder son Adeeb on the forehead. After reaching Rampur, Azam told the media, "There will be no election, but a revolution. There will be no change, but a surge." He said, "People will no longer fight in the name of religion or caste; the fight will instead be over issues. People like us were ready to die for the Constitution and the law, and we were, are and will remain ready. The ED officials should repair their image and reform themselves. They should neither ruin the country nor themselves." Taking a dig, Azam said, "If someone who gets chickens, buffaloes and goats stolen can be an ED accused and builds a university, then I pray that one such person is born in every street." "If the ED, CBI and IT had existed during the time of Madan Mohan Malaviya and Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, they too would have been in jail. I thank the judiciary. My belief has now grown stronger that the country is free, but the Constitution is imprisoned." His troubles may still increase in this case On 10 September, UP Vigilance registered a case against five people, including Azam, over irregularities in the sale of the State Haj Committee's land. The Vigilance investigation has confirmed that the land sale caused the committee a revenue loss of ₹2.08 crore in total. It is alleged that rules were ignored and the position was misused in the sale of the land to benefit a private firm. The government ordered an investigation into the matter on 3 May 2024. Azam has not yet been questioned in the case. Legal experts say Azam can be arrested in this case, but the Vigilance Department will need the government's permission to arrest a former minister, which it has not received yet. However, that possibility currently appears remote because the High Court has granted Azam bail. The ED's petition was also dismissed by the Supreme Court. Know the case in which the ED arrested Azam The ED's action is linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University and the Jauhar Trust associated with it. The agency is investigating the alleged misuse of funds and materials meant for government construction work, the purchase of land and the source of funds used to build the university. According to the ED, an investigation was launched on the basis of 26 FIRs registered at the Azeem Nagar police station in Rampur. The agency alleged that funds and construction materials linked to government contracts were used to build the university campus. The investigation valued the construction of 59 buildings and the land acquired through 114 sale deeds at ₹499.09 crore. According to the agency, only ₹72.63 crore could be accounted for through legitimate sources. The remaining ₹426.46 crore was described as alleged proceeds of crime. On this basis, the ED provisionally attached university land and buildings worth approximately ₹426.46 crore on 28 October.

stories.title: Akhilesh says, 'Don't welcome me with bulldozers':Child crushed to death by JCB in Gorakhpur, CM Yogi to visit family
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav asked party workers not to welcome him with bulldozers in future. On Wednesday, the 14-year-old son of a BJP leader died after being hit by a JCB during the PDA rath yatra in Gorakhpur. Akhilesh said- "I would ask my Samajwadi colleagues not to welcome anyone with bulldozers in future. We are not competing with anyone. The truth is that a bulldozer has no brain; it is driven by the driver." On Thursday, Chief Minister Yogi attacked the Samajwadi Party over the incident. He said, "An innocent child was made a victim at the Samajwadi Party's road show. He had come to study. After all, what was his fault? The Samajwadi Party's road show was a display of mafia rule and hooliganism." The Chief Minister warned that those creating chaos and indulging in mafia activity on the roads would be wiped out. Yogi will also meet the victim's family today. The accident occurred near Jharkhandi Mor at around 2:30 p.m. on Wednesday. Student Aryavardhan was walking towards the crossroads to pick up his sister when he was hit and injured by a JCB. He was taken to hospital, where he died. An FIR has been registered at the AIIMS police station against 66 people, including the JCB driver and the organiser. Akhilesh says politics is being played over the accident Akhilesh Yadav wrote on X, "We are all deeply hurt by the death of the innocent child in the accident. We express our deepest condolences to the bereaved family. We have already asked our people to meet the family and provide them with all possible assistance." Those politicising this unfortunate incident should remember how they mistreated and threatened the grieving mother of the young man who died in the Lucknow fire. The public has seen through the pretence of those putting on a show of mourning. Video released, questions raised over CM's allegations Releasing a video, Akhilesh Yadav wrote on X, "It is clearly visible that there was neither a roadshow nor a rally at the site of the incident. Despite this, the Chief Minister is blaming others for the accident." He said that politicising the matter was also an injustice to the bereaved family. He demanded a probe into the incident at the highest level. Yogi says: Innocent boy was made a victim at SP roadshow CM Yogi targeted the Samajwadi Party over the incident during a programme on Thursday. He said, "The SP held a roadshow yesterday. They made a minor boy a victim of their roadshow. He was killed. He had come to study. After all, what fault was there of that innocent 12-13-year-old?" The CM said that before 2017, forest mafias, mining mafias and cattle mafias were active in the state. If you want to see what the mafia looks like, you should look at the Samajwadi Party's roadshow yesterday. They made an innocent person their victim. See the height of their shamelessness: they remained silent. There was not even a single word of sympathy. Yogi said that just as a dog's tail can never be straightened, these goons and mafias can never mend their ways. They will only be brought into line through the use of force. He also directed the administration to take strict action against those spreading anarchy. Rajbhar said-You went and got yourselves disgraced; did you create mayhem on the roads? Cabinet minister and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party president Om Prakash Rajbhar targeted Akhilesh Yadav in a post on the social media platform X. He wrote, "My friend Akhilesh Yadav ji! Did you get yourself disgraced in Gorakhpur? Did you unleash mayhem on the roads? Amid this mayhem, your goons killed an innocent child in Gorakhpur." Rajbhar went on to write that a 13-year-old child had to lose his life because of his men who were jumping around on the road. "The bulldozer in your roadshow claimed Aryavardhan's life. It is true that not everyone can handle a bulldozer." He demanded a high-level inquiry into the matter and that those involved in the incident be charged with murder. Rajbhar also accused Akhilesh Yadav of not expressing grief or condolences after the incident. Sanjay Nishad enquired about the family's well-being over the phone Dr Sanjay Kumar Nishad, national president of the Nishad Party and a Cabinet Minister in Uttar Pradesh, also enquired about the victim's family over the phone. Expressing deep sorrow over the incident, he said, "The Nishad Party never engages in politics over dead bodies." Dr Sanjay directed the MLA to immediately meet the victim's family, offer condolences and provide all possible assistance. Now, here is how the accident happened... Student was hit by a JCB during a roadshow on Wednesday Aryavardhan, the son of BJP leader Omkar Singh, allegedly died after being hit by a JCB deployed to welcome Akhilesh Yadav during his PDA Rath Yatra in Gorakhpur on Wednesday. He was a Class 10 student at Kendriya Vidyalaya Nandanagar. His family said Aryavardhan was heading towards the crossroads at around 2:30 p.m. on Wednesday to pick up his sister. During this time, he was seriously injured after being hit by the JCB. He was taken to AIIMS, where doctors declared him dead. After the accident, his family members and BJP workers blocked the Gorakhpur-Deoria road at Jharkhandi Mor. The road remained blocked for around one and a half hours. The family had demanded action against the JCB driver and the organisers of the roadshow. On the basis of Omkar Singh's complaint, an FIR has been registered at the AIIMS police station against 66 people, including the JCB driver and Samajwadi Party leaders. Now learn about BJP leader Onkar Singh Onkar Singh is the district co-convenor of the BJP's Election Commission Liaison Department. He is originally from Rajdhani village in the Chauri Chaura area of Gorakhpur. His family currently lives in the Awas Vikas Colony in Jharkhandi. Onkar Singh's grandfather, Shiv Sampat Singh Shrineth, was also involved in politics. His family included his wife, Archana, daughter Samriddhi and two sons, Aryavardhan and Kirtiwardhan. His elder son, Aryavardhan, died in the accident on Wednesday. DM assures action DM Deepak Meena said that the family's demands had been taken seriously. Action would be taken in accordance with the rules. The concerned officials would also be given necessary instructions regarding the demand to install a speed breaker near Jharkhandi Gate. SSP Dr Kaustubh said that an FIR had been registered in connection with the accident. The roles of the JCB operator and the organiser are being investigated. Legal action will be taken against those found guilty based on the facts that emerge during the investigation.

stories.title: Posters projecting Raja Bhaiya as CM appear at Ram Katha:Dhirendra Shastri's Katha enters final day; Golden Baba arrives wearing 6 kg gold
stories.summary: The final day of Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri's Shri Ram Katha is being held today in Benti, Pratapgarh. Golden Baba has also arrived for the event. He is wearing around 6 kg 50 grams of gold jewellery. Hyderabad MLA T. Raja Singh also attended the event. He said, "In Hyderabad, Raja Bhaiya is called the gun-wielding Raja Bhaiya." Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Maurya, Finance Minister Suresh Khanna, MLA Aditi Singh and Rakesh Pratap Singh have also attended the event. So far, five helicopters have arrived at the Ram Katha today. Large numbers of people are gathering not only in Benti but also in the surrounding towns to listen to the Katha. A sound system has been installed in Manikpur town, around 15 kilometres from the venue. People are listening to the Katha there. A similar arrangement has been made in Kunda. A market with around 100 shops has been set up at the venue. Crowds of people are shopping at the stalls. Groups of young people were seen carrying posters and banners with political messages on the roads around the religious discourse tent. The posters called for Kunda MLA Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya, to be made Uttar Pradesh chief minister and Yogi to be made prime minister. On Friday, Bageshwar Dham's Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri will hold his divine court at Raja Bhaiya's Benti Palace.

stories.title: 2 lakh small fish released into Ganga:Initiative to increase Chitala population; river ranching programme held at Sant Ravidas Ghat
stories.summary: Two lakh fish found a new home in the Ganga on Thursday as part of a river ranching programme held at Sant Ravidas Ghat to protect the river's biodiversity and increase the declining fish population. During the programme, one lakh Rajyameen Chitala and one lakh Indian major carp fingerlings were released into the Ganga. Efforts to increase the Chitala population The main objective of the Fisheries Department's initiative is to promote the conservation and propagation of Chitala fish in the Ganga. According to department Deputy Director Suresh Kumar, efforts are being made through river ranching to increase the fish population in the river and strengthen the aquatic ecosystem. A larger fish population will strengthen the food chain The chitala fish is an important part of the Ganga's aquatic ecosystem. Its increasing numbers are expected to strengthen the river's natural food chain and biodiversity. The release of Indian major carp fingerlings will also boost fishery resources. This could benefit the livelihoods of fishermen and fish farmers in the future. The chital fish's unique appearance: a distinct identity shaped by its knife-like body The chitala fish is a highly attractive and distinctive freshwater fish. It is also known as the Indian knifefish or featherback. It has been granted the status of Uttar Pradesh's state fish. Its body is long, broad and flattened on both sides, giving it the appearance of a knife blade. A hump-like protrusion behind its head is its distinctive feature. Its silver colour and dark spots on the body enhance its beauty. Its lower and tail fins are connected, enabling it to swim in both forward and backward directions. It can grow up to four feet long.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan lifts former rival Ramdev in his arms:Baba stops him from touching his feet, hugs him; Raja Bhaiya looks surprised
stories.summary: Former MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and Baba Ramdev, once arch-rivals, appeared in a completely different manner. The occasion was a katha by Baba Bageshwar held at Raja Bhaiya's Raj Bhavan in Pratapgarh. The two warmly greeted each other. Brij Bhushan smiled as soon as he saw Ramdev and bent down to touch his feet. Baba Ramdev held his hand, helped him up and embraced him with a laugh. Meanwhile, Brij Bhushan held Ramdev by the waist and lifted him up. Raja Bhaiya, who was standing nearby, was taken aback by the sight. Saints and police officers present at the venue burst out laughing. The incident took place on 17 November, and its video emerged on Thursday (19 November). The four-year dispute between Brij Bhushan and Ramdev was resolved on 23 September this year. In fact, Acharya Balkrishna, president of Patanjali Yogpeeth, had sent Brij Bhushan a ₹50 crore defamation notice for calling Patanjali ghee fake. Brij Bhushan had said he was ready to go to jail but would not seek bail. See the pictures- Brij Bhushan returned to the stage and listened to the discourse alongside Ramdev Baba Ramdev reached Kunda after the Shri Ram Katha organised in Gonda. Meanwhile, he came face to face with Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, who was returning from the event. After their meeting, Brij Bhushan was about to leave for Gonda, but at Ramdev's request, he returned to the stage. The two then sat together and listened to the discourse. Now, here is what the dispute between the two was about 1. 2022: Dispute began after Patanjali ghee was called fake In November-December 2022, Brij Bhushan called Patanjali's desi ghee fake and advised people to keep cows and buffaloes at home. He also announced a campaign against adulteration. Acharya Balkrishna objected to this, sent him a legal notice and asked him to apologise. 2. 2025: Brij Bhushan questioned accountability after the sample failed On 27 November 2025, the Pithoragarh court imposed a fine of ₹1.40 lakh on the company and the sellers after a sample of Patanjali ghee failed in a 2020 case. Brij Bhushan questioned why a report that should have been issued within 2-4 hours came four years later, asking who would be held responsible for those who fell ill after consuming the ghee in the meantime. 3. September: Patanjali files ₹50 crore defamation case On 21 August, Brij Bhushan commented on Ramdev's Swadeshi movement, bringing the controversy back into the spotlight. Patanjali Foods filed a ₹50 crore defamation case against Brij Bhushan, accusing him of tarnishing the company's image. The case was heard in the Madhya Pradesh High Court on 15 September. Brij Bhushan said he was ready to go to prison if convicted but would not seek bail. 4. 23 September: Four-year-old dispute resolved after meeting Amid the legal battle, the two met on 23 September and ended the dispute. Ramdev said Brij Bhushan's misunderstandings had been cleared up and that he did not want to pursue the matter further. Brij Bhushan also said, "We have always respected saints and Sanatan, and we also respect the work you do for the country."

The candidates symbolically protested by sweeping outside the office and raised slogans. Police who arrived to remove the protesters forcibly picked them up and removed them from the site. See two pictures of the protest... Symbolic protest by sweeping the ground The candidates said the demonstration was organised under the "Dastak Do Abhiyan" and "Gorilla Gherao" campaigns. They said they had been fighting for a long time for their demand for appointments, but no one was listening to them. In protest, they tried to draw the government's and the party's attention by sweeping outside the RLD office. Demand to convey their concerns to the Centre through Jayant Chaudhary The protesters said that RLD chief Jayant Chaudhary is part of the central government. Therefore, he should convey the candidates' demands to the central government so that the issue of the recruitment of 68,500 teachers can be resolved. The candidates said they had already raised their demands with several political parties and leaders, but no solution had been found so far. Police forcibly removed them Police arrived at the site as the protest outside the office intensified. The police took action to remove the candidates. During this, the protesters were forcibly picked up and taken away. The candidates said their agitation would continue until their demand for appointment was met.
