stories.title: Mayawati-like protocol for Akash in Agra:Only one sofa on stage, other chairs placed behind; says SP loves only Etawah-Saifai
stories.summary: BSP chief Mayawati's nephew Akash Anand held a rally in Etmadpur, Agra, on Sunday. The stage arrangements appeared similar to those made for Mayawati. Only one sofa was placed on the stage for Akash, while the other chairs were arranged behind him. During the rally, Akash asked people not to fall for the opposition's attempts to mislead them through promises, pressure or division. He said, "A whole group of people will come to mislead you. Some will come from Gujarat, while others will come from monasteries. Some people love Saifai so much, but now they will leave Saifai and come to Agra." Akash said the BSP had waited for its turn to come to power for 70 years, but would not wait any longer. He added, "If we do not get the key to power, we will kick the door open and take power." SP's love affair with Etawah-Saifai Aakash said, "The BJP loves Ayodhya, the Samajwadi Party is in love with Etawah and Saifai, while the Bahujan Samaj Party is fond of Agra. Who could know better than Agra what love can create?" Both deputy CMs are beautiful showpieces Aakash said, "Just as people decorate their drawing rooms with beautiful showpieces, the government has kept both deputy chief ministers standing in a showcase. They are brought out for display when guests arrive and pushed to the forefront when elections approach." Shah Jahan had the Taj built, Behenji had the roads built Aakash claimed that Mayawati gave Agra an excellent road like an expressway. Shah Jahan had the Taj Mahal built, but Behenji had the good road to it built. He appealed to the people to make Mayawati chief minister for the fifth time. Raised the issue of closed factories and unemployment in Agra Akash Anand said that factories in Agra had shut down and shoe artisans were unemployed. The city's development stalled after the BSP government left office. Agra is still standing where it was 14 years ago. BJP and SP targeted over caste and religious politics He said that as elections approach, attempts are made to divide people along caste and religious lines. Inflation does not ask about religion when people buy a cooking gas cylinder, and unemployment does not look at the caste of someone seeking a job. Dalits, Thakurs, Muslims and Brahmins all face the same problems.

stories.summary: A private bus rammed a tempo from behind in Hathras, killing four people, including two sisters. The accident occurred at around 1 p.m. on Sunday. The tempo passengers were residents of the Nauserwala area in Aligarh district and members of the same family. They worked in Gurugram (Gurgaon) and were travelling from there to attend a wedding in Naurangabad, Sikandrarao. See the pictures : Police sent the bodies for post-mortem examination. The injured were also sent to hospital. The family was travelling to attend a wedding Haji Waris's daughter was getting married in Naurangabad, Sikandra Rao. The family members living in Gurgaon had first come to Hathras to attend the wedding. They were then travelling by tempo. During this journey, a private bus hit the tempo from behind. As soon as information about the accident was received, teams from the district administration, police, ambulance services and the health department reached the spot. The injured were sent to different hospitals. Some were taken to Akrabad CHC, while those with serious injuries were sent to Aligarh. The bodies of the deceased were sent to Hathras for post-mortem examinations. Bus driver fled; police examining CCTV footage The bus driver fled the spot after the accident. Police are searching for him. CCTV footage from the scene and surrounding areas is also being examined. Police are gathering information about the cause of the accident.

stories.title: Major reshuffle in UP Police, 144 Deputy SPs transferred:17 women officers among them; Pragya Pathak posted in Lucknow, Rupali Rao in Ghaziabad
stories.summary: Ahead of the elections in Uttar Pradesh, the police department has undergone a major reshuffle. The state government has transferred 144 Deputy Superintendent of Police (DySPs) and Assistant Commissioners of Police (ACPs). The list includes 17 women police officers. Most of the officers named in the list are those who were recently promoted from the rank of inspector. Lucknow Commissionerate: Sujeet Kumar Dubey from Mirzapur, Ramkaran from Bulandshahr, Amrish Kumar from Firozabad, Vivek Yadav from Prayagraj, Arvind Kumar-I from Unnao and Sameer Kumar Singh from Barabanki have been posted as Assistant Commissioners of Police (ACPs) in the Lucknow Commissionerate. Rajnish Verma, posted in the Lucknow Commissionerate, has been transferred to Baghpat; Radha Raman Singh to Kheri; Ratnesh Singh to the Security Headquarters in Lucknow; Shakeel Ahmad to the Agra Commissionerate; Pragya Pathak from the Varanasi Commissionerate; Anoop Kumar to Banda; and Ranjit Kumar to the STF Headquarters in Lucknow. Gautam Buddh Nagar and Ghaziabad Commissionerates: Praveen Kumar Singh from Hapur, Siddharth Gautam from the Ghaziabad Commissionerate, Shiv Narayan Vaishya from Pratapgarh and Anurag Kumar Singh from Gorakhpur have been appointed as new ACPs in the Gautam Buddh Nagar Commissionerate. Meanwhile, Omkar Dutt Tiwari from Gorakhpur and Imran Ahmad from the Agra Commissionerate have been transferred to the Ghaziabad Commissionerate. Kanpur Nagar, Varanasi, Prayagraj and Agra Commissionerates: Bhaskar Verma from Ghaziabad, Mahesh Kumar from Aligarh and Ziauddin Ahmad from Ghaziabad have been given new postings in the Kanpur Nagar Commissionerate. Sandeep Singh from Bareilly, Ravikant Parasar from Saharanpur and Pragya Pathak from Lucknow have been transferred to the Varanasi Commissionerate. Munendra Pal Singh from Mirzapur, Anoop Kumar Singh from Ambedkar Nagar and Vikant Dwivedi from Moradabad PAC have been appointed as ACPs in the Prayagraj Commissionerate. Other important changes and cancellation of transfers: Transfers cancelled: The previous transfers of two officers have been cancelled. The transfer of Dharmendra Singh Yadav, Assistant Commandant of the 35th Battalion PAC in Lucknow, to the Police Academy in Moradabad has been cancelled. The transfer of Deputy Superintendent of Police Sunita Dahiya from Bareilly has also been cancelled. Special branches and headquarters: Akhilesh Rajan, DSP in Banda, has been posted to the UP-112 Headquarters in Lucknow; Neelam Bisht, DSP in Baghpat, has been posted to the Women and Child Security Organisation in Lucknow; and Ritik Kapoor, DSP in Sultanpur, has been posted to the ACO Headquarters in Lucknow. stories.title: 'Your degree will open doors, but skills will define you':Rajnath urges youngsters to face challenges with confidence and avoid blindly following others
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh told graduates in Lucknow that a degree would give them their first opportunity to get a job. However, their identity thereafter would be shaped by their knowledge and skills. He said that if they had confidence, they would be able to face any challenge that came their way. “Do not become someone's follower. Move ahead,” he said. Rajnath Singh made these remarks on Sunday at the convocation ceremony of Babu Banarasi Das (BBD) University, where he attended as the chief guest. He awarded degrees and presented medals to meritorious students on stage. The ceremony began at 11.30 am at the Dr Akhilesh Das Gupta Stadium on the BBD University campus. stories.title: Akhilesh distributes laptops on Mulayam Singh Yadav's birth anniversary:Says, 'We are not against religious stories; BJP leaders make even Hanuman dance'
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party founder Mulayam Singh Yadav was paid tribute by the party's national president Akhilesh Yadav on his birth anniversary. On the occasion, he gave laptops and bags to 200 children. All the students are from Uttar Pradesh's Abhinav schools and had been brought to the SP headquarters in Lucknow from different districts. Speaking to the media, Akhilesh said, "BJP leaders are spreading false propaganda. The SP is not against the Ram Katha, but look at what Dhirendra Shastri said about the God worshipped by you and us... See this. BJP leaders made Hanuman dance at their programme; if we did the same, just imagine what would happen..." On the Uttar Pradesh elections, he said, "A campaign to corner us is under way in the Kairana seat in western Uttar Pradesh. Such attempts have been made before, but we will be the ones to win. The BJP is headed for defeat in this election all the way to Gorakhpur; it will have to save its so-called strongholds. You will see this in the election." He was speaking at a gathering held at the SP headquarters in Lucknow. MP Dimple Yadav and general secretary Shivpal Yadav were also present. ‘If voted to power, we will provide weavers with electricity at fixed rates’ Akhilesh further said, "If we come to power, we will provide electricity to our weaver brothers at fixed rates, because weavers create employment through their skill and craft. They are a strong link in our organisation." Farmers will be our priority. We will take Kannauj's perfume to new heights because it is a non-alcoholic perfume. The BJP has even ruined the perfume museum. What do they want... cow urine? That is what they like. On Mulayam's birth anniversary, Akhilesh says, 'He helped everyone…' Akhilesh Yadav said, "On Netaji's birth anniversary, I pay my profound respects to him. I reaffirm my resolve to implement his socialist principles and practical human values more firmly in every sphere of life. The simplest lesson we learnt from Netaji was to stand by someone in difficult times and to help anyone who came seeking 'help'." He further said, "A person may turn against someone for some reason or under pressure, but not everyone is always bad or ill-intentioned. Therefore, if someone sincerely and selflessly takes a step towards mending relations, one should not hesitate to extend a hand." Why Akhilesh had to say he was not against the religious discourse In fact, Dhirendra Shastri compared Lord Ram and Lord Krishna last month. He called Lord Krishna crooked. He then faced opposition. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav went so far as to say, "They hurt the sentiments of both the Yaduvanshis and the Raghuvanshis. They will be denied entry into both Braj and Awadh... Their programmes should also be cancelled." After this, Akhilesh Yadav targeted the Ram Katha by Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, the head of Bageshwar Dham, organised in Kunda by Raja Bhaiya, the chief of the Jansatta Dal (Loktantrik). He said, "Leaders who are unable to tell the public about their work are using religious discourses to garner public support." He also demanded that the administration ban such events. In response, Raja Bhaiya said, "Ram Katha can never be controversial," after which opponents began portraying Akhilesh as being opposed to the religious discourse.

stories.title: 8-month-old kidnapped from Delhi found in UP:Couple with three daughters abducted him in hope of having a male heir; three arrested
stories.summary: Police have recovered the eight-month-old baby abducted from Pandav Nagar in east Delhi from Wajidpur village in Uttar Pradesh's Aligarh district. Three people, including a couple, have been arrested in the case. According to police, the child's mother drives an e-rickshaw. She had gone to work, while the baby was in the care of a caregiver. During this time, a man fled with the child. A kidnapping case was registered at Mandawali police station following the mother's complaint. The investigation revealed that the accused couple already have three daughters. They wanted a son to carry forward the family name and inheritance. Police are now also investigating possible child-trafficking aspects of the case. Initial information obtained from caregiver's statement Police said that during questioning, the caregiver revealed that she had gone to buy some items from Ganesh Nagar at around 11:30 a.m. During this time, she met an unknown man, who later left with the child. Police then examined CCTV footage from the area and investigated the possible routes the accused may have taken to escape. The footage showed a man fleeing with the child. Questioning auto-rickshaw drivers led police to trace the accused's movements towards Akshardham. Police traced the mini-truck driver During the investigation, police identified the mini-truck driver, Rishipal (40), based on the vehicle's movements. He is a resident of Mathura and drives the truck. Technical surveillance and local intelligence revealed that the child had been handed over to a man named Chhatru in Wajidpur village, Aligarh district. According to police, Chhatru (50) is a farmer by profession. His wife, Kusma (45), is also an accused in the case. Both are residents of Wajidpur village, and Chhatru is a distant relative of Rishipal. They had planned to obtain the child a year earlier According to the police, Chhatru and Kusma had planned to have a son about a year ago. They have three daughters. They wanted a son both to carry on the family name and inheritance and to care for them in their old age. Following questioning and a search operation, the police team recovered the child from the village. All three accused were arrested within 24 hours of the abduction. According to the police, none of the accused had a previous criminal record. Investigation continues into child trafficking angle The police are now trying to determine who was involved in the entire process of abducting the child and handing him over to others. Further investigation is under way.

stories.title: Wife dies after jumping before train in front of husband:Mother alleges she was pushed onto the tracks in Kanpur
stories.summary: A 28-year-old woman died after allegedly jumping in front of a moving train in front of her husband in Kanpur on Sunday morning. She was hit by the train and her head was severed from her body. Her husband reportedly fled the spot after witnessing the incident and informed his mother-in-law about it some time later. The incident took place in the Kalyanpur police station area at around 10 am. The woman was identified as Simran. Her mother, who reached the spot, claimed that her daughter could not have died by suicide and raised suspicion of murder. Husband works as a project assistant at IIT Simran was married to Aman Kumar, a Kalyanpur resident who works as a project assistant at IIT. The couple had a four-year-old daughter, Anubha. According to local residents, the couple was arguing over an issue on Sunday morning. During the argument, they moved towards the railway tracks. Woman hit by passenger train travelling towards Kannauj Simran reportedly lay down on the railway track and was hit by a passenger train travelling from Kalyanpur towards Kannauj. The impact severed her head from her body. After receiving information about the incident, teams from the Government Railway Police (GRP) and Kalyanpur police station reached the spot.

stories.title: Train service to connect Ayodhya with Janakpur in Nepal:Check full schedule; PM Modi and Balen Shah to inaugurate it tomorrow
stories.summary: A direct train service is set to begin between Ayodhya, the city of Lord Ram, and Janakpur Dham in Nepal, the birthplace of Mata Sita. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepalese Prime Minister Balen Shah will virtually inaugurate the Janakpur Dham-Ayodhya Cantt Express (15595/15596) on Monday. The two prime ministers will flag off the train. Chief Minister Yogi and Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw will be present at the event venue in Ayodhya. According to the Railways, regular operations for passengers will begin on 28 November. The train will take around 19 hours to cover the distance of approximately 604 kilometres. It will be a weekly express train. It will depart from Janakpur Dham on Saturday afternoon and arrive in Ayodhya on Sunday morning. On its return journey, it will leave Ayodhya on Monday evening and reach Janakpur on Tuesday afternoon. The train fare has not yet been finalised. Find out when and where the train from Ayodhya to Janakpur will arrive... The train will depart from Ayodhya station every Monday at 5.50 p.m. and reach Janakpur railway station at 12.40 p.m. the following day, Tuesday. Schedule of the train from Janakpur to Ayodhya... The train will depart from Janakpur every Saturday at 1.10 p.m. and reach Ayodhya Cantt railway station at around 8.10 a.m. the following day, Sunday. Documents will be checked at Jayanagar station The train travelling from India to Nepal will cross the international border. Accordingly, passengers' identity cards and necessary documents will be checked at Jayanagar station in Bihar in accordance with security requirements and prescribed rules. As part of this process, the train has been given a long halt at Jayanagar station. It will stop for one hour while travelling from Janakpur to Ayodhya and for two hours while travelling from Ayodhya to Janakpur. Passengers will have to carry the necessary identity cards and documents during the journey. The train will not have a general coach; travel will be allowed only on confirmed tickets A total of 17 coaches will be attached to this special train. These will include 8 AC coaches and 7 sleeper coaches. The AC category will have 6 third AC coaches and 2 second AC coaches. Two coaches will be reserved for luggage, guards, pantry facilities and other purposes. The train will not have a first AC or general-class coach. According to railway rules, RAC and waitlisted tickets will not be available on this train. This means passengers will be able to travel only on confirmed tickets. In addition, no separate quota will be provided for senior citizens and passengers with disabilities. Separate reservation charts for passengers from India and Nepal Separate reservation charts will be printed for passengers travelling from India to Nepal and from Nepal to India. The charts will include passengers' identity card and nationality details. They will be made available to the relevant authorities for verification.

stories.title: Bride living with partner after leaving three husbands:Was preparing for her fourth wedding in Kanpur; broke down after being caught
stories.summary: A Kanpur bride who had married three times was living in a live-in relationship with a fourth man. She was preparing for her fourth marriage when her actions were exposed. The case is from the Barra police station area. Her third husband had accused the bride of fleeing with jewellery and cash worth ₹16 lakh. On Saturday, the police arrested six accused, including Pragati and five other members of her family, and sent them to jail. After the case was registered, the police traced her location and reached the address, where they found her with a man. During questioning, the man said she had been living with him for around four months. The two were preparing to get married soon. However, after her arrest, the young woman began sobbing uncontrollably. She said, "False facts have been presented against me. If I do not get justice, I will set myself on fire and die here." Here is the full story... Barra Inspector Kshitij Kumar Singh said that auto surveyor Vishal Vishwakarma, a resident of D-Block, Vishva Bank, in the city, married Pragati, a resident of Juhi Lal Colony, on 18 May 2025. The wedding took place at Karan Banquet Hall in Govind Nagar. Vishal alleged that around a month after the wedding, on 18 June 2025, Pragati left for her parental home with jewellery worth around ₹15 lakh and ₹1 lakh in cash. After an extensive search and investigation, Vishal learnt that Pragati had already been married twice. She had concealed this from Vishal. Pragati's first marriage took place on 20 March 2017 to Sonu Vishwakarma, a resident of Baradevi in Juhi. She then married Sumit Batham of Etawah on 23 June 2017. After her arrest, the police examined Pragati's mobile phone and found photographs of all three of her husbands. According to the police, she lured all three into her trap and married them. Pragati's mother demanded ₹20 lakh to hush up the case Vishal alleges that on 13 August 2026, he reached the house of Pragati's father, Ashok Kumar Vishwakarma, with his younger brother. He sought an explanation for concealing Pragati's previous marriages. The family members then assaulted him. Pragati's mother demanded ₹20 lakh to hush up the case. It is alleged that when he refused to pay the money, he was threatened with being framed in a false case. Following Vishal's complaint, the police registered a case. The investigation revealed that Pragati had left her third husband and was living in a live-in relationship with a fourth man. Young woman's family also supported her Police arrested Pragati, along with her adoptive father Ashok Vishwakarma, mother Seema, biological mother Somvati, who lives in Arra KDA Colony, and maternal aunt Komal and uncle Sharad Saini. Ashok and Seema are also Pragati's maternal uncle and aunt by relation. Her other maternal aunt Lalita and aunt-in-law Gomti Vishwakarma are still absconding. Police teams are conducting raids to find both of them. DCP South says-This is an entire gang DCP South Dipendra Nath Chaudhary said: This is an entire gang that used to trap innocent people. The victims were married to female members of the gang. After the wedding, they would flee with jewellery and cash. They would then extort money by threatening the victims with false criminal cases.

stories.title: US software engineer visits Varanasi after embracing Sanatan:Says it changed his life; chants Hanuman Chalisa 108 times at Assi Ghat
stories.summary: Alex Mom Silivik, who is from Chicago, USA, arrived in Varanasi. He performed the Ganga aarti at Assi Ghat and conducted the rituals according to tradition. He then sat at the ghat and recited the Hanuman Chalisa 108 times. Alex Mom Silivik said- I am a devotee of Hanumanji and Neem Karoli Baba. I recite the Hanuman Chalisa every day. It is a means of connecting with God, love and service. Reciting it opens the heart and gives one the strength to serve those in need. Alex said-Sanatan changed my life and gave me a new direction Alex arrived in Kashi three days ago. He is accompanied by seven friends. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar on Sunday, he said that he was a software engineer and had worked for a company in Chicago. He began taking drugs while working. He wanted to quit drugs but was unable to do so. About 10 years ago, he heard about Neem Karoli Baba. He came here and researched Neem Karoli Baba. He then began practising spiritual discipline. That was when he learned about Sanatan Dharma. He read spiritual literature and studied several religious books, including the Bhagavad Gita. After embracing Sanatan Dharma, his life found a new direction. His life underwent an extraordinary change. He gave up drugs. He felt a power within himself. He then accepted Neem Karoli Baba as his guru. He now practises yoga and meditation with his group. He also organises bhandaras in the name of Hanumanji and Neem Karoli Baba. Alex said: Shiva's spiritual energy attracts me Alex said that Varanasi is the city of light, which he likes immensely. The spiritual energy of Lord Shiva here attracts me. I keep travelling to different parts of India, but Varanasi holds a special place in my heart. The life of Goswami Tulsidas, Maha Shamshan Ghat, and the temples of Lord Shiva, Goddess Kali and Lord Hanuman connect me spiritually to this place. It is only through my guru's blessings that I keep returning to Kashi. Teaches yoga in America and helps people Alex says that he teaches yoga and meditation in America. Alongside writing books on spirituality, he also hosts podcasts. He helps people struggling with drug and alcohol addiction overcome it and move towards a better life. For him, spirituality does not mean only worship and religious rituals; it also means bringing positive change to people's lives through love, compassion and service. Priest said: Alex meditates on the banks of the Ganga Priest Deepak Kumar Pandey said that they have been coming here for quite some time. Earlier, they had organised a special puja here and donated to people in need. They all stay at a place on the banks of the Ganga in Banaras and meditate there. Today, they expressed their wish to worship Mother Ganga and perform the aarti, after which they recited the Hanuman Chalisa 108 times at the ghat itself.

stories.title: Body of girl found at neighbour woman's house in Bulandshahr:Sandalwood and vermilion marks on her, cloth stuffed in mouth; family suspects occult ritual
stories.summary: The body of a three-year-old girl was found in the home of a neighbouring woman in Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh. A cloth had been stuffed into her mouth, and sandalwood paste and vermilion had been applied to her body. The family alleges that the girl was strangled to death for occult rituals. The girl suddenly went missing at 11 a.m. on Saturday while playing outside her home. Her family searched for her but could not find her. They then informed the police. Acting on suspicion, the police searched the neighbouring woman's house and found the girl's body inside. The police detained the accused woman at the scene. Angered by the incident, the family and local residents blocked Delhi Road and staged a protest. Police and administrative officials who reached the spot assured them of action, following which the blockade was lifted. The incident took place in the Dehat Kotwali area, one kilometre from the district headquarters. See 3 pictures... Now read the full details of the case Sachin, a resident of the Bhud locality, drives an e-rickshaw. His three-year-old daughter, Manya, also known as Vania, suddenly went missing at around 11 a.m. on Saturday while playing outside their home. Her mother, Sharda, and other family members searched for her in nearby areas and at relatives' homes, but found no clues. The family then informed the police that the girl was missing. Police personnel also began searching for her in the surrounding area. At around 9 p.m. late that night, Manya's body was recovered from the house of a woman living in the neighbourhood during the search. The woman is reportedly involved in occult activities. As news of the girl's body being found spread, a large crowd gathered at the scene. The incident left the family distraught. Family creates commotion after blocking Delhi Road Angered by the incident, the family members and local residents blocked Delhi Road, demanding strict action against those responsible. They also raised slogans against the police administration. The blockade disrupted traffic on the main road, leading to long queues of vehicles. Following the report, the SSP and police personnel from several police stations reached the spot. The officials calmed the people by assuring them of an impartial investigation and strict action. According to the police, the accused woman is originally from Bisrakh. Her husband had already died. She also has an eight-year-old daughter, who was not at home at the time of the incident. The accused woman has repeatedly changed her statements during questioning. To mislead the police, she has given her name as Sonali at times and Ananya at others. The SSP said that during the preliminary investigation, the Aadhaar card recovered from the woman showed her name as Sonali. The police are also having her other documents examined. Only after this will her actual identity become clear. Local residents remain angry over the incident. Several people are still sitting by the roadside and trying to block the road. Police have begun removing those obstructing traffic. Barricades have also been put up at the spot to prevent the road from being blocked again and to maintain law and order. Woman in custody, body sent for post-mortem City SP Abhishek Pratap said all aspects of the murder were being investigated. The possibility of occult practices was also being examined. Further legal action will be taken on the basis of the post-mortem report and the facts that emerge during questioning.

stories.title: Probe ordered into guard of honour for Owaisi:Saharanpur SP (Rural) to investigate; negligent police personnel face action
stories.summary: Police in Saharanpur mistakenly gave AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi a guard of honour on Saturday while preparing to receive a Supreme Court judge. A guard of honour had been arranged for Supreme Court judge Manmohan Singh, who was scheduled to arrive at the Circuit House at 11 am. However, Owaisi reached the venue before him, and police personnel mistakenly presented the salute to the AIMIM chief. Probe handed over to SP Rural, action to follow City SP Vyom Bindal said the inquiry into the incident had been assigned to SP Rural Mayank Pathak. Further action will be taken after the investigation report is submitted. See two pictures... Police became confused as soon as Owaisi reached the Circuit House SSP Abhinandan Singh said a government programme attended by Supreme Court judge Manmohan Singh had been scheduled, and police had made arrangements to give him a guard of honour. However, officials learnt at the last moment that the judge had gone directly to the programme venue in Gagalheri. Owaisi arrived at Circuit House as judge proceeded to Gagalheri The SSP said the programme was related to the judiciary. Around the same time, MP Asaduddin Owaisi arrived at the Circuit House, where police personnel mistakenly gave him a guard of honour. Singh said an investigation was underway to establish who was responsible for the lapse. Now read: What is a 'guard of honour'? According to former Uttar Pradesh DGP Sulkhan Singh, a guard of honour involves a contingent of the police or armed forces conducting a ceremonial parade and showing respect with a salute. It is given in accordance with established protocols, rules and constitutional conventions. The police salute as part of the guard is entirely a departmental process. A person from outside the department is given a guard of honour only on the occasion of state functions. MPs and MLAs do not receive a guard of honour When an Armed Forces officer or employee dies, the body is given a funeral gun salute. If state honours are declared, the bodies of other dignitaries are also given a salute. However, MPs and MLAs cannot be given this kind of guard salute. Owaisi meets ADM over Saharanpur mosque demolition Owaisi and Nagina MP Chandrashekhar met ADM Lavi Tripathi over the demolition of a mosque in Saharanpur. They submitted a memorandum demanding a high-level inquiry into the mosque demolition. Demolition action was carried out on 5 September Both leaders said the dispute related to the mosque was pending before the court. Despite this, administrative officials demolished the mosque on 5 September. No clear stay order had been passed by the district judge's court. The administration acted in haste before the High Court could hear the case. Counterattack over Azam's remark on Hyderabadi biryani Owaisi said, "I am not the issue; the people of Uttar Pradesh are the issue. I have never been fond of eating. I lived outside India and earned my law and barrister's degrees. I had to endure great hardships. Some people now live only to eat; whatever I get is enough for me." "We were arranging food for people in the camps in Muzaffarnagar. At that time, a naked dance of lawlessness was taking place in Saifai. While people were sitting in their homes, we went to Akhlaq Saifi's house and met him." “Whose government was in power during the Muzaffarnagar incident? We went and met his elderly mother after Akhlaq Saifi's death. It is very good news that Azam Khan has been granted bail. He has turned 80; may Allah grant him good health, and may he take care of his health.”

stories.title: Alok Singh set to become UPPSC chairman:All 4 UP recruitment boards may come under IPS officers if appointment goes through
stories.summary: IPS officer Alok Singh may become the new chairman of the UPPSC. The government has agreed to his appointment. If this happens, all four recruitment boards in the state will come under the leadership of IPS officers. Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission chairman Sanjay Srineth retired on 21 November. With the election approaching, the government will want to complete the recruitments pending before the commission soon. Therefore, the chairman is to be appointed shortly. The Director General of the PAC and a 1995-batch IPS officer is a native of Aligarh. He also holds the charge of Director General of the Uttar Pradesh Special Police. He is due to retire in January 2027. As a result, he will serve as chairman for two years. At present, the Subordinate Services Selection Commission is headed by former DGP Satyanarayan Sabat, the Uttar Pradesh Education Services Selection Commission is headed by former DGP Prashant Kumar, and the Police Recruitment and Promotion Board is headed by DGP SB Shiradkar. Work progressed slowly during the IAS officers' tenure Alok Singh was Noida's first police commissioner Alok Singh was the first Police Commissioner of Noida (Gautam Buddh Nagar). He was appointed in January 2020. He has also served as ADG of the Kanpur Zone, IG of the Meerut Range, and SSP and IG of Kanpur. He has received several medals during his police service. Alok Singh has been awarded the Police Medal for Gallantry (PMG - 2003), Police Medal for Meritorious Service (PM - 2012), President's Police Medal for Distinguished Service (PPM - 2021), Medal for Outstanding Service (2020) and Medal for Extremely Outstanding Service (2026).

stories.title: Grooms wear garlands made of ₹1 crore in currency notes:100 feet long, gifted by their brother-in-law during wedding procession in Mathura
stories.summary: In Mathura, a brother-in-law put garlands made of currency notes worth ₹1 crore each around the necks of the two grooms during their wedding procession. The garlands, each around 100 feet long, required several people to hold them. The procession for Prashant and Kanha Raghav, the sons of Yogendra Singh and Kushalpal Singh of Nagla Fonda village, was being taken out on Saturday. The two are scheduled to marry women from Mudseras village at a marriage home in Govardhan. See two pictures... The young man is a marble businessman; his brother-in-law is a sarpanch Both young men are in the marble business, while their brother-in-law, Yogesh Kumar, also known as Bhura Thakur, is the sarpanch (village head) of Nandola village in Kaman, Rajasthan. Yogesh decided to give the brothers-in-law a memorable gift. He draped each of them in a garland worth ₹1 crore, made from new ₹500 notes. Several people worked to handle the 100-foot-long garlands Each garland was around 100 feet long. The garlands were so huge and heavy that several people had to work together to handle them. The garlands were placed around the two grooms while they stood on the roof. Relatives and villagers watched the scene in amazement. The horse-riding procession was captured on mobile phone cameras Usually, during the ghurchadhi ceremony, sisters ask their brothers-in-law for shagun, but here the brother-in-law made the ritual special by gifting his saalas a gift worth crores of rupees. Relatives and villagers captured the moment on their mobile phone cameras. Both grooms are the nephews of farmer leader Mahavir Swami.

stories.title: Fog blankets 24 UP districts, rain alert for Purvanchal:Cyclone ‘Akvan’ impacts weather; Hardoi coldest at 11°C
stories.summary: Weather conditions have changed across Uttar Pradesh due to Cyclonic Storm Akvan and snowfall in the mountains. Light drizzle was reported in Mirzapur and Varanasi late on Saturday (21 Nov) night. Meanwhile, dense fog covered 24 districts, including Prayagraj, Kaushambi and Pratapgarh, on Sunday morning. Visibility dropped sharply in several areas, making it difficult for motorists to see even 10 metres ahead. Rain and strong winds likely in four eastern UP districts The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast light rain accompanied by strong winds in four eastern Uttar Pradesh districts, Varanasi, Mirzapur, Sonbhadra and Chandauli on Sunday. Dense fog is also expected to persist across the Purvanchal region. The Uttar Pradesh Relief Commissioner has urged people to step out in the morning only for essential work. Residents have also been advised to take special care of elderly people and children. Day temperatures fall below 30°C across most districts Over the past 24 hours, mornings and nights have turned colder across the state. Except in Gorakhpur, daytime temperatures remained below 30°C in all districts, while the minimum night-time temperature was recorded at 11°C. Hardoi and Fatehpur were the coldest districts in the state. Temperatures to fall further from next week as wind direction changes Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said the cyclonic storm that developed over the Bay of Bengal has weakened. Northerly and north-westerly winds have now started gaining strength, replacing the easterly winds. As a result, night-time temperatures in western Uttar Pradesh will gradually decline. Fog may also develop in some areas during the morning. Cold to intensify from next week, but severe winter still some distance away Singh said temperatures are expected to fall further from next week, bringing colder conditions across the region. However, people will have to wait longer for severe winter to set in. Earlier, police had arrested Kunwar Suryadev Singh alias Shiva, a resident of Kharrela in Mahoba. Raids are under way to trace the two remaining accused. Four men opened fire after argument with shopkeeper The incident took place on Monday when all four accused arrived at the tea stall in Gomtinagar in a Scorpio. They allegedly abused the shopkeeper, prompting two friends present at the spot to object. The four men then opened fire several times. Here's the full story... Four men arrive at tea stall in Scorpio-N, abuse staff Upendra Singh, a native of Ballia, works in the construction sector in Lucknow. His friend Prashant Singh said that around 5 pm on Monday, Upendra and another friend, Amit Singh, visited Man Singh Yadav's tea stall near Greenwood Apartment in Sector 1 of Gomtinagar. After having tea, the two men were preparing to pay the bill when four men arrived in a Scorpio-N and demanded tea while hurling abuses. Upendra and Amit objected to their language and said they would place their order only after paying their own bill. Accused open fire after friends object to abusive language The accused then began abusing Upendra and Amit as well. When the two men objected, one of the accused took a pistol from the vehicle and opened fire. During the incident, the pistol fell to the ground. The accused then took out another pistol from the vehicle and fired several rounds. The firing caused panic in the area, but Upendra and Amit escaped unhurt. The police were informed and registered a case. They had been searching for the accused since the incident, with one of them arrested two days ago. Injured Shekhar seen shouting in video before arrest Lucknow Police arrested Shekhar Kaushal on Saturday. A video recorded before his arrest has surfaced, showing an injury to his hand as he shouts while speaking. The video of the accused has emerged, and police are verifying the facts related to it.

stories.title: Is Sanjay Nishad planning a major move?:Akhilesh first, then CM Yogi comment on him, sparking speculation
stories.summary: Nishad Party national president Dr Sanjay Nishad has recently been seen sharing a close rapport with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. However, his recent political moves have triggered speculation in Uttar Pradesh. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, during his visit to Gorakhpur, made remarks that appeared to hint at Nishad's political plans. The very next day, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also took an indirect swipe at him. Remarks by Akhilesh and Yogi fuel speculation over political switch Both leaders' comments revolved around the possibility of a political shift. Their remarks have triggered fresh discussions in Gorakhpur's political circles, with speculation over whether Dr Sanjay Nishad is planning a major move ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. There is also talk about whether the two leaders have received some indication of his intentions. Akhilesh Yadav visited Gorakhpur on 18 November for a day-long programme and addressed journalists on two occasions. Both times, he made indirect references to Dr Sanjay Nishad. He indicated that the existing INDIA alliance could expand at the last moment, suggesting that another political party might join it. Akhilesh also referred to a demand for 36 seats and alleged that the BJP was trying to persuade one of his allies. These remarks, too, have been linked to the Nishad Party and have added to speculation about its possible political alignment ahead of the 2027 elections. On 18 November, the Nishad Party organised a major protest in Farenda, in Maharajganj district, demanding reservation for the Nishad community. Protesters raised slogans against the government and blocked the road. When Akhilesh Yadav was asked about the demonstration, he said the Nishad Party had not taken to the streets and that the protesters were from another group supporting the party. He was referring to the Samajwadi Party's roadshow. Akhilesh also stressed that the two parties were allies and would continue to remain so. He said they were supporting one party today and would extend support to another tomorrow. Yogi takes indirect dig at Sanjay Nishad during university event On the afternoon of 19 November, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath attended the foundation stone-laying ceremony of a forestry university in the Campierganj Assembly constituency. During the event, he made two remarks about Sanjay Nishad. In his first comment, Yogi claimed that he had saved Sanjay Nishad's life in 2016. His second remark carried a political message. He said he had told Sanjay Nishad that the problem could be resolved if they stayed on the same path. The Chief Minister added that Sanjay Nishad was an experienced leader who understood that one should travel in the same boat rather than try to board two boats at once. Sanjay Nishad was also present on the stage and continued smiling as Yogi made the remark. Senior journalist DBB Mishra believes Dr Sanjay Nishad is using different tactics to put pressure on political allies as the 2027 Assembly elections approach. He said Nishad could be exploring alternative political options ahead of the polls, a possibility that Akhilesh Yadav appeared to hint at. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also made a remark about switching sides the following day. Seat-sharing dispute adds to political speculation Mishra said Yogi's comment could also have been a reference to the Nishad Party's recent protest. A day before the Chief Minister's remarks, the party had blocked a road in the adjoining Farenda Assembly constituency, where the foundation stone-laying ceremony for the Forestry University was being held. According to Mishra, the remarks made by Akhilesh and Yogi could be interpreted in only one way. Political circles are abuzz with speculation that the Nishad Party is facing disagreements with both the BJP and the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) over seat-sharing arrangements. In this backdrop, Mishra said, the possibility of the Nishad Party taking an unexpected political step cannot be ruled out. Sanjay Nishad's presence at tribute event draws attention Dr Sanjay Nishad attended a tribute programme for late Jamuna Nishad on 19 November. Jamuna Nishad is regarded as a prominent leader of the Nishad community, whose political support Sanjay Nishad seeks to represent. Political analysts point out that Sanjay could have organised a death anniversary programme at his own office if his intention was simply to pay tribute. Instead, he attended the event organised by Jamuna Nishad's son, Amarendra Nishad, a Samajwadi Party leader. Amarendra represents the Nishad community's political interests on behalf of the SP in an Assembly constituency. Sanjay Nishad's decision to attend a programme organised by a leader from a rival party has therefore attracted attention amid the ongoing political speculation.

stories.title: Bageshwar Baba's kathas increase in UP after Akhilesh's protest:Five lined up in 20 days, compared with two in 18 months; will Thakur influence backfire
stories.summary: Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya, organised a Ram Katha in Kunda, Pratapgarh. Leaders from the Thakur community and influential political figures from eastern Uttar Pradesh shared the stage. Raja Bhaiya was projected as a face of Hindutva. The message was that Thakur leaders in UP had united under his leadership. The gathering of around 5 lakh people over the three-day event surprised everyone. The UP Assembly election is due to be announced in two months. Before that, 12 such religious discourses are scheduled to take place. Five of these will be held by Dhirendra Shastri, the head of Bageshwar Dham. This means he will be seen in different districts of UP for 20 of the next 40 days. It is well known that his discourses often feature strong views on Sanatan Dharma and Hindutva. There are now two kinds of discussions around these events. One view is that they are an attempt to shift election issues towards Hindutva and Sanatan Dharma. Another section believes that the prominence of one community at these events could backfire. What is the truth? We explain it in today's Sunday Big Story... Kunda in UP is identified with Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya. However, the Ram Katha in Kunda suddenly made headlines across the country. Even more widely discussed was the show of organisational strength by Raja Bhaiya in arranging the event. The reason was that Dhirendra Shastri had compared Lord Ram and Lord Krishna last month, following which he faced opposition. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav went so far as to say, "He has hurt the sentiments of both the Yaduvanshis and the Raghuvanshis. He will not be allowed to enter either Braj or Awadh... His programmes should also be cancelled." The opposition to Dhirendra Shastri was seen as opposition to Sanatan Dharma. As a result, when the head of Bageshwar Dham, Dhirendra Shastri, delivered the Ram Katha from 17 to 19 November, lakhs of people attended every day. The tent, spread over 56,000 square feet, was packed with people, while twice as many were seated outside. The Katha was scheduled to take place from 2 pm to 6 pm every day, but it did not last the full four hours on any of the three days. This was because several prominent leaders from UP and other states kept arriving as guests. They were also given an opportunity to speak from the stage. Notably, more than half of the leaders who attended the Katha belonged to the Thakur community. From the stage, Raja Bhaiya was described as a prominent face of Sanatan Dharma and Hindutva. His supporters also projected him as the Chief Minister of UP and Yogi Adityanath as the Prime Minister, putting up banners to this effect. Dhirendra Shastri to hold Kathas in UP for 20 days next month Before delivering the Ram Katha in Kunda, Bageshwar Dham head Dhirendra Shastri had held only two such events in UP. The first was in Gorakhpur in 2024 and the second in Meerut in March 2025. This means he had not held a Katha in UP for the past one-and-a-half years. Now, five such events are suddenly scheduled to take place across the state. These will be completed over around 20 days. The first Katha will be held in Gonda from 3 to 6 December, organised by BJP MLA Bawan Singh. In Jhansi, BJP MLA Ravi Sharma will organise a Katha from 11 to 13 December. Another event is proposed in Mathura from 15 to 19 December, organised by a local saint. BJP MLA Dr Rajeshwar Singh will organise a Katha in Lucknow from 21 to 25 December. Another Katha is scheduled to take place in Agra from 27 to 29 December. These dates have been uploaded on the website of Bageshwar Dham Sarkar. This means Dhirendra Shastri's Kathas will be held across western UP, Awadh, Bundelkhand and Purvanchal. Attempt to shift election discourse towards Hindutva through Kathas Senior Lucknow-based journalist Rajkumar Singh says, "The BJP has always created a religious atmosphere just before elections. It has also benefited from this. Earlier, it used to talk about the Ram temple. Now that its construction has been completed, it is talking about building a Krishna temple. Kathas are the best medium to take this issue to people in every village. The way Hindutva, Sanatan Dharma and the party's ideology are being discussed from the Katha stage makes it clear that the purpose of these events is to gain electoral benefits. However, it is difficult to say at this stage whether the people attending these events will vote for the party." Rajkumar Singh adds, "There is also a possibility that these events could cause damage. During the Ram Katha in Kunda, statements such as 'our dominance will continue' were made from the stage, accompanied by people raising their hands. Leaders from one caste were seen more prominently on the stages. This can create negative feelings among people from other castes sitting in the audience." On the back foot over Ram temple donation theft, BJP turns to the Krishna issue Another senior Lucknow-based journalist, Alok Pathak, says, "The BJP gives prominence to religious issues during elections. Following the case involving the theft of donations at the Ram temple, that issue can no longer be used, so the Krishna temple is being brought into focus. There is a lot of talk about building a Krishna temple during these Kathas. However, the Krishna temple issue may not gain traction because it does not have the same connection with the public as the Ram temple. These events may benefit Hindutva, but it seems less likely that any particular party will benefit from them." Alok says, "Another thing that is becoming apparent is that this is Team Yogi, which is using these Kathas to demonstrate its strength. Messages are also being sent through these events to those within the BJP who want to see Yogi removed."

stories.title: Man's head severed in rotavator accident:Body mangled as he tried to climb onto tractor while ploughing field in Lucknow
stories.summary: A 20-year-old man died after getting caught in a rotavator in Lucknow. He was climbing onto a tractor while the field was being ploughed when he came under the rotavator. In the accident, Luvkush's head was half severed and his body was mutilated. He had gone with his cousin to a villager's field, taking the tractor. The police took the body into custody. The incident took place in the Sarojininagar area on Saturday evening. Read the full report He had gone ploughing with his uncle Ramvilas, a resident of Meeranpur Pinvat, lives with his family. He works in farming. His family comprises his wife, Archana, sons Luvkush and Kaushal, and daughter Maya. Luvkush used to drive a tractor. On Saturday evening, he was ploughing the field of Manohar Lal, a fellow villager, with his uncle Kundan, 24, son of Jamuna Prasad. Kundan was driving the tractor, while Luvkush was in the field. During this, he began climbing onto the tractor from the rear. He came under the rotavator after slipping As Luvkush was climbing onto the tractor, his foot suddenly slipped and he fell directly under the rotavator. Before Kundan could understand what had happened and stop the tractor, Luvkush was caught in the rotavator and died on the spot. Family members broke down after seeing the body Half of Luvkush's head was severed, and his body was mutilated. After the incident, Kundan abandoned the tractor and fled the scene. As soon as the family members learnt about the accident, they reached the field. They broke down after seeing Luvkush's mutilated body there. The family members were inconsolable. Police reached the scene after being informed, inspected the site and took the body into custody before initiating the process of sending it for a post-mortem examination.

stories.title: Raja Bhaiya's wife speaks out over distance from family:'I am his wife'; says she and daughters were not allowed home during Ram Katha
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh strongman MLA Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya, was the subject of an emotional Facebook post by his wife, Bhanvi Singh, in which she expressed her pain over family relationships. She said she had wished to sit with Raja Bhaiya and perform prayers during the auspicious occasion of the Ram Katha, with the entire family taking part in the religious ceremony. But that did not happen. Bhanvi Singh wrote, "The same woman because of whom I was thrown out of my own home so many years ago is the reason why, even on a sacred occasion such as the Ram Katha, my two daughters and I were not allowed to return to our home. It is difficult to express this pain in words." Peethadhishwar of Bageshwar Dham, Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, held the Shri Ram Katha at Benti Raj Bhavan in Kunda, Pratapgarh, from 17 to 20 November. Bhanvi Singh had expressed her wish to attend it, but she was not invited to the Katha. 'Could not return home even on such a sacred occasion' Bhanvi Singh began her post by expressing gratitude to the person who had shared an emotional song along with a photograph of her and Huzoor. She wrote, "The affection and sense of belonging you expressed by adding such an emotional song to the photograph of Huzoor and me truly touched my heart. I am sincerely grateful for your selfless love and respect." She then mentioned her desire to attend the Ram Katha. Bhanvi wrote that she wanted to sit with Raja Bhaiya and offer prayers at the sacred Ram Katha, and for her entire family to be part of the religious event together. But that did not happen. In her post, she wrote, "Unfortunately, because of the same woman who led to my being thrown out of my own home several years ago, my two daughters and I were not allowed to return to our home even on an auspicious occasion as sacred as the Ram Katha today. It is difficult to express this pain in words." 'I am his wife; I do not accept this distance between us' Bhanvi Singh also spoke about her marital relationship with Raja Bhaiya. She made it clear that she is Raja Bhaiya's wife and, as his wife, does not accept any distance between them. Referring to her religious beliefs regarding marriage, she wrote that in Sanatan Dharma and its traditions, marriage is not merely a social bond but a sacred vow spanning seven lifetimes. Divorce has never been part of her religious beliefs. Through this statement, Bhanvi has expressed her perspective on her marital relationship. She also indicated that she still considers the relationship equally sacred and wants the family to be united again. Describes people's love as a blessing In her post, Bhanvi Singh also mentioned the people who have been writing messages in her support on social media. She said she was deeply moved by reading their beautiful, affectionate and emotional comments. She wrote, "The affection and love with which everyone is wishing for me to return to my own home and family is no less than a blessing for me." According to Bhanvi, this affection and sense of belonging from people mean a great deal to her. She thanked everyone who had expressed respect and sympathy towards her. Prayed for love and unity in the family again At the end of her post, Bhanvi Singh prayed to God that one day truth, righteousness and the sanctity of relationships would prevail. She prayed that love, peace and unity would be restored in her family. While her post reflects her unfulfilled desire to attend the Ram Katha and the pain of staying away from her family, it also reveals her unwavering faith in her marital relationship with Raja Bhaiya. Through her words, Bhanvi has conveyed that she hopes the family will live together again and that unity will return to their relationships.

stories.title: Sub-Inspector dies in Lalitpur hours after messaging daughter:‘Inspector could stage my encounter or poison my food’
stories.summary: A 52-year-old RPF sub-inspector died in Lalitpur. At around 3 a.m. on Saturday, fellow employees took him to the medical college, where doctors declared him dead. His daughter reached the medical college after being informed of her father's death. She accused officers from the department of harassing him. The daughter said her father had sent a WhatsApp message at night, accusing his senior inspector of either having him killed in an encounter or mixing poison into his food. Joined the RPF in 2019 after retiring from the Air Force Rakesh Kumar Sinha lived at H-46, Lane Number 2, Raj Nagar, Palam Colony, New Delhi. He was the fifth of four brothers and two sisters. He has two daughters, who live in Delhi. Rakesh's wife died four years ago. Rakesh Sinha had retired from the Air Force. In 2019, he was appointed as a sub-inspector in the RPF. Around four months ago, he was transferred from Jhansi to Lalitpur. Sent message to daughter, levelled allegations against inspector Following her father's death, Rakesh's daughter Shikha arrived in Lalitpur on Saturday afternoon. Shikha said, "At around 9 p.m. on Friday, my father sent me a message on WhatsApp. He wrote, 'Look at the result of honesty. A passenger complained about the woman who was asking for money. The inspector could not do anything in the matter and became angry.'" "The inspector magnifies minor mistakes and threatens to take action against me. He could have me killed in an encounter or even poison my food." Shikha said her father had mentioned departmental stress in the message. He used to say the station was a hub of bribery Rakesh's brother-in-law, Anand Sinha, said he was very honest. He would often say that Lalitpur station was a hub of bribery. He did not like the atmosphere there. He wanted nothing to do with bribery. According to Anand, people from the department would tell him to get along with others. Rakesh feared that if he did not agree with them, he would be mistreated. RPF station house officer Arjun Diwasar refused to comment on the matter. However, the cause of his death will become clear only after the post-mortem report is released.

stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri says, ‘I bow to the people of Braj’:I have come to the city of my beloved Banke Bihari Thakurji
stories.summary: After his remarks on Lord Krishna, Bageshwar Dham Peethadhishwar Dhirendra Krishna Shastri arrived in Mathura for the first time on Saturday. Laughing, Dhirendra Shastri said, "We have come to the city of our beloved crooked and twisted Thakur Ji... Banke Bihari Ji. We bow down by rubbing our noses at the feet of all the people of Braj." Dhirendra Shastri said, "A person's stature becomes great only when, as a Sanatani, they put service first. There are also some people who call themselves Sanatanis but are not truly so. Stay away from such seasonal frogs." Today, we came to Banke Bihari for two or three reasons. First, it was Babuji's birth anniversary; second, the daughters' weddings at Gauri Gopal; and third, we wanted to have darshan of Banke Bihari Ji. Because, at present, he was the most viral and trending. After having darshan of Banke Bihari, Dhirendra Shastri led the chants: "Victory to crooked Thakur Ji... Victory to Hanuman Ji with the crooked leg... Victory to Thakur Ji with the crooked leg... As long as we live, we will continue to pamper our beloved Thakur Ji in this way." 'You have opposed Baba Bageshwar-when will you come to Mathura now?' Dhirendra Shastri targeted those trolling him on social media. He said, "You have opposed Baba Bageshwar and posted extensively against him. When will you take to the field for Banke Bihari now? When will you come to Mathura-Vrindavan? When will you step forward to erase the stain on Mathura? In the coming days, we will also reside in Braj. Some people had become devotees of Krishna for a few days, but they are no longer visible." Dhirendra Shastri said that they were going to seek the blessings of Shri Banke Bihari Ji. "We belong to Bihari Ji. We sing of his grace and undertake padyatras for him. After having darshan of Banke Bihari, we will pray for the good sense of those who troll us. May God ensure that those who have become Krishna devotees on social media for a few days become true devotees and work for Hindus." Will not allow Hindus to divide or be wiped out Dhirendra Shastri said, "We live for Hindus and will continue to live for Hindus. We will continue to work for Hindutva and Hindustan. We will not let Hindus be divided, nor will we let Hindus be wiped out. We will ensure Hindu unity." When the media asked Dhirendra Shastri whether opposition leaders were alleging that he was campaigning for the BJP in the 2027 Assembly elections, he said, "We are saints and have nothing to do with politics." He said, "We are not campaigning for anyone; we are campaigning for Lord Hanuman. We are promoting Sanatan and spreading the idea of Hindutva. There are Hindus in all the political parties in this country, which means we are campaigning for all the parties." We will not stop working for Hindu unity even if we have to endure abuse and face bullets Dhirendra Shastri said, "Our resolve is simple: if Hindus do not survive, how will India survive? If Hindus do not unite, if Sanatanis do not unite, how will our temples, shrines and pilgrimage sites survive? Hindu unity means bidding caste divisions farewell: we are all Hindu brothers. Those who work against this will naturally need some excuse or another to troll us. I pray to Lord Banke Bihari that he grants all of them wisdom." "We have endured abuses so far, and even if we have to face bullets, we will not abandon the work of Hindu unity. As long as there is life in this body, it is dedicated to the nation and Sanatan." After offering prayers at Banke Bihari, he said - Now turn Sanatan's chariot towards Mathura After offering prayers at Banke Bihari, Dhirendra Shastri said, "We keep coming to Thakur Ji's temple. We prayed to Thakur Ji. Now we say that those who trolled us should come to Bihariji like us. They should join us in addressing the stain left by Aurangzeb in Krishna Janmabhoomi, Mathura. Let all of us, and all Sanatani residents of Braj, work together to find a way to erase that stain. Now turn Sanatan's chariot towards Mathura, otherwise you are not Sanatani but Tanatani." Know which statement by Dhirendra Shastri sparked controversy Shastri had said, "Your Thakurji is bent at three places" Dhirendra Krishna's remarks about Lord Krishna sparked controversy. Comparing Lord Ram with Lord Krishna, he said: "Just look at a single photograph of your Thakurji. Even when he stands, he is bent at three places. One foot over the other, sometimes with his waist bent, and playing the flute with his neck tilted. Our Lord stands completely straight. Even his name is straight. The way he walks is straight, and he looks straight as well. Your Lord's name is also bent, he walks bent and even stands bent. Lifting a mountain is not a big deal. A disciple of our Lord lifted an entire mountain and carried it away. The abode of our Lord also has a straight name-Ayodhya, while your Lord's is-Vrindavan!" Shastri said, "Many people misinterpreted what I said" However, as the controversy grew, Dhirendra Shastri released a video clarifying his remarks. He said, "Many people misunderstood what I said. We ourselves are devotees of Thakurji and Braj. Whenever we pray to Thakurji, we say that we should be granted a place to live in Braj." "We also recite the Shrimad Bhagwat Katha and sing the praises of Thakurji. We had no intention of distinguishing between Lord Ram and Lord Krishna." In fact, Dhirendra Shastri had commented on Lord Krishna during the Shri Ram Katha being held in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh. After a video of the remarks emerged on 10 October (Sunday), the sadhus and saints of Mathura expressed their displeasure. They had asked Dhirendra Shastri to apologise.

stories.title: Bride calls off wedding after garland exchange:Firozabad woman accuses groom of spending 30 minutes with another woman in his room
stories.summary: The bride refused to go ahead with the marriage after the jaimala ceremony in Firozabad, alleging that the groom had called another woman into his room and spent around half an hour with her. Argument breaks out at marriage hall The allegation triggered a heated argument and a commotion between the two families at the marriage hall. Later, the bride, dressed in a red bridal outfit with mehndi on her hands, reached the police station and demanded action against the groom. The groom, however, denied the allegations. The incident took place in the jurisdiction of the Uttar police station. Aakash, 26, and Kajal, 24, were scheduled to get married at Gopal Marriage Home on the night of 20 November. The jaimala ceremony had already taken place when the incident occurred. The bride and groom were in a room when Aakash called another woman inside and asked Kajal to leave. According to Kajal, the groom then remained in the room with the woman for around half an hour. She and her family members objected to his behaviour, triggering an argument between the two families. As the dispute escalated, Kajal refused to go ahead with the wedding. Bride reaches police station in bridal outfit, refuses to marry Kajal later reached the police station wearing her red bridal outfit, with mehndi on her hands. She told the police, "I am from Etah district. My parents had come to Firozabad for the wedding." She said Aakash was a resident of Dwarakapuri, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Uttar police station, and that was why the wedding was being held there. However, after the jaimala ceremony, she decided to call off the marriage over his behaviour. "I no longer want to marry Aakash. Strict action should be taken against the groom. What happened to me should not happen to another girl," Kajal said. Groom denies allegations, says woman was his friend's sister After the bride, Aakash also reached the police station wearing a turban and sherwani. He denied the allegations and claimed that he had done nothing wrong. "The woman who came to meet me was my friend's sister. She works in Gurugram and lives in Kasganj," Aakash said. He added that she had attended the wedding and had come to inform him that she was leaving. "I had not closed the door or asked the bride to leave the room. The cameraman had asked her to step out," he said. Wedding guest says woman was left inside room, door locked Seema Rathore, who attended the wedding, said everything was normal initially and the photography was under way when the groom asked the bride to leave the room. "After this, two boys left a girl inside the room and went away. The door was then locked from the inside and remained shut for a long time. However, I do not know what happened inside the room," Seema said. Police call both families to station, try to resolve dispute After receiving information about the disturbance, the police called both sides to the North police station. Station House Officer Ravi Tyagi spoke to the families and tried to resolve the matter. For now, the bride remains firm on her decision not to marry, while the groom has dismissed the allegations against him as false.

stories.title: Police drag groom away by his collar from wedding pavilion:He was marrying for the second time, wife caught him with the bride
stories.summary: In Etah, police grabbed the groom by the collar and dragged him away from the wedding pavilion. He was marrying for the second time without a divorce. His first wife, who arrived with the police, stopped the wedding. The first wife alleged that their divorce case had been pending in court for three years. The groom was marrying again to receive the ₹1 lakh available under the Chief Minister's Mass Marriage Scheme. The incident took place at around 1:30 on Saturday during a Chief Minister's Mass Marriage Scheme ceremony. See two pictures... Husband seen with bride in wedding pavilion Akash (28) lives with his family in Meera Sarai village under Marhara police station. He works as a painter. The family includes two sisters, Khushbu (24) and Khushi (22), and three brothers, Vikas (26), Praveen (18) and Manjeet (14). Akash married Soni (27), from Chaman Nagariya village under Aliganj police station, on 14 November 2021. His wife alleges that Akash often assaulted her after their marriage. A divorce case between the two has been pending in court for about three years. Soni said, "My friend was due to get married at the Chief Minister's mass marriage ceremony. I had come to attend it. I saw Akash sitting with the bride in the wedding pavilion. His family members had also arrived." Police pulled him away from the wedding pavilion and took him to the police station Soni said, "I immediately informed the police. My divorce case is pending in court. Aakash is getting married again without the divorce being finalised. The police arrived, stopped the wedding, grabbed him by the collar and dragged him to the police station." Husband demanded a Bullet motorcycle Soni said, "Aakash assaulted me and drove me out of the house. He demands dowry. He wants a Bullet motorcycle. He says he will not keep me with him until he gets the vehicle. He also threatens to kill me." Kotwali in-charge Dharmendra Pawar said: This is a case involving a man who was already married getting married for the second time at a mass wedding ceremony. The accused has been taken into custody.

stories.title: 'Don't spare the Vice-Chancellor':Farmer dies by suicide, accuses Gorakhpur University VC of taking over his land
stories.summary: A farmer in Bareilly took his own life after consuming poison. Before his death, he wrote a three-page suicide note accusing Professor K.P. Singh, vice-chancellor of Deen Dayal Upadhyaya University (DDU) in Gorakhpur, of fraudulently taking over his land. The suicide note names four people-Ankit, Arun Kumar, Ratan and Srivastava-and includes their mobile numbers. The farmer wrote, "These five or six people have ruined my life." In the suicide note, the farmer told his sons: "These people are responsible for my death. They have looted lakhs of rupees from me. Tell the police and do not let them go. The vice-chancellor of Bareilly University is behind my death; he had the deed for our land registered through fraud. The Baheri CO calls us and threatens to have the land seized. Please do not spare any of them." In the suicide note, the farmer wrote: "This was all the time I had with you. Who wants to die? If I had told you, everyone would have said the next day that I was mad. We bought the land; we did not encroach on it." He concluded: "Ankit is the most guilty of all." See 3 pictures... Now read the full incident in sequence... Sardar Bhagwan Singh, who lived in Pachpeda village in Bahedi, was 55 years old. His father had moved here from Punjab and settled in 1992. Bhagwan Singh has two sons and two daughters. One son, Bhajan Singh, lives in New Zealand and works in the hospitality sector. His other son, Bhag Singh, is a lawyer at the Bahedi court. His wife is Gurdeep Kaur. According to his son Bhag Singh, they bought the land from Gurnam Singh and others in 1995 through registered sale deeds. There was a dispute over around 12 acres of the total 24 acres of land under plot number 519. The family had built a house on this land and lived there. They also farmed it. The family alleges that the land consolidation process had been completed in 1965. However, in 2015, their names were removed from the land records on the orders of the Consolidation Officer. A petition was filed in the Allahabad High Court against this in 2019. Despite the matter being sub judice, former Rohilkhand University Bareilly vice-chancellor Prof. K.P. Singh, who is now the VC of DDU, had the disputed land registered in the names of his wife Sanjesh and relatives on 24 January 2025. Son says former deputy tehsildar had demanded ₹10 lakh Bhag Singh has also accused former deputy tehsildar Shobhit Chaudhary of collusion. He said the tehsildar threatened his father in court and demanded ₹10 lakh. He also threatened to have the standing crop destroyed and the land seized with the help of the police. Bhag Singh said his father had planned to complain to the Governor, the district magistrate and the sub-divisional magistrate. Complaints had also been made to the Chief Minister and the senior superintendent of police. The issue had been raised at a press conference around four months earlier. SP says complaints had not been brought to his notice earlier Northern SP Santosh Singh said he had not previously been informed that the aggrieved party had been repeatedly approaching officials. The matter was pending before the court. The process was being carried out solely on the basis of the court's decision. Regarding the complaints made to the DM, SSP, Chief Minister and Governor, as well as the press conference held four months ago, the SP said this information had now come to light. An investigation would be conducted. The SP said it would first be examined why the allegations had been made and against whom. The family members would be spoken to. Further legal action would be taken according to their complaint. Body taken to village after post-mortem On Friday, the farmer consumed poison while going to his brother-in-law's house in Bajpur, Uttarakhand. He was first taken to a private hospital in Bahedi. When his condition became critical, he was referred to Bareilly, but he died on the way. After the post-mortem, the family took the body to the village. A large police contingent has been deployed in the village. MLA Ataur Rahman said: "Our deepest condolences are with the family. May Allah grant him comfort and peace, and grant peace to his family. We also urge the administration to extend its sympathy and provide them with the best possible assistance." Farmer says: Funeral rites will be stopped if FIR is not registered Office-bearers of the farmers' organisation have warned that the last rites will not be performed until an FIR is registered against the accused. They accused the police of delaying the registration of the FIR. The farmers' organisations say the accused are influential. They are preventing the FIR from being registered.

stories.title: Akhilesh takes a swipe at BJP over 'Radhe-Radhe' slogan:Says the party is on its way out, warns new SP members about investigations
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav said, "The people who have left the lotus have joined us. Now the lotus will wilt further. They will have to come up with a new slogan." Akhilesh said: They are now raising the slogan, 'Radhe Radhe, make the lotus bloom'. This means the lotus has wilted. In our tradition, we say 'Radhe Radhe' when bidding someone farewell. This means their departure is approaching. That is why they are saying 'Radhe Radhe'. Akhilesh also said that the SP organises Ramleela events too. He said Dr Rammanohar Lohia had asked artist MF Husain to create posters on the Ramayana. Akhilesh Yadav made these remarks during a press conference at the SP headquarters in Lucknow on Saturday. Several leaders from different political parties joined the SP on the occasion. What Akhilesh Said About Those Joining the SP ‘If We Come to Power, We Will Scrap the Agniveer Scheme’ Akhilesh said, "Whenever the Samajwadis get an opportunity, we will end arrangements such as the Agniveer scheme." He said the SP had launched its website. "At a time when people want to join through technology, they are welcome to do so. Today, getting justice, receiving respect and protecting people's dignity under the Constitution have become major challenges. The BJP is responsible for all these problems. Once the BJP is removed, these problems will go away." Seats Will Be Allocated Based on Winning Prospects Speaking about the 2027 Assembly elections, Akhilesh made it clear that talks with the Congress were continuing. Seats would be allocated based on the prospects of winning. He said removing the BJP was necessary to protect democracy and the Constitution. He described his meeting with Aam Aadmi Party leader Sanjay Singh as a discussion between the two leaders. Questions Raised Over Election Commission and Voter Lists Akhilesh accused the Election Commission of India of working under pressure from the BJP. He took a dig at the Chief Minister's statement that the names of 1.27 crore Hindu voters had been deleted from the electoral rolls. He asked what 'divine vision from heaven' had given the Chief Minister this information after the names were deleted. ‘In 2027, the Lathis Will Lose and Laptops Will Win’ Akhilesh Yadav released a new video with the slogan, 'In 2027, the lathis will lose and laptops will win... A PDA government in 2027'. He said the strength of the PDA had reached the grassroots and had become an issue of social justice, which would lead to the BJP's defeat in the upcoming elections. The SP chief accused the state government of corruption and alleged irregularities in the 'Har Ghar Nal Yojana'. He said everything would come to light in the CAG report. He announced that if the SP formed the government, a 'superconductor' factory would be set up in the state. Police services such as 'Dial 100' would also be made efficient again, as they were earlier. ‘Police and Some Officials Are Working Like BJP Office-Bearers’ Akhilesh said, "We will not hold a press conference on Gorakhpur now. We will do so after two days of mourning. The entire police force and some officials are working as BJP office-bearers." He added, "I had said earlier that I would write to the Election Commission. BJP leaders are sitting in the government and making preparations. They know that the public will remove them. The day the election dates are announced, the BJP will lose." He said, "We will write to the Election Commission with signatures of all our MLAs, MLCs and MPs, giving examples of officials who have worked like BJP workers. These officials have not been removed since the BJP came to power. Their relatives are occupying positions from which we cannot expect justice." Who Is Utpal Rai, Who Has Joined the SP? Utpal Rai, who hails from Mau district, has also contested elections from the Madhuban Assembly constituency. He has served as the vice-president of the Allahabad University Students' Union. He is the younger brother of Nishith Rai, former vice-chancellor of Dr Shakuntala Misra National Rehabilitation University. Utpal Rai was once considered close to Manoj Sinha. He joined the BJP in July 2016. Now, after a decade, he has left the BJP and joined the SP. However, his political career has not been limited to the BJP. He has been associated with different political parties. Utpal Rai also served as a minister of state with independent charge during the BSP government.
