stories.title: Pramod Tiwari to host Samajwadi Party-Congress seat-sharing talks:Azam Khan says party ready to offer more seats to keep alliance intact
stories.summary: Negotiations between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress over seat-sharing for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections will begin on Monday. Leaders of the two parties will meet at the Delhi residence of senior Congress leader and Rajya Sabha MP Pramod Tiwari at around noon. Ajay Maken will lead the Congress delegation, while Prof Ram Gopal Yadav will represent the SP. Both parties have formed committees to negotiate the seat-sharing arrangement. Discussions between the panels will continue for three days, with the aim of working out an electoral understanding for all 403 Assembly constituencies in Uttar Pradesh. The talks will focus on how many seats each party will contest and which party will field candidates in different constituencies. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has formed a four-member committee to discuss the alliance and seat-sharing arrangement with the Congress. It includes the party's national principal general secretary, Prof Ram Gopal Yadav; state president Shyamlal Pal; Ghosi MP Rajeev Rai; and Kairana MP Iqra Hasan. Congress panel includes Priyanka and KC Venugopal The Congress has also formed a five-member panel to negotiate seat-sharing with the SP. The committee comprises Ajay Maken, Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, state president Aradhana Mishra 'Mona', working president Imran Masood and Congress Legislature Party leader Virendra Chaudhary. Meeting to be held at Pramod Tiwari's residence The meeting between the two parties was initially scheduled for November 17 but was postponed because preparations had not been completed. It will now be held at the Delhi residence of Rajya Sabha MP Pramod Tiwari, father of Uttar Pradesh Congress president Aradhana Mishra 'Mona'. Discussions are expected to begin around noon. Representatives of both parties have left for Delhi. Congress initially sought 181 seats, SP reportedly firm on 55-60 There is a significant difference between the two parties over the number of seats to be contested. The Congress had initially demanded 181 seats, while the SP is reportedly unwilling to offer more than 55-60 seats. This leaves both parties with the challenge of reaching an agreement on the number of constituencies each will contest. Meanwhile, senior SP leader Azam Khan told Dainik Bhaskar that the Congress of today was different from what it used to be and that the distinction needed to be understood. He said Rahul Gandhi did not speak like leaders of the earlier generation. Regional parties play an important role in states because local problems and circumstances differ from one region to another. Azam Khan said leaders based at the Centre often neither fully understand nor recognise regional issues. They tend to focus more on national concerns, leaving local problems overlooked. He said the Congress had faced a similar situation in Uttar Pradesh because of three major issues concerning Ayodhya, Mathura and Kashi, which did not have the same significance in other states. He stressed that experience and understanding were essential to maintaining an alliance. The same principle applied to the SP, he said. "If we have to offer a few more seats to keep the alliance intact, we are ready to do so. The Congress should also be prepared to give up some seats if necessary. Our objective is not just to win seats but to ensure justice for people," he said. Congress prepares three-phase strategy for seat-sharing talks The Congress has prepared a revised list of constituencies after its initial demand for 181 seats. The list has reportedly received Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's approval. The party has now shifted its focus from the total number of seats to their electoral viability. It plans to stake a claim to constituencies where it has a stronger organisational presence and performed relatively well in previous elections. The proposed list reportedly includes a larger number of constituencies in western Uttar Pradesh and the Bundelkhand region. The Congress has drawn up a three-phase strategy to present its demands. First phase: 60 seats With Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's approval, the Congress has identified 60 seats that it wants to retain under its quota under all circumstances. These constituencies are spread across regions ranging from Purvanchal to western Uttar Pradesh. Second phase: 50 seats The second phase will focus on 50 constituencies where the Congress has performed in previous elections. The party will pay particular attention to seats in the Saharanpur, Meerut and Moradabad regions of western Uttar Pradesh. Third phase: 70 seats In the third phase, the Congress will stake its claim to another 70 seats based on the strength of its organisation and its prospects in those constituencies. These include seats linked to parliamentary constituencies such as Rae Bareli, Amethi and Prayagraj. SP and Congress to discuss constituencies individually According to Rajendra Pal Gautam, the Congress's Uttar Pradesh in-charge, the meeting will focus on discussing each Assembly constituency individually rather than deciding the total number of seats to be shared. Congress leaders say the objective of seat-sharing is not to create differences within the alliance but to ensure its electoral success. The party argues that it should be given an opportunity to contest constituencies where its position is stronger than that of the SP. Meanwhile, the SP has advised its leaders against making public statements on seat-sharing. After the meetings in Delhi on Monday and Tuesday, representatives of both parties will submit reports on the discussions to their respective top leaderships. The next round of negotiations will be planned based on these reports.

stories.title: Sister ties Rakhi on wrist of martyred brother:Wife faints, mother pleads to see his face one last time; 2 soldiers died during military exercise
stories.summary: The bodies of two soldiers killed during a military exercise in Haryana reached Uttar Pradesh on Monday morning. As Naik Manish Kumar's (26) body reached Shamli, the family was overwhelmed with grief. His sisters tied rakhis on their martyred soldier brother's wrist. His wife fainted while crying. His mother broke down as she pleaded to see her son's face one last time. As the bier was lifted for the funeral procession, his mother ran over and clung to his body. She kept saying, "Show me my beloved son's face one last time." Meanwhile, the body of Naik Ankush Kumar (29) reached Badaun. The entire village turned out to pay tribute. Family members kept consoling his wife. Their young children repeatedly asked their mother, "What happened to Papa? Will he never come back?" Manish and Ankush were run over by a tank during a routine military exercise. The tank passed over both soldiers. They died on the spot. Three heartbreaking pictures- As soon as the army personnel closed the coffin, the mother began sobbing uncontrollably. She pleaded, "Let me see my son's face one last time." First, let us learn about Naik Manish Kumar... Naik Manish Kumar was the only son in his family. He had three sisters. Two of his sisters, Guddan and Meenakshi, are married. His younger sister Ritu lives at home with their father Ramkumar, mother Manju and Manish's wife, Bulbul. Manish's body was brought to Bajjhu village in Shamli at 9 a.m. in a flower-decorated vehicle. As soon as the body reached the house, his mother, Manju, and wife, Bulbul, broke down. When Army personnel opened the coffin and showed them his face, they began wailing uncontrollably. When family members tried to console them and move them away, they continued staring intently at Manish's face. As Bulbul began to lose consciousness, a woman supported her. When she patted her face, Bulbul let out a scream. Her brother then helped support her. Clinging to their brother's photograph, his sisters kept saying that the light of the household had gone out. "With whom will we celebrate Raksha Bandhan now? Whom will we tie the rakhi to? We have lost our only support." Manish's father, Ramveer, is also a retired Army personnel. He said that if he had had more sons, he would have sent them to the Army as well. After the final viewing, the funeral procession travelled about 2 km to the village cremation ground. His cousin, Suraj, lit the funeral pyre. BKU president Naresh Tikait, former Cabinet minister Sanjeev Balyan and Lok Dal MLA Prasann Chaudhary also attended the funeral procession. Now learn about Badaun's Ankush... Naik Ankush Kumar lived in Aamgaon under the Civil Lines police station area in Badaun. His cousin Amit Kumar said that Ankush had spoken to his children over the phone at around 2 p.m. on Saturday. He was due to return home on Sunday. But the accident occurred before that. He is survived by his wife, Pooja, son Harsh (7) and daughter Nandini (11). His younger brother Vineet has a job. Ankur joined the Indian Army in 2010 from Kanthi in Nagpur. He was promoted two years ago. Ankur's father, Adesh Kumar, is also a retired Army personnel. His uncle Ghanendra Singh and his elder uncle's son, Amit Kumar, have also served in the Army and have since retired. Find out how the accident happened involving a tank... A routine military exercise was underway in the Bhojraj area, with around 32 tanks moving together. The movement of the heavy tanks raised a thick cloud of dust in the area, significantly reducing visibility ahead. During this, a tank driver could not see the personnel deployed at the front, and the tank ran over both of them. They were taken to a military hospital in critical condition Immediately after the accident, Army personnel and officers present at the site attended to both injured men. They were taken to the military hospital in Hisar without delay, but doctors could not save them because their injuries were severe.

stories.title: 'Study hard and become a prince':CM Yogi assures Class 8 student of cricket coaching after hearing his dream at Janata Darshan
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath took on the role of a mentor during his Janata Darshan programme on Monday, where he heard people's grievances and encouraged a young boy to pursue his sporting ambitions. Prince Sahu, a Class 8 student from Gonda, told the Chief Minister that he wanted to become a cricketer but his family's poor financial condition made it difficult to afford coaching fees and cricket equipment. Yogi assured him that financial constraints would not come in the way of his dream. He said the government would arrange cricket coaching and admission for him. CM advises student to balance studies and cricket Prince, a resident of Padri Parasray village in the Itiathok area of Gonda district, told the Chief Minister that he had been interested in cricket since childhood and wanted to pursue a career in the sport. However, his family's financial difficulties made it difficult to pay for coaching and buy a cricket kit. The Chief Minister spoke to the boy for around four to five minutes and guided him. He advised Prince to focus on his studies alongside cricket, pointing out that he was currently in Class 8. Yogi said arrangements for his admission to cricket coaching would be made after he passed his examinations with good marks. "Son, your name is Prince, so study hard and become a prince. Play as much as you want, but education is equally important," the Chief Minister told him. CM directs officials to resolve public grievances During the Janata Darshan programme, Yogi met people individually, received their written complaints and listened to their problems. He directed officials present at the venue to ensure that all complaints were resolved within a stipulated timeframe. He also stressed the need for fairness and sensitivity so that complainants were satisfied with the action taken. Assures financial assistance for medical treatment The Chief Minister also assured people seeking financial assistance for medical treatment that no needy patient would be denied treatment because of a lack of money. He said the government would provide financial assistance as soon as it received the estimated cost of the patient's treatment.

stories.title: ‘Dream big, build character, not just CVs’:Air Force Chief in Lucknow urges students to aim high; Shubhanshu Shukla says their experiments could reach space
stories.summary: A science fair was organised at CMS Golf City campus in Lucknow. Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Chief of the Air Staff, and astronaut Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla attended the event. They visited the students’ science exhibition and learnt about their models and experiments. During the event, Ashutosh Dixit urged young people to dream big, work hard and build strong character. He said students should not focus only on building their CVs but also on strengthening their character. He advised them to remain humble after achieving success. He also said Shubhanshu Shukla’s achievements remind us that the sky is not the limit. CMS students’ experiments are being prepared for possible testing in space. The Voyager Mixstix Microgravity Student Research Programme has been launched for this purpose. In collaboration with Earthizen and Israel’s Rakia mission, students from Classes 6 to 12 will develop experiments. Selected experiments may be tested aboard the International Space Station (ISS) in 2027. Robotics, drones and mobile planetarium among the attractions The fair will feature live demonstrations of scientific experiments, research presentations and discussions on space science. Students will get to see a mobile planetarium, a giant replica of the Moon, Arthaizen's space chariot and the Infosys Mobile Experience Bus. Floating models of Indian Navy warships will also be displayed.

stories.title: Four, including mother and son, killed in Mathura:Swift car crashes into truck, 5 injured; family had come from Madhya Pradesh to visit Vrindavan
stories.summary: A speeding Maruti Swift car rammed into the rear of a truck in Mathura. Four people, including a mother and her son, died in the accident. The deceased include two children and two women. Five other occupants of the car were injured. The family had travelled from Bhind in Madhya Pradesh to visit Mathura. The accident took place on the National Highway in the Jaint area at around 7.30 am on Monday, when the family was travelling from Barsana to Ramanreti. The collision was so severe that the car was badly mangled. The people inside were trapped in the wreckage. Police reached the spot, rescued those trapped in the car and rushed them to hospital. Police said Devashish was driving the car, which had nine people on board, including his wife and children. Devashish's son Rudra (4), his maternal aunt Ruby (32), Ruby's son Kanhaiya (10) and Ruby's friend Jyoti (30) died in the accident. Devashish, his mother Asha Devi, his wife Girja Devi, his daughter Gauri (5) and Jyoti's daughter Palak (12) were injured. Take a look at the pictures… Family performed parikrama throughout the night; accident suspected to have occurred due to driver dozing off According to the police, the car rammed into the truck from behind. The investigation revealed that the family had spent the entire night visiting temples and performing parikrama in Mathura-Vrindavan. This meant they had not slept. Devashish was driving the car, and police suspect that he may have dozed off, causing the vehicle to crash into a stationary truck. The injured have been admitted to Sarvodaya Hospital. One of them is in critical condition. District Magistrate Chandra Prakash Singh said the government would bear the entire cost of treatment for the injured. Yogi Adityanath has announced financial assistance of ₹1.5 lakh each for the families of the deceased.

stories.summary: An IndiGo flight travelling from Pune to Patna was diverted to Lucknow late on Sunday night because of bad weather in Patna. The aircraft was landed at Lucknow Airport as weather conditions in Patna were unsuitable. Flight 6E 653 landed safely in Lucknow at 2:45 a.m. on 23 November. 187 passengers and 5 infants were on board According to information from the airport, the IndiGo flight had departed from Pune for Patna. There were 187 passengers, five infants and six crew members on board. A total of 198 people were travelling on the aircraft. The flight was commanded by pilot in command Amit Sharma. Due to bad weather in Patna, the aircraft was sent to Lucknow instead of landing at its scheduled destination. Departed for Patna after around five hours After remaining at Lucknow Airport for around five hours, the aircraft departed for Patna at 8 a.m. The flight schedule was disrupted due to the bad weather, and passengers faced delays.

stories.title: Yogi gets emotional remembering his mother:She could not believe it when he arrived seeking alms; asked, 'Son, what have you done to yourself?'
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi wrote an emotional letter remembering his mother. He wrote that a mother can take everyone's place, but no one can take a mother's place. He also shared with people the story of asking his mother for alms after renouncing worldly life. In 'Yogi's Letter', the Chief Minister wrote, "Following the rules of monastic life, I called out for alms at the door. Hearing my voice, my mother came outside. Before she could say anything, I said, 'Mother, please give me alms.'" Composing herself, his mother said, "Son, what have you done to yourself? What was lacking at home that you are begging?" I replied, "Mother, monastic life is now my dharma, and a yogi's hunger can be satisfied only through alms." "I have not come here to stay, but to receive alms. Whatever you give me as alms will help fulfil my resolve." His mother then respected her monk son's decision and gave him alms. Yogi's mother, Savitri Devi, died at her home in Panchur, her ancestral village in Pauri, Uttarakhand, on Friday. She was 91. Her last rites were performed at Chandi Ghat in Haridwar on Saturday. Yogi lit the funeral pyre along with his younger brother. What did Yogi write? Read it in five points 1. Without mothers, neither would we exist nor would any living being Yogi wrote, "This letter is dedicated to every mother, without whom life would not be possible. If there were no mothers, neither would we exist nor would any living being, and this world would not exist either. A mother is not merely the one who gives birth; she is the creator of the entire universe. Even God is born to a mother." 2. Remembering my mother brings tears to my eyes Today, remembering my mother, my eyes are welling up with tears. Losing one's mother is not merely like losing a person; it feels as though a dense shade from over one's head, unconditional love and emotional support have all been taken away. 3. An old moment suddenly flashed before my eyes When my first teacher and the mother who taught me my letters departed this world, an old moment suddenly flashed before my eyes: after more than three years of becoming a monk, I was standing outside the door of my home in saffron robes. During that journey from Gorakhpur to my village, Panchur, a flood of emotions was surging through my mind. 4. Trying to fulfil my duty towards all mothers and sisters There are some debts in life that can never be repaid, but we can certainly fulfil our duty. Since entering politics and social service, I have been trying to fulfil this duty towards all the mothers and sisters in the state. Our true respect for every mother will be shown when every citizen of the state takes a pledge today to support a mother who has no one to rely on, understand the suffering of a mother in need and bring a smile to the face of a distressed mother.

stories.title: Cylinder blast at councillor's house in Jalaun, 23 injured:13 children and 5 women among them; 5 children critical, burns of up to 60%
stories.summary: A gas cylinder exploded at councillor Mata Prasad's house in Orai, Jalaun. The incident left 23 people with burns, including 13 children, 5 women and 5 men. Nineteen people who suffered serious burns have been referred to Jhansi Medical College. Ten of them, including 5 young children, remain in critical condition. They have suffered burns to between 20% and 60% of their bodies. At midnight late on Sunday, Jhansi Range Inspector General Akash Kulhari reached the medical college. He spoke to the injured and their family members to gather information about the incident. The IG said, "A fire broke out after the gas cylinder leaked. Some children and women from the settlement went to watch the fire, when the cylinder exploded. A team of 15 doctors is treating the injured." See two pictures- Here is the full sequence of events... Family members were making tea at the home of councillor Mata Prasad, a resident of Shantinagar in Orai, on Sunday evening. During this, the gas cylinder suddenly caught fire. Before the family could understand what was happening, the fire had already intensified and the cylinder exploded with a loud blast. The force of the explosion sent pieces of the cylinder flying into the surrounding area. More than 10 members of the councillor's family, along with people from the neighbourhood, were caught in the blast. The loud explosion caused panic in the area. A crowd gathered at the scene. Fire brigade douses blaze, 19 people with burn injuries brought to Jhansi As soon as the accident was reported, police and fire brigade teams reached the spot. Fire brigade personnel brought the fire under control after a strenuous operation. With the help of local residents and the police, the injured were taken to the district hospital and Government Medical College, Orai. From there, doctors referred 19 seriously burned people to Jhansi Medical College. 15 doctors deployed in Jhansi, principal takes charge The administration went on alert after the cylinder blast. The AD Health officer called Jhansi Medical College Principal Dr Sudhir Singh and instructed him to make arrangements. Jhansi District Magistrate Gaurang Rathi also alerted the hospital administration. A team of 15 doctors from the surgery and plastic surgery departments was then deployed. The beds in the plastic surgery ward were also vacated. The injured began arriving from 10 p.m. The 19th injured person, Pushpendra, reached the medical college at 12:35 a.m. All the injured have been admitted, and treatment has begun. These people suffered serious burns Dayawati (32) and Bablu (45), admitted to Jhansi Medical College, have suffered 60% burns; Vaishnavi (8) has suffered 55% burns; Dayanand (41) and Munni Devi (62) have suffered 50% burns; and Somwati (45) has suffered 40% burns. Krish (7) has suffered 40% burns, while Anshika (10) and Umang (9) have suffered 30% burns, and Dipesh (8) up to 25% burns. The remaining injured people have suffered burns ranging from 5% to 20%.

stories.title: Truck that killed elephant in Gorakhpur seized:CCTV helped identify vehicle; driver fled after delivering milk and parking it in Baghagada
stories.summary: Police have identified the truck that hit an elephant returning from a wedding procession in the Belipar area of Gorakhpur. The elephant, which was seriously injured in the accident, died during treatment. Two men riding on it were also injured. The accident took place near Mehroli village on the Gorakhpur-Varanasi Highway between 5.30 am and 5.55 am on November 21. Elephant owner Rafi Ullah Ansari was returning from a wedding procession with his elephant when a speeding truck hit it from behind. The driver fled with the truck after the accident. Using CCTV footage, police traced the vehicle bearing registration number UP78 MN 0529 and seized it. A case has been registered based on the mahout's complaint, and efforts are underway to trace the absconding driver. Truck hits elephant while returning from wedding Rafi Ullah Ansari, a resident of Sevai village, had attended a wedding procession in Gajpur with his elephant on November 21. He was returning home the following morning. His sons, Jafar Ansari and Firoz Ansari, were riding on the elephant. The group was travelling on foot towards Gorakhpur. When they reached near Rajkumar's brick kiln in Mehroli village under Belipar police station limits, a speeding truck approached from behind and hit the elephant. The elephant suffered serious injuries, while Jafar and Firoz were also hurt. The truck driver fled the spot immediately after the collision. Elephant dies during treatment at hospital The injured elephant was taken to Rachit Hospital in Gorakhpur for treatment. Doctors tried to save its life, but it died during treatment. Meanwhile, Jafar and Firoz were taken to the district hospital by ambulance. The elephant's death has left its owner and family members mourning. Driver leaves truck in Baghagada after milk delivery After fleeing the accident site, the driver allegedly delivered milk at another location before parking the truck in Baghagada and escaping. Meanwhile, police examined CCTV footage from the accident site and nearby areas. Based on the footage, they identified the truck bearing registration number UP78 MN 0529 and seized it. FIR registered on mahout's complaint; driver yet to be traced A case was registered at Belipar police station on November 22 based on a complaint filed by elephant mahout Rafi Ullah Ansari. The FIR mentions the truck's registration number, UP78 MN 0529, but the driver's name and address are not known. Police have registered a case against the unidentified driver. A sub-inspector has been assigned to investigate the matter. Efforts are underway to trace the driver using CCTV footage and other evidence.

stories.title: Rain alert issued for four UP districts today:Dense fog to cover eastern UP; Hardoi records lowest temperature at 11°C
stories.summary: Rain is likely in four districts of Uttar Pradesh on Monday, while dense fog is expected in the eastern part of the state. The weather has changed in UP due to Cyclone Akvan and snowfall in the mountains. Light rain is likely in Sonbhadra, Mirzapur, Chandauli and Varanasi. Dense fog is also expected in eastern Uttar Pradesh. On Sunday, Hardoi was the coldest district in the state, recording a minimum temperature of 11°C. Dense fog covered 24 districts in the morning, including Prayagraj, Kaushambi and Pratapgarh. Visibility dropped to such low levels in several places that people could barely see beyond 10 metres on the roads. Amid the rising cold and fog, the Uttar Pradesh Relief Commissioner has urged people to step out in the morning only when necessary. People have also been advised to take special care of children and elderly family members. Temperatures likely to drop further next week Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, said the cyclone that had formed over the Bay of Bengal had weakened. As a result, northerly and north-westerly winds have started gaining strength, replacing easterly winds. He said night temperatures in western Uttar Pradesh would gradually fall. Fog may occur in some areas during the morning. "Cold conditions will intensify from next week. However, people will have to wait a little longer for severe cold," Singh said. Farmers advised to take precautions during sowing and irrigation With rain likely in November, farmers have been advised to take precautions while managing their rabi crops. In particular, farmers in eastern Uttar Pradesh should ensure proper drainage in fields while sowing wheat, gram, peas and mustard. Waterlogging in low-lying fields could damage crops. Farmers should avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields that already have sufficient moisture due to rainfall. Decisions on sowing and irrigation should be based on weather conditions and soil moisture. stories.title: Husband arrested in BKT woman’s suicide case:Confesses to murder; mother-in-law says she spoke to another man on phone
stories.summary: Police have arrested the woman's husband in connection with her suicide in Lucknow's BKT area. During questioning, he confessed to killing her. The couple had quarrelled on the day of the incident, after which he killed her. The woman's parental family had accused her in-laws of killing her and destroying evidence. Ashok's mother, Ramkumari, meanwhile, said that her daughter-in-law Sunita used to speak to another man on the phone. This had led to an argument between the husband and wife. The husband and wife had quarrelled before the incident Sunita, aged around 35, was found hanging in Achramau village under the BKT police station area on the night of 16 November. Her in-laws said that Sunita had hanged herself. After this, her in-laws cremated Sunita without waiting for her maternal family to arrive. Her family had alleged that she was murdered. They had married 17 years ago Police registered a case based on a complaint by Sunita's father, Panchu, and arrested Ashok. Sunita was a resident of Udatpur Majra Raipur Raja village under the Itaunja police station area. She had married Ashok Gautam of Achramau village around 17 years ago. Ashok worked as a labourer. The couple have two sons, Aakash (13) and Adarsh (10). Ashok's mother, Ramkumari, and his two brothers also live in the family. All three brothers live separately with their respective families. 'There was never any dispute between the two' Mohammad Fuzail, a resident of the village, said that there had never been any dispute between Sunita and Ashok. They had been married for around 16 years. According to him, everyone in the family had a good nature. The villagers were shocked when they suddenly learnt that Sunita had hanged herself.

stories.title: Will Congress's stubborn stand hurt its own allies?:Seat-sharing tussle in UP mirrors Bihar elections; Akhilesh, like Tejashwi, returns empty-handed from Delhi
stories.summary: On 17 November 2026, a meeting between the top leadership of the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress was scheduled to discuss seat-sharing for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Akhilesh Yadav had reached Delhi early on the morning of 16 November, a day before the proposed meeting. However, news emerged in the afternoon that Congress had formed a five-member committee to hold discussions. Akhilesh was now expected to negotiate with this committee. He returned to Lucknow. A similar situation had unfolded during the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections, when Tejashwi Yadav had arrived to negotiate seat-sharing. He was told to discuss the matter with KC Venugopal and Krishna Allavaru, the Congress in-charge for Bihar. Several other developments involving the SP and Congress also bring back memories of last year's Bihar elections and the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. On both occasions, Congress's rigid stand dealt a major blow to its opposition allies. After the 2017 defeat, Akhilesh even said that forming an alliance with Congress had been his biggest mistake. So, will Akhilesh Yadav suffer a setback this time too because of Congress's rigid stand? Read today's UP Explainer... Question 1: How similar is the Congress tussle with the RJD in the 2025 Bihar elections to its current differences with the SP in Uttar Pradesh? Answer: A) Congress demanded 70 seats in Bihar and is now staking a claim to 181 in UP Bihar: The RJD and Congress had contested the 2020 Assembly elections together. Of the 243 Assembly seats, Congress was allotted 70, while the remaining seats went to the RJD and other parties. Congress won only 19 of the seats it contested. Congress again wanted 70 seats for the 2025 elections. However, considering its poor strike rate, Tejashwi wanted to give it only 50-55 seats. After prolonged negotiations, Congress eventually agreed to contest 61 seats. Uttar Pradesh: In the 2022 Assembly elections, Congress contested 399 of the state's 403 seats without an alliance and won just two. Despite this, it is now demanding 181 seats for the 2027 elections. Congress is staking its claim based on the six Lok Sabha seats it won in Uttar Pradesh in 2024 and its increased voter base. Akhilesh, however, has asked the party to explain not just which seats it wants but also its prospects of winning them. At a meeting of SP MLAs and MPs on 30 September 2026, Akhilesh had said that his party would contest 350 seats. Overall, he is not inclined to offer Congress more than 50-55 seats. B) Tejashwi returned from Delhi without a meeting in 2025; Akhilesh did the same this time Bihar: On 12 October 2025, Tejashwi Yadav reached Delhi for seat-sharing talks. Despite several rounds of discussions, no agreement was reached. The situation deteriorated to such an extent that he had to return to Patna without meeting Congress's top leaders, Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge. Uttar Pradesh: Akhilesh had reached Delhi a day before the scheduled meeting. On the evening of 16 November, he spoke to Rahul at the launch of Sonia Gandhi's book. Rahul reiterated that a committee had been formed for the negotiations. Akhilesh was not comfortable holding discussions with the committee and returned to Lucknow. C) RJD and Congress contested the Bihar elections without announcing a formal seat-sharing arrangement Symbol row in Bihar: The election dates had already been announced in Bihar. On 14 October 2025, after seat-sharing talks failed, RJD chief Lalu Prasad Yadav began distributing party symbols to candidates, further escalating tensions. However, some symbols were later taken back and negotiations continued. Eventually, the RJD and Congress released their candidate lists without making a joint announcement. Congress contested 61 seats and the RJD 143. Formation of committees in UP: On 16 November 2026, Congress formed a committee headed by Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. After the proposed meeting on 17 November was postponed, the SP also formed a seven-member committee on 20 November under the leadership of Prof Ram Gopal Yadav. It comprises five leaders and two data experts. The aim is to hold seat-by-seat discussions based on data. The electoral cost of prolonged differences Due to the prolonged tussle until the last moment in Bihar, the BJP and its allies won 202 seats, while the RJD-Congress alliance was reduced to just 31 seats. The absence of a formal seat-sharing announcement delayed the selection of candidates. Contradictory statements by leaders also created confusion among grassroots workers. The cadre votes of one party could not be transferred to the candidates of the other. Due to a lack of coordination, alliance partners, including the RJD, Congress, CPI and VIP, ended up contesting against one another in several constituencies. According to reports after the withdrawal of nominations, Mahagathbandhan candidates were directly pitted against each other in 12 seats. The division of opposition votes directly benefited the NDA. Question 2: Did the same thing happen during the 2017 UP Assembly elections? Answer: Yes. The current tussle bears considerable resemblance to the experience of 2017. At that time too, the two parties held prolonged discussions over seat-sharing. The situation deteriorated to such an extent that SP chief Akhilesh Yadav released his list of candidates even before the alliance was formally announced. After the 2025 Bihar experience, Uttar Pradesh's own history from 2017 serves as a reminder that seat-sharing becomes the biggest challenge whenever a party tries to join hands with Congress. The situations in 2017 and 2026 can be understood as follows: A) Congress insisted on 125 seats in 2017 Insistence on a three-digit figure: Then Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav wanted to give Congress 80-85 seats. However, Congress insisted on 125 seats. Its argument was that, being a national party, it deserved a respectable share of more than 100 seats, or a 'three-digit' figure. Akhilesh's unilateral move: When the talks failed to make progress, Akhilesh released his candidate list on 20 January 2017 without waiting for the formal announcement of the alliance. The list also included constituencies where Congress had sitting MLAs, further escalating tensions. A comparison between 2017 and recent developments shows a similar strategy of pressure politics in Congress's demands and the SP's offer. In 2026, Congress has raised its claim to 181 seats, while Akhilesh has reduced his 2017 offer to 50-55 seats. B) Priyanka emerged as a tough negotiator in 2017; Congress has put her in charge again After the SP released its candidate list in 2017, UP Congress leaders began withdrawing from the negotiations. Priyanka Gandhi then took charge of the talks. She is regarded as a tough negotiator. As a result, Akhilesh had to concede 105 seats to Congress. This time too, Priyanka is leading the committee formed by Congress to negotiate seat-sharing. C) The cost of the 2017 political turmoil The SP won only 47 seats, while Congress managed just seven. Following the bitter experience of the alliance, Akhilesh publicly said that joining hands with Congress had been a big mistake. This was one of the reasons the two parties contested separately in the 2022 Assembly elections. The SP improved its tally to 111 seats, while Congress, without the SP's support, was reduced to just two. The factors behind the alliance's defeat were also similar to those seen in the 2025 Bihar elections: poor coordination and the failure to transfer votes led to the alliance's downfall. However, several other major political factors also played a decisive role, including the strong electoral wave in favour of PM Narendra Modi and the BJP, effective booth management, aggressive campaigning and internal family disputes within the Akhilesh-led SP. Question 3: Will the old SP-Congress story repeat itself in 2027? Answer: If the seat-sharing deadlock is not resolved in time, a situation similar to 2017 and 2025 is likely to emerge. A) Will Akhilesh release another candidate list without a seat-sharing agreement? Several constituencies claimed by Congress have sitting SP MLAs or were seats where the SP finished second in 2022. The SP is not willing to give up these seats. It is also using internal surveys and its organisational network to mobilise potential candidates. A few days ago, Congress also formed a screening committee under the leadership of Ajay Maken to shortlist potential candidates. If seat-sharing negotiations drag on, both parties may signal to their prospective candidates to begin preparations in their respective constituencies. This could lead to a situation similar to 2017 and 2025, when candidates were announced before an agreement was reached. B) SP and Congress could find themselves contesting against each other in several seats Both parties have their own assessments of which party has a stronger organisation in each constituency. When seats where local leaders of one alliance partner have been preparing for a long time are allotted to another party, it often leads to competing claims and resentment at the local level. If this happens, even after an alliance is formed, SP grassroots workers may not fully support Congress candidates. Leaders unhappy with a seat being allotted to another party may contest as Independents or rebel candidates from rival parties. Moreover, if neither party is willing to withdraw from a particular constituency, candidates from alliance partners could end up contesting against each other. C) Seat-sharing disputes could upset the arithmetic of opposition votes The margin of victory is very narrow in several constituencies. Here, the consolidation of opposition votes plays a decisive role. If coordination between the SP and Congress breaks down and they contest separately, the division of opposition votes, particularly among Muslim and non-BJP voters, will directly benefit the BJP. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, votes were transferred more effectively between the SP and Congress, helping the alliance perform well. However, if public statements over seat-sharing intensify before the next election, transferring cadre votes between the two parties could become difficult, even if the alliance remains intact. If the seat-sharing decision is taken just before the election announcement or close to the nomination deadline, the parties will not have enough time to campaign together or prepare a joint election strategy. D) Congress wants to regain its voter base, while the SP wants to retain its strong seats At the heart of the negotiations are the political ambitions and questions of survival facing both parties. Congress wants to regain the ground it has lost in Uttar Pradesh. This is why it wants to contest a larger number of seats. The SP, meanwhile, is the state's principal opposition party. It wants to retain as many seats as possible, relying on its voter base, sitting MLAs and strong organisational network. An agreement will be possible only if both parties accept a formula based on constituency-wise data from the 2022 Assembly or 2024 Lok Sabha elections, along with the winning prospects of individual candidates. For this, Congress will have to scale back its demands, or the SP will have to give up some seats to allow Congress to expand its organisation. E) Despite tensions, there is hope that the alliance will remain intact The SP's decision to form a committee on 20 November makes it clear that Akhilesh wants to keep the doors open for negotiations. Just a few days earlier, he had travelled to Delhi with the same hope but returned without any breakthrough. If Priyanka Gandhi and senior SP leaders reach an agreement based on data and ground realities, the parties can announce joint candidates and prepare a campaign strategy well ahead of the 2027 elections. Ultimately, if Congress fails to learn from the experiences of previous elections and refuses to accept a middle ground, the SP is likely to suffer the biggest setback.

stories.title: Yadavs in Kunda say Raja Bhaiya is 'everything' here:How true is Akhilesh's claim of losing ground? What did Raja Bhaiya gain from Ram Katha?
stories.summary: “When people's support starts declining, they organise Ram Kathas…” - Akhilesh Yadav, Agra These words were aimed at Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya. After opposition to Dhirendra Shastri, Raja Bhaiya organised a Ram Katha in Kunda. The three-day event has ended, but it has left behind several political messages. By bringing prominent Thakur leaders from across eastern Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan onto one platform, Raja Bhaiya has staged a major show of strength. There is a reason behind this. During the 2022 Assembly elections, Akhilesh Yadav had made the remark, “We will put a lock on Kunda.” For the first time since 2002, Raja Bhaiya won by a margin of just 15 percentage points. In previous elections, the candidates contesting against him had lost by margins of more than 50 percentage points. So, what has Raja Bhaiya managed to achieve through the Ram Katha? Read this ground report... Around 5 lakh people attended the three-day Ram Katha. What did Raja Bhaiya gain from bringing together prominent political figures from Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan? To understand this, the Bhaskar team spoke to people who attended the event and examined the caste equations of the Kunda Assembly constituency. Here is the political atmosphere in the area explained in three points: Beti Raj Bhavan Chosen as the Venue, Twice as Many People as the Pandal's Capacity Turned Up Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya, is the MLA from Kunda. He chose the area behind his residence, Beti Raj Bhavan, to organise the Ram Katha. A pandal covering 56,000 square feet was set up, but as the event progressed, twice as many people as its capacity turned up. People came not only from Kunda in Pratapgarh but also from Prayagraj, Kaushambi, Rae Bareli, Fatehpur and other parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh. The Bhaskar team spoke to people who had come to listen to the Ram Katha. Shivmurat Yadav from Kunda said, “Those who oppose the Ram Katha are fools. They do not even know what Sanatan is. The same people are opposing it. Thousands of Yadavs in Kunda stand with Raja Bhaiya. He is our government here. He listens to poor people in all kinds of situations, whether they are happy or facing difficulties. That is why no caste equation works here. A few votes slipped away in the last election, but this time the SP candidate will lose by 50,000 votes.” Those Opposing the Pandit or the Ram Katha Are Not from Kunda Lavlesh Saroj, who attended the event, said, “I have listened to several Ram Kathas before, but I have never seen such a grand event here. Even Hindu refugees from Pakistan attended it. Those opposing it on Facebook are not from Kunda. Everyone who belongs here is attending the Katha. Not just one or two, but more than 50,000 people from the Yadav community are here to support Raja Bhaiya.” Lavlesh further said, “The opposition of a few people cannot represent the entire community. Raja Bhaiya brought Pandit Dhirendra Shastri from the airport to Kunda in his car to prove this. Nobody came to block the road because these people only try to create an atmosphere of opposition. They do not represent the people here.” ‘No Caste Equation Works Here; Everyone Is Concerned Only About Raja Bhaiya’ Shobhnath Patel lives around 4 km from the Katha venue. We asked him whether the PDA slogan given by the SP works in this area. Shobhnath said, “There is no PDA here. Even if someone from this community contests the election, it will make no difference. We look after our own area. Here, we are concerned only about Raja Bhaiya. As for Bageshwar Baba, wherever he goes, people turn up on their own. Raja Bhaiya also has a large number of supporters here, which is why the crowd is so big.” ‘Whether Raja Bhaiya contests himself or fields someone else, they will win’ Rajesh Yadav from Bansiyara village said, “Those who say Raja Bhaiya's political influence is declining should visit Kunda. People from every community have affection for him. Whether he contests himself or fields someone else, they will all win by a big margin.” An elderly man, Bhullar, who had come from Mohaddipur, folded his hands while speaking about Raja Bhaiya. He said, “He looks after everyone in society. We have served Raja Bhaiya, and our children will also do so because he has taken such good care of us. When my wife died, he helped us with her last rites. If you speak to anyone here, you will find that everyone works for him.” Ram Katha and Politics Are Separate, Do Not Link the Two The Ram Katha has strengthened Raja Bhaiya's religious image. Most of the young people we spoke to in the area appeared to project him as a prominent Hindutva figure. Pradeep Mishra from Kunda said, “Some people spread false claims that the Ram Katha was organised to get votes. This Katha is being held for religion. There is no caste issue here. Raja Bhaiya himself is asking everyone to stay united. Even those who used to wear white caps and visit mosques have now started believing in Sanatan. In Kaliyug, demons used to exist, and these people still display the same nature today. These people who oppose religion are not even human. That is why they find faults with everything.” Dhirendra Pratap Singh, the village head of Bansiyara, said, “Raja Bhaiya is a devotee of Lord Ram, which is why he organised the Katha. There is no one who can compete with him here.” Bharat Singh, who was accompanying him, said, “The Katha and politics are two separate things. Some people unnecessarily link them. Please do not do that.” Supporters Also Built an Atmosphere in Raja Bhaiya's Favour During the Ram Katha, Dhirendra Shastri also spoke about Raja Bhaiya's Hindutva credentials from the stage on several occasions. He praised Raja Bhaiya for performing Shastra Puja and said that there should be someone like Raja Bhaiya in every district. During the event, several young people were also seen displaying a hoarding across the area. It called for Raja Bhaiya to become the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh and Yogi Adityanath to become the Prime Minister. The hoarding became one of the most discussed aspects of the Katha. Discussion: Raja Bhaiya Managed to Demonstrate Unity Several Thakur leaders from Uttar Pradesh appeared united at the Ram Katha. Among those who attended the event were Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, MLC Brijesh Singh 'Prinsu', Sushil Singh, MLC Vineet Singh, MLA Abhay Singh, Rakesh Singh, Abhijeet Singh Sanga, Aditi Singh, Uttar Pradesh minister Dinesh Pratap Singh and Bhojpuri actor Pawan Singh. Independent MLA Ravindra Bhati from Rajasthan also attended. The biggest discussion centred on the presence of prominent eastern Uttar Pradesh strongmen Brijesh Singh and Dhananjay Singh. Both attended the Katha. It was said that differences between people who had disagreements in the past were resolved during the event. An attempt was also made to send a message to those holding senior political positions that Thakurs in Uttar Pradesh are united. Going by the discussions in political circles, Raja Bhaiya appears to have succeeded in demonstrating this unity.

stories.title: CM योगी आदित्यनाथ की मां सावित्री देवी का निधन, 91 साल की उम्र में ली अंतिम सांस, कल ऋषिकेश के संपूर्णानंद घाट पर होगा अंतिम संस्कार

stories.title: UP police use AI to trace missing woman:Recreated her face using a 19-year-old photograph; found her with husband in Rajasthan
stories.summary: Sonbhadra police found a woman using AI. She had gone missing from Sonbhadra on 14 July. Her family had no photograph of her. After an extensive search, they found one photograph, but it was from 2007, when the woman was studying in Class 4. With the help of ChatGPT and Google Gemini, the police had a current photograph of the woman created. She was safely recovered from Rajasthan. The SP awarded Constable Vijay Pandey a commendation certificate and a ₹2,100 reward. The case is from the Babni police station area. Young man accused of luring her away Kismat Devi, a resident of Jaurahi village, filed a complaint on 14 July that her daughter was missing. Kismat alleged that a young man took her daughter Manju (30) to Varanasi on the pretext of marriage. There has been no trace of her since. The police registered a case and began an investigation. Neither in-laws nor maternal family had a photograph The police had no photograph of the woman. Neither her maternal family nor her in-laws had a picture of her. During the investigation, the police went to the woman's school. Manju had studied in Class 4 there in 2007 and had filled out a scholarship form with a photograph attached. Identifying the woman's present-day face from this approximately 23-year-old photograph was a challenge for the police. Family identified her from the AI-generated photograph To find a solution to the problem, constable Vijay Pandey, posted at Babhni police station, sought the help of artificial intelligence (AI). The constable provided Manju's childhood photograph to ChatGPT and Google Gemini. He used the childhood photograph along with pictures of the woman's parents and sister. Based on all these images, a probable face matching Manju's current age was generated. After seeing the photograph, her family identified her as Manju Devi. Found in Rajasthan with her husband and children After receiving the photograph and verifying it along with the other information, the police learned that Manju was in Rajasthan. The police reached Govind Singh Ka Bas village in the Hamirwas police station area of Churu district. Manju Devi was safely recovered from there. The investigation revealed that she had been living there with her husband, Umendra, and that they also have two children. Woman had been missing from home for 5 years SP Abhishek Verma said that a woman named Manju Devi Kharwar had been missing from her home for nearly five years. The police launched a special operation to trace her. Constable Vijay Pandey did commendable work by uploading an old photograph of the woman from when she was in Class 7, along with photographs of her parents, to Google Gemini and ChatGPT. By entering several prompts, he generated an image showing what the woman might look like today. When the AI-generated photograph was shown to her parents, they too recognised that their daughter would probably look approximately like that now. UP DGP and SP honour constable Using this photograph, the police traced the woman safely to Rajasthan's Churu district via Varanasi and Agra and handed her over to her family. After she was handed over, it emerged that she had got married and settled down, but her parents had been extremely worried because they had received no news of her. For this commendable work, the Uttar Pradesh DGP awarded constable Vijay Pandey ₹5,000, while Sonbhadra Police also gave him a certificate of commendation and a cash prize of ₹2,100.

stories.title: Azam Khan on Yogi's mother:'This is a great shock'; says no one has wealth like a mother; supporters chant 'the lion has arrived' as he reaches Moradabad
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan reached Moradabad with his son, Abdullah Azam, late on Friday evening. There, he expressed grief over the death of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's mother. Azam said, "It is a great shock. May Allah grant her patience. It is a great loss; no one possesses a treasure like a mother." Supporters welcomed Azam on his arrival in Moradabad and raised slogans. They said, "Look, look who has arrived-the lion has arrived, the lion has arrived." Azam Khan waved his hand and asked them not to raise slogans. He said he had not come to engage in politics. After this, Azam Khan reached Gulab Mosque in Harthala and offered prayers. Azam visits SP leader Yusuf Malik's home After offering prayers, Azam Khan reached the home of his close associate and SP leader Yusuf Malik. There, he expressed grief over the death of Yusuf Malik's son. He then went to the cemetery and visited his son's grave. Yusuf Malik was held with Azam Khan in Rampur jail for a long time. During that period, police arrested him on charges of threatening to kill and attacking the Additional Municipal Commissioner of Moradabad. He was later also booked under the National Security Act (NSA). Azam Khan released from jail after a year Azam Khan reached Rampur at around 10 p.m. on Wednesday after being released from jail. There, he had said, "There will be no election; there will be a revolution. There will be no change; there will be a flood. The ED officials should repair their image and reform themselves. They should neither ruin the country nor themselves." Earlier, as soon as Azam came out of Dasna jail in Ghaziabad, supporters and the media surrounded him. Azam remained silent, then said only this: "I stand by what I have always said. A Muslim built the temple of education; this is his punishment." Find out which case led the ED to arrest Azam Read what happened after Azam was released from jail On 29 October, the High Court suspended the 10-year sentences handed down to Azam and his son Abdullah in the two PAN card cases and granted them bail. Both were subsequently released from Rampur jail. Azam walked out of Rampur jail on the evening of 31 October, after 11 months in custody. Just 15 minutes later, the ED arrested him in the money laundering case and took him to Ghaziabad. The ED's special PMLA court first sent Azam to judicial custody until 14 November and then extended it until 26 November.

stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri holds court with people claiming to be possessed:Women roll on ground, men tear clothes while grinding teeth at Raja Bhaiya's event
stories.summary: Dhirendra Shastri's divine court was held in Pratapgarh on Friday. Slips bearing the names of devotees were drawn. During the event, he said, "Those suffering from spirit-related ailments should come forward." After this, women and men from all three marquees went near the stage. As soon as Dhirendra Shastri began reciting the Hanuman Chalisa, some people started screaming and shouting. Several women began rolling on the ground and swaying. One young man began beating his head, while another performed a snake dance. Some men were seen gnashing their teeth. One young man tore his shirt and began beating his chest. At the court, Dhirendra Shastri said, "If miracles could be performed merely with sacred ash, why would he have a cancer hospital built?" He cited the example of Lord Hanuman bringing the Sanjeevani herb and saving Lakshman's life. He said people should not stop taking medicines after getting caught up in such gatherings. After the divine court, Dhirendra Shastri jumped off the stage and climbed down. He met Raja Bhaiya and took his leave. Raja Bhaiya himself drove him to the helicopter. Earlier, Raja Bhaiya explained why he drove Dhirendra Shastri himself from Prayagraj to Pratapgarh. He said, "If we wanted, we could have brought Bageshwar Dham Sarkar here from Prayag by helicopter. But we wanted to see who would try to stop us, which is why I went there myself. I did not see anyone on the way." Earlier, a three-day Ram Katha was held at Raja Bhaiya's residence in Benti from 17 to 19 November. Several ministers in the Uttar Pradesh government, film actors and several VIPs attended it. Strongman leaders Brij Bhushan Singh, Brijesh Singh and Dhananjay Singh also attended the religious discourse.

stories.title: Woman employee beats XEN inside his office in Hamirpur:Says he holds her hand and asks for her address, asks when she will treat him to tea
stories.summary: In Hamirpur, a woman employee of the electricity department severely beat the XEN in his cabin. The woman alleges that the XEN behaved indecently towards her. She said he called her into his cabin, held her hand and asked for her home address. When the woman beat the XEN, the other office staff continued to support her. A video of the incident has also emerged. The XEN was heard saying only, "This is wrong." The woman, who has filed a written complaint with the police, has demanded action. The matter falls under the jurisdiction of the Nagar Kotwali police station. First, look at the two pictures... Now read the full matter... Manoj Kumar Vishwakarma is posted as an executive engineer (XEN) in the Electricity Testing Division. A woman works there as an executive assistant. The woman said that after her husband's death, she lived alone in a rented room. Manoj often behaved inappropriately around her. He asked her over the phone for the address of her room. On Friday, Manoj Kumar called her to his chamber and asked, "When are you inviting me to your home for tea?" She told him that if he wanted tea from her home, they could order it there and he could have tea in the chamber, but that she would not invite him to her home. After this, he grabbed her hand and pulled her towards him. He would call her to his cabin In response, I beat him. By what right did he hold my hand? If he is the boss, he should behave like one. Earlier too, he would call me to his cabin. There, he would keep talking about one pointless thing or another. He would hold my hand and say, "Your line is very long; someone will support you." I told the other people in the office about it as well. Everyone went with me to the cabin. I asked him why he had held her hand, but he began making false excuses. I then beat him in anger. Office staff also strongly criticised him It may be noted that a video of the assault has emerged, showing a heated argument taking place inside the office. Other office staff also berated the executive engineer, accusing him of holding the female employee's hand and inviting her home for tea. They said he should be ashamed of holding the hand of a woman who was the same age as his daughter. When the executive engineer tried to offer an explanation, the victim slapped him. Woman says- Pressure is being exerted to reach a settlement The woman says that pressure is being exerted on her to reach a settlement in the case. Robbie Gautam, the assistant engineer in the meter department, has also been calling her repeatedly. She has been frightened since the incident. She fears that the accused may enter her rented house one day and do something untoward. She has filed a complaint with the police and sought protection. XEN says- I have been wronged Meanwhile, XEN Manoj Kumar said that false allegations had been levelled against him. "After being so humiliated, I am sitting before you. If I were a thief or a criminal, or had done anything wrong, I would not be sitting before you; I would have left. I am sitting here because I have been wronged-I have not wronged anyone. When I asked them to do the work, they beat me and filmed me." Kotwali in-charge Ramakant Shukla said The female employee has submitted a written complaint. We have sent a team to the spot. Further action will be taken after the investigation.

stories.title: '₹15,000 crore scam in Jal Jeevan Mission':Sanjay Singh says tanks are collapsing, blacklisted firms getting tenders; government shielding them
stories.summary: Aam Aadmi Party Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh has alleged corruption amounting to ₹15,000 crore in work carried out under the Jal Jeevan Mission in Uttar Pradesh. He said government funds had been looted in the name of a scheme to supply water to villages. Around ₹15,000 crore had been withdrawn without any work being carried out. Questioning the department's Principal Secretary, Anurag Srivastava, and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Sanjay Singh said officials involved in corruption were being protected. He also said central investigative agencies were silent on the matter. Sanjay Singh referred to water tanks collapsing in Kasganj, Bareilly, Sitapur and Basti. He alleged a scam in the name of excavation and accused officials of purchasing materials from blacklisted companies. He also questioned how the company that built the tank in Bareilly received a tender worth crores of rupees in Hyderabad. Questions raised over company that donated ₹60 crore to BJP Referring to Nagarjuna Construction Company, Sanjay Singh alleged that the company had donated ₹60 crore to the BJP. He questioned how the company was continuing to receive tenders despite allegations of corruption. He also questioned the role of the Enforcement Directorate. He claimed that on 14 September, the ED had sought a report related to corruption from the department, but no action had been taken so far. He asked why the investigation against the company had not progressed. Government cornered over Gorakhpur incident At the press conference, Sanjay Singh referred to the Gorakhpur incident and expressed his condolences to the victim's family. He alleged that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was trying to provoke the family in the matter. The MP also accused the government of alleging murder without an investigation and politicising the accident. He said that Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav had released CCTV footage related to the incident and expressed his condolences to the victims. Asked about accident involving CM's convoy: What action was taken? Sanjay Singh raised the issue of the accident involving Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's convoy in Arjunganj, Lucknow. He claimed that a mother and her son had died in the accident. He questioned what action had been taken in the case so far. He alleged that no action is taken in cases involving people linked to the BJP, while the police take immediate action in other cases. Also alleges cases and pressure The AAP MP said that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had several cases registered against him. He alleged that the owner of the house where his office is located had also been intimidated and threatened. Sanjay Singh said that those who criticise the government are being targeted.

stories.title: Azam Khan offers Friday prayers with son Abdullah:Says, ‘There is no major issue to talk about’
stories.summary: Azam Khan went to the mosque near his home in Rampur today, Friday, to offer Jumu'ah prayers along with his son, Abdullah Azam, and several associates. He left home at 1:07 p.m. and entered the mosque at around 1:10 p.m. After offering prayers for around 10 minutes, he came out at 1:21 p.m. Two minutes later, Azam Khan and Abdullah Azam reached home. Spoke to media, said, "We spoke at length yesterday" As he came out of the mosque, Azam Khan told media personnel, "We spoke to you at length yesterday. There is no such major issue to discuss." He then went inside the house. People continued to arrive at the house to meet him. Supporters have been arriving in large numbers since his release Azam Khan reached his home at around 9:40 p.m. on Wednesday night after being released from Ghaziabad's Dasna jail. Thousands of supporters and well-wishers arrived to meet him. The stream of people arriving and meeting him continued until around 2 a.m. People continued to arrive to meet him from 10 a.m. on Thursday until 11 p.m. People have been arriving at his residence since Friday morning. Many have already met him, while a large number of people are waiting for their turn. Supporters who have come from distant places are asking about his well-being and also telling him about their problems. Azam Khan is meeting them and enquiring about their well-being. Spent 2.5 hours at Jauhar University as well Azam Khan had also arrived at his dream project, Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, on Thursday night. He spent around 2.5 hours there and took stock of the situation on the campus by speaking to employees and administrative officials. Meetings continued at his residence on Friday even after the Friday prayers. The police also appeared alert regarding security arrangements.

stories.title: Yogi went to his mother’s door seeking alms:She broke down upon seeing him in saffron robes and asked, ‘What was lacking at home?’
stories.summary: Her son, who had been missing for three years, was returning home. His mother was overjoyed on hearing the news. She had several questions running through her mind. How would her son look? What was he doing? She went to the door, but froze at the sight before her. The son she had last seen leaving home in jeans and trousers was now standing in saffron robes. His head was shaved, he wore large earrings in both ears and held a begging bowl in his hand. He had not come for an ordinary meeting. He had come to seek alms from his own mother. This son was none other than the present-day Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. At the time, his name was Ajay Singh Bisht and he had become a monk. Standing before his mother, he said just one thing: “Mother, please give me alms.” Senior journalist Vijay Trivedi has described this emotional incident in his book Yada Yada Hi Yogi. According to him, Ajay arrived outside his house and called out for alms. Hearing the voice, the woman of the house came to the door but could not believe her eyes. Her mouth fell open, but no words came out. Here is what happened next. Mother asked, ‘What was lacking at home that you are begging?’ His mother was unable to understand what she was seeing. Ajay then said, “Mother, please give me alms.” Gathering herself, she asked, “Son, what have you done to yourself? What was lacking at home that you have to beg?” Ajay replied, “Mother, renunciation is my duty. A yogi can satisfy his hunger only through alms. Whatever you give me will help fulfil my purpose.” His mother still hoped that he would come inside the house. She said, “Son, come inside first.” But Ajay firmly refused. He said, “No, Mother. I cannot enter the house or leave this place without receiving alms. Whatever you can give me, please do so. Only then will I leave.” His mother eventually gave in to his insistence. She went inside and brought some rice and money, placing them in Ajay’s bowl. As soon as he received the alms, Ajay turned around and walked away. His mother stood at the doorway with tears in her eyes, watching her son leave. Vijay Trivedi has described the incident in an emotional manner in his book. In his words, as soon as Yogi received the alms, he walked away. His voice echoed towards the clouds gathering near the mountains as he chanted, “Alakh Niranjan!” The sun appeared to be hiding behind the clouds and moving towards the mountains. Its light had become meaningless for the mother. Father searched for six months before learning that his son was in Gorakhpur Yogi Adityanath’s childhood name was Ajay Singh Bisht. He completed his intermediate education in 1989 from Bharat Mandir Inter College in Rishikesh. In the same year, he enrolled for a BSc course at Dr Pitambar Datt Barthwal Himalayan Government Postgraduate College in Kotdwar, Pauri. He completed his studies there in 1992. After this, he enrolled for an MSc in Physics at Gorakhpur University but did not complete the course. It was during this period that he left home. For nearly six months, his family had no idea where Ajay was. His father, Anand Singh Bisht, searched for him everywhere he thought his son might be. However, he could not find him. Later, someone informed the family that Ajay was at the Gorakhnath Peeth in Gorakhpur and had become a monk. The news deeply saddened his father. He wanted to bring his son back home, but Ajay was firm about his decision. Declared successor to Gorakshapeeth on February 15, 1994 Ajay had chosen the path of renunciation. On February 15, 1994, Gorakshapeethadhishwar Mahant Avaidyanath formally declared him his successor following the prescribed rituals. After this, the purpose of his life changed. Away from family and domestic life, he dedicated himself to the Gorakshapeeth and service to society. The same Ajay later became Yogi Adityanath. He was first elected as the MP from Gorakhpur in 1998 and went on to win five consecutive Lok Sabha elections. In 2017, he became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh. Mahant Avaidyanath had reportedly told the family, “You have four sons. Give one of them to us.” The decision was not easy for Yogi’s mother. She kept looking first at Mahant Avaidyanath and then at her son. Eventually, she returned home with her husband. Yogi remained firm on his decision to become a monk Yogi Adityanath faced several challenges in his monastic life but remained committed to his decision. On February 15, 1994, Gorakshapeethadhishwar Mahant Avaidyanath formally declared him his successor following the prescribed rituals. Yogi Adityanath later expressed the purpose of his life through the following Sanskrit verse: Na Tvam Kamayé Rajyam, Na Swargam Na Punarbhavam. Kamayé Duhkh-Taptanam Praninam Arti-Nashanam. Its meaning is: “O Lord, I do not seek power, heaven or liberation. My only wish is to relieve the suffering of living beings who are afflicted by pain.” Yogi Adityanath was first elected as the MP from Gorakhpur in 1998. He went on to win five consecutive Lok Sabha elections and became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in 2017. Even after entering politics, he remained in touch with his family and continued to meet his mother, Savitri Devi. In May 2022, nearly five years after becoming Chief Minister, he visited his native village. He touched his mother’s feet to seek her blessings and asked her, “You recognised me, didn’t you?” He also visited her at AIIMS Rishikesh in June 2024 when she was admitted there. He met her again on February 9, 2026. Following his mother’s death, Yogi Adityanath may once again visit his ancestral village of Panchur. This time, however, his mother will not be waiting for him at the doorstep.

stories.title: Officer informs Yogi of mother's death:Remains composed on stage in Gorakhpur; completes programme before leaving for temple
stories.summary: When the tragic news of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's mother's death arrived, he was addressing a tablet distribution programme in Gorakhpur. Former IAS officer Awanish Awasthi and MP Ravi Kishan, who were present on the stage, shared the news with each other. They began waiting for the Chief Minister to finish his address. He spoke for around 61 minutes. After finishing his speech, he turned around and found Awanish Awasthi behind him. Awasthi whispered something in his ear. It is believed that Awasthi informed him of his mother's death. His facial expression changed for a few moments. However, he did not make his personal grief public. He concluded the programme, took selfies with the children and then left for the temple. He subsequently departed from Gorakhpur for Uttarakhand. This was not the first time in Yogi's life that he had prioritised his public responsibilities amid personal grief. Earlier, in 2020, his father, Anand Singh Bisht, died during the coronavirus pandemic. At that time too, he prioritised his responsibilities as Chief Minister. He could not attend his father's last rites. At the time, Yogi had said that wherever his father might be, he would be blessing him. He had said that his father would also have wished for his son to serve the people of the country and the state. Even at such a time, he gave priority to the concerns of nearly 25 crore people of the state over those of his family. Ravi Kishan paid tribute during the programme Gorakhpur MP Ravi Kishan was also present at the tablet distribution programme. During the event, he shared the news of Savitri Devi's death on social media and paid a heartfelt tribute to her. Despite this, the Chief Minister completed his address and proceeded according to the scheduled programme. When he left home, his mother thought he was going away for a job Yogi Adityanath's original name is Ajay Singh Bisht. When he decided to leave home in 1993, his family thought he was going away for work. The family later learnt that he had taken initiation into the Nath sect and become a monk. When he returned home for the first time after becoming a monk, his mother, Savitri Devi, tried to stop him. She also gave her son fruit, rice and money. However, seeing Ajay's resolve, his mother ultimately blessed him. When he returned to the village five years later, he asked his mother, "You recognised me, didn't you?" Even after becoming Chief Minister, Yogi Adityanath remained emotionally attached to his mother. After becoming Chief Minister for the second time on 3 May 2022, he visited his ancestral village, Panchur, after a gap of nearly five years. After touching his mother's feet to seek her blessings, he smiled and asked, "You recognised me, didn't you?" His mother also said that she recognised him. The meeting was highly emotional. In June 2024, Yogi Adityanath had also visited AIIMS Rishikesh to meet his mother. At the time, Savitri Devi was admitted to the hospital due to health-related problems. Yogi met her and enquired about her well-being. Attention also on whether he will attend the Prime Minister's programme Prime Minister Narendra Modi's programme is scheduled to be held in Lucknow on 21 November. It remains to be seen whether Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will attend it. However, people close to him claim that he may be present at the programme. After receiving news of his mother's death, he may travel today to Panchur, his ancestral village in Pauri Garhwal, Uttarakhand, to pay his last respects.
