Ladakh dialogue to resume after December 15; elected representatives, LAB, KDA to be involved, says chief secretary
Guo Wengui's $67.5 million New York apartment sells for just $8 million to billionaire's son
Neighbours' safety fears put 100-acre Kansas deer-hunting business under zoning rules
stories.summary: A Kansas appeals court has ruled that a 100-acre deer-hunting business run by a couple cannot be treated as an agricultural operation and must obtain a special-use zoning permit. The ruling followed objections from two neighbouring couples, who raised safety concerns about commercial hunting taking place close to their properties.

stories.title: Wisconsin’s $1.1M Barbie Dream House goes under contract
stories.summary: In Hudson, Wisconsin, a charming pink Victorian house constructed in 1900 has made a remarkable transformation from its original Goth style. Recently listed at $1.1 million, the property is now under contract. Featuring seven bedrooms and four bathrooms, the home boasts inviting spaces for gatherings and rentals. The creative homeowner painted it pink and opened it up for various uses, showcasing its versatility.

stories.title: Historic gold dredging damaged a California river used by salmon and steelhead
stories.summary: Major funding has been secured for restoration initiatives aimed at revitalizing the salmon habitat along the Tuolumne River. The project will reestablish 20 acres at La Grange, improving conditions for salmon and steelhead. With new side channels and a historic floodplain, the area will become conducive for salmon spawning. Collaborative efforts by various organizations since 2020 highlight an ongoing dedication to ecological preservation in this region.

stories.title: Titanic survivor Lucy, Lady Duff Gordon’s diamond ring sells for £150,000 after staying in family for generations
stories.summary: A diamond ring belonging to Titanic survivor Lucy, Lady Duff Gordon, sold for £150,000 at auction. The ring was expected to fetch around £80,000 but achieved a much higher final price. Lady Duff Gordon wore the ring during the sinking of the Titanic, which occurred in 1912. Other Titanic memorabilia, including a rare ticket and a postcard, were also sold at the auction.

stories.title: UP polls: SP names four-member panel for seat-sharing talks with Congress from Monday
Phoenix man's 2015 deed had wrong address; court upheld invalidation of rival deeds
stories.summary: A property dispute arose in Phoenix, Arizona, due to a mistake in a property's street address. Robert Olsen received a quitclaim deed from his father, which included incorrect address details but correct property descriptions. Bonitas Casitas LLC later claimed ownership and filed a lawsuit, leading to competing claims over the property. The Arizona Court of Appeals upheld the lower court's ruling, reaffirming the validity of Olsen's original deed.

stories.title: Chef Jose Andres rescues Baltimore's 45-year-old Thanksgiving food tradition
stories.summary: Cynthia Brooks' efforts to continue her mother Bea Gaddy's 45-year-old Thanksgiving food tradition in Baltimore faced a setback after donations fell short, leaving her with only eight turkeys days before the event. Celebrity chef Jose Andres World Central Kitchen and the Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services stepped in with food and resources, helping save the annual dinner that began in 1981.

stories.title: Marshall’s 700 Meals: Family keeps holiday dinners going; her home serves hundreds in need
stories.summary: Carolyn Marshall honors her late mother, Reverend Annie Woodridge, by preparing festive meals for those in need. Overcoming various obstacles, she turned her home into a hub for food prep, drawing support from volunteers who help package and deliver meals. This initiative has blossomed into a cherished family and community effort, reinforcing the values of kindness and remembrance associated with her mother's legacy during the holidays.

stories.title: Adirondack Mountain Rescue: Becky’s arrival triggered search; rescuers found owner alive
stories.summary: When a basset hound named Becky showed up unaccompanied at a mountain lodge, it triggered an urgent search for her owner, a 69-year-old man living with dementia. Spending a night in the frigid wilderness, he was finally located by a hunter. Thanks to Becky's unexpected arrival, the rescue effort commenced quickly, potentially saving her owner's life.

stories.title: China’s secret AI chip hunt: How its spyverse is helping firms bypass US curbs

'Lotus has withered': Akhilesh Yadav's swipe at BJP over 'Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De' slogan
Factory Fire: Seven bodies recovered; about 50 workers remain unaccounted for
stories.summary: A massive fire erupted at a candy factory in Cikande, Indonesia, resulting in the recovery of seven body bags. Authorities reported that around 50 workers remain unaccounted for as rescue efforts continue. The factory owner indicated that approximately 300 workers were present during the incident, which occurred on Saturday evening. Investigation teams are working to determine the cause of the fire while assessing the damage.

stories.title: 'Uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists’: Rahul shares Ardhanareshwar image to target BJP-RSS
'This is new India's response': BJP takes swipe at Pakistan over its minister's applause at Purana Qila
stories.summary: BJP criticized Pakistan by sharing a video of Minister Musadik Malik applauding Indian cultural presentations. This event took place at the three-day SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum hosted in Purana Qila, India. The BJP's montage highlighted contrasting statements made by Pakistani officials regarding Kashmir and India's culture. During the forum, Malik referenced historical figures associated with the Purana Qila fortress.

stories.title: 'Population up in 40 China-border villages': Amit Shah reaches out to Arunachal amid dam protests
stories.summary: Amit Shah unveiled key development initiatives in Arunachal Pradesh as part of the Vibrant Villages Programme, noting a population increase in 40 border villages that has curbed migration. He highlighted the need for self-reliance in food production while assuring local leaders of the Centre's ongoing support for development projects. Additionally, the Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision 2047 was introduced, focusing on future growth strategies.

stories.title: Opposition questions US policy after report flags China’s support to Pakistan during Op Sindoor
Maine court upholds $1 million museum donation 14 years after collector's death
stories.summary: A charitable trust from Maine faced a legal battle over a donation intended for another museum. The Supreme Judicial Court determined that this donation did not violate any prior agreements. While the trust was obligated to fulfill its financial duties to the original museum, it could also manage its assets.

stories.title: Delta Seat Lawsuit: Judge lets claims proceed; airlines may face scrutiny over seat descriptions
stories.summary: Passengers have raised concerns, claiming Delta Air Lines sold them window seats that lacked actual windows. A New York federal judge recently gave the green light for a class-action lawsuit against the airline. This issue emerged when a traveler discovered his seat had no window, prompting Delta to argue that seat assignments aren’t guaranteed. United Airlines is facing similar complaints about windowless seating as well.

stories.title: Karthigai Deepam row: Tamil Nadu govt moves SC against one-time lamp lighting permission atop Thiruparankundram hill
Galloo Island Conservation Easement: TILT protects 1,410 acres; Patten family retains ownership
stories.summary: A landmark conservation deal has been executed for Galloo Island, safeguarding 1,410 acres of pristine land. The Thousand Islands Land Trust has joined forces with Galloo Island Farms and the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation to enforce permanent land use restrictions aimed at preserving the island's ecological integrity.

stories.title: Carnegie Museum will prepare three sauropods in public; researchers study rare skin samples
stories.summary: Three sauropod fossils from Wyoming, nicknamed Daisy, Lucky, and Lucy, are headed for Pittsburgh. A $5 million donation from Ken Griffin will construct a public fossil preparation laboratory at the Carnegie Museum of Natural History. Visitors will be able to observe the cleaning and studying process of these 150-million-year-old dinosaurs. Additionally, research will focus on rare fossilized skin samples associated with the fossils.

stories.title: COP31: Backlash after Türkiye's draft agreement omits fossil fuels
‘Bitten by dogs’: Revanth Reddy’s swipe at dissenting MLAs sparks row in Telangana Congress
'No such proposal': India dismisses reports of seeking Nepal's airspace for military flights
stories.summary: Reports claiming India sought permission from Nepal for military aircraft usage have been clarified as false. Sources have stated that there is no proposal regarding such military access to Bagdogra. This clarification coincides with discussions on air connectivity ahead of Prime Minister Balendra Shah's visit to India. During his visit, Shah will engage in talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to strengthen bilateral relations.

stories.title: Nepal PM Balen Shah arrives in India for first visit; talks with PM Modi on Monday - top developments
'No place for hate in cricket’: Congress leader rejects Masood’s religious bias charge over Siraj
‘Vote Chori’ allegations: Nitin Nabin to lead BJP's Hyderabad rally to counter criticism
stories.summary: BJP president Nitin Nabin will lead a rally in Hyderabad to counter criticism about the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Union minister Bandi Sanjay Kumar supports this event, claiming it to be historic, and anticipates a large turnout. Kumar accused opposition parties, including Congress and BRS, of collaborating to impede BJP's growth in Telangana. He argued that only Indian citizens should have the right to elect their leaders.

stories.title: Sabarimala pilgrimage: Kerala puts security, transport arrangements in place amid devotee rush
stories.summary: The Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa Temple has commenced its much-anticipated annual Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage. This year, the influx of devotees is met with extensive security measures and administrative support. The Kerala government has undertaken significant infrastructure upgrades, enhancing roads and transport services. Throughout the pilgrimage, police will be actively deployed to ensure safety and manage traffic. This first phase will last until December 27, followed by festivities for Makaravilakku.

stories.title: After first-ever foreign office talks, Jaishankar calls for deeper India-Lebanon ties
stories.summary: S Jaishankar, India’s External Affairs Minister, sent heartfelt National Day wishes to Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi and the people of Lebanon. With a focus on deepening diplomatic relations, both countries recently initiated their first foreign office consultations. These discussions emphasized political, security, and economic partnerships, reflecting India's vital contributions to peacekeeping in Lebanon. The intent is to foster stronger ties via consistent high-level dialogues and collaborative efforts.

stories.title: Iran says 428 children killed in two wars, Red Crescent chief calls for independent probe into Minab school attack
US sells Jammeh-linked mansion, returns $2.5 million to Gambian victims
Trump moves to limit congressional scrutiny before Democrats take power of Congress
Flatbush Collapse Lawsuit: Tenant alleges landlord ignored cracks; claims remain unproven
stories.summary: In the wake of a devastating building collapse in Brooklyn that claimed eight lives, a musician has taken legal action against the landlord for ignoring warnings about visible cracks weeks prior. The lawsuit also raises alarms about nearby construction projects lacking proper structural support. Authorities are now probing the oversight of such projects in densely populated neighborhoods, questioning the responsiveness to residents' concerns before the tragic incident occurred.

stories.title: Former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
stories.summary: At a recent auction, a rare lock of George Washington’s hair sold for an impressive $4,000. This fascinating artifact once belonged to John Gadsby, who shared a meal with Washington shortly before his passing. Gadsby’s granddaughter later cherished the lock alongside a portrait of the first president, making it a remarkable piece of history. Notably, Washington's hair has previously commanded prices nearing $40,000 at auctions, alongside other treasured memorabilia.

stories.title: COP31 Talks Remain Divided: Countries review Turkish draft; climate support remains uncertain
stories.summary: At the COP31 climate conference in Turkey, urgent last-minute discussions are underway as Turkish officials unveil a draft agreement amid ongoing disputes regarding fossil fuels. Civil groups voice their frustration over the gradual pace of negotiations, demanding swift action on vital climate challenges. Nations most vulnerable to climate change are advocating for enhanced financial support for recovery and adaptation.

stories.title: Ohio shooting: 3 killed, 1 injured at event venue; two suspects in custody
ICMR: Common antibiotics losing potency as drug resistance rises
Arizona Appeals Court upholds son's 2015 property deed despite address error
stories.summary: In a complex legal battle over a Phoenix property, Robert Olsen asserted his ownership via a deed from 2015. His father's mistake in addressing the deed was countered by the accurate legal description, raising legal challenges. Following a transfer to a business entity in 2019, disputes escalated. Ultimately, the Arizona Court of Appeals affirmed Olsen's deed, nullifying subsequent transfers and clarifying his rightful ownership while clearing invalid records.

India's cyber security agency Cert-IN flags payment fraud in govt-linked platforms
India crosses 1 crore HPV vax in 9 months
California mom sues school over third-grader's report card after 4-0 board vote
Lorri Cramer is known as the Turtle Lady of Manhattan and one summer she took in 680 babies
stories.summary: In the heart of Manhattan, Lorri Cramer, famously known as the Turtle Lady, dedicates her life to rescuing and rehabilitating injured and abandoned turtles. Her mission, not only to restore their health but also to secure safe environments for their future, has brought to light the troubling issue of non-native turtles being wrongfully released into inappropriate habitats.

stories.title: Over 10k postgraduate medical seats in blocked category; govt may review float system
China's support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor impacted Indian planning: US panel
Ohio landlord mistakenly throws away tenant's loved belongings; court upholds $6,000 award
stories.summary: Grace Davis was awarded $6,000 by an Ohio court after her landlord mistakenly discarded her personal belongings. Despite lacking receipts or photographs, she provided a detailed list with estimated values. The landlord's management company challenged the award, arguing that sufficient proof was missing. The appeals court upheld the ruling, stating that the unique nature of the items justified Davis's valuation.

stories.title: More than 8,000 people applied to be NASA astronauts last time and just 10 were picked
stories.summary: NASA is currently accepting applications until December 3, 2026, for aspiring astronauts who dream of exploring outer space. To qualify, applicants must be U.S. citizens possessing a master's degree and relevant experience. Those with medical certifications or extensive flight backgrounds are particularly encouraged to apply. Selected astronauts will undergo rigorous training before embarking on missions to the Moon and Mars, with final candidates expected to be revealed by late 2027.

stories.title: An LA diner that served generations since 1924 shut down in 2025, has reopened under a nonprofit operator
stories.summary: After a lengthy shutdown in 2025 due to property issues, Original Pantry Cafe in Los Angeles has triumphantly reopened! With new management from Hope the Mission, the cafe will utilize its profits to bolster homelessness services. Diners can still indulge in the beloved classic menu while also enjoying fresh additions. Although hours have shifted, there are plans to bring back 24-hour service.

stories.title: As ice receded on a Swiss Alpine pass, archaeologists discovered a 4,000 years old bronze neck ring
stories.summary: A remarkable discovery at Lötschen Pass has unearthed a 4,000-year-old bronze neck ring, making it the first metal artifact found at this significant historical site. While previous discoveries were primarily organic materials preserved in ice, this find suggests that ancient peoples may have practiced mobility through Alpine passes, connecting various regions. Experts speculate that the ring could have served as a ritual offering or token of gratitude.

stories.title: Over 1,000 emergency employees told to work from home after FEMA's Washington DC office was found infested with bed bugs
Asmongold's infamous house controversy returns after GTA 6 livestream with girlfriend Kaise
stories.summary: During a hilarious GTA 6 livestream, Asmongold and Kaise found themselves exploring a disheveled virtual home. Kaise jokingly compared the digital mess to Asmongold's real-life living situation, prompting laughs and nostalgia about Asmongold's cleanliness challenges. Even with improvements noted in 2026, his home remains a hot topic among viewers, fueling the ongoing chatter about his infamous house saga.

stories.title: IShowSpeed teases huge announcement after completing GTA 6 following 52-hour livestream
stories.summary: IShowSpeed celebrated a remarkable achievement by completing GTA 6's story mode in just 52 hours, far surpassing his initial plan of a 12-hour stream. His enthusiasm led him to extend the session, and upon finishing, he expressed heartfelt thanks and hinted at exciting future plans. Although a PS5 crash presented some obstacles, his progress was secure, keeping fans on the edge of their seats for his next move.

stories.title: Indiana man paid $9,489 towards condo debt after $9,213 judgment, but court says he still owes more
stories.summary: Onnie James Florence Jr. encountered significant legal troubles stemming from his failure to pay homeowners' association fees for his condominium in Indiana. After acquiring the unit, he neglected to keep up with payments while residing in Illinois. The Meridian Arch Owners Association successfully secured a default judgment against him for the overdue fees. Despite making a partial payment later, additional fees remained unpaid, prompting ongoing legal action.

stories.title: Dua Lipa's £6.75 million London home renovation set to finish in 2027
stories.summary: Dua Lipa is making waves with the transformation of her Victorian home in Hampstead, which includes an ambitious plan for a luxurious basement pool. After encountering numerous setbacks, the project received the green light to commence construction in 2024. Local environmental concerns have prompted strict adherence to regulations, pushing the anticipated completion to 2027. With an investment estimated at around £3 million, this renovation underscores its intricate and grand vision.

stories.title: Reflecting on Purana Qila's history, Pakistan minister invokes Humanyun & Sher Shah Suri at SCO civilisational dialogue to assert cultural diversity
Scientists flew drones through humpback whales' breath off Canada and sequenced entire genomes
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of St Andrews have pioneered a groundbreaking technique to harness whale DNA through the use of drones. This method captures genetic material from the whales' breath, often referred to as whale snot. Their findings successfully sequenced complete genomes from specimens gathered off the coast of British Columbia.

stories.title: Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren writes to CJI seeking urgent appointment of HC chief justice successor
After Oleshky ceasefire, Melania Trump wants more Ukraine ceasefires before Christmas; Zelenskyy reacts
Texas Fraud Charges: Man allegedly won 70 contracts; counterfeit gear raises concerns
stories.summary: Marcelo Fascino, a 24-year-old from San Antonio, Texas, stands accused of securing more than $1.6 million in federal contracts by deceitfully claiming his business was owned by veterans. He allegedly misrepresented his military background, impersonated government officials, and manipulated suppliers to stifle competition. Furthermore, investigators found he sold counterfeit military gear, mislabeling it as American-made but failing to meet specifications. He faces several charges as the investigation proceeds.

stories.title: Beverly Hills penthouse sells for $21M, with rooftop pool and $18,740 monthly dues
stories.summary: In a stunning real estate move, a penthouse in Beverly Hills has shattered local records by selling for $21 million within just 10 days of listing. Initially priced at $27.5 million, the luxe property ultimately changed hands for 24% less, showcasing its many high-end amenities and hotel-style services for residents. The fortunate buyer also saved over $1 million in transfer taxes by opting for Beverly Hills over Los Angeles.

stories.title: New York couple give 77 acres to protect drinking water and preserve wildlife
stories.summary: Jerry and Joanne Braun donated approximately 77 acres of land to the Town of Newburgh. This land donation aims to protect the drinking water supply sourced from the Chadwick Lake Reservoir. The couple requested reimbursement for subdividing the land, not seeking payment for it. Residents will still have access for passive recreational activities like hiking and enjoying nature.

stories.title: NGT scanner on waste dumping near J&K’s saffron fields
NCB busts interstate pharma drugs syndicate
Ladakh records 70% voting in panchayat polls, 52% in municpal elections
Pak national apprehended along International Border in Jammu
Princeton PhD student, Chinese-born neuroscientist, Eva Yi Xie detained by ICE at airport; DHS says she overstayed visa, lawyers challenge arrest
Brooklyn man removed from US in 1999 wins right to seek sale of home he bought with his wife
stories.summary: Clyde and Verna Nelson's shared Brooklyn home has been at the center of a complicated legal battle following their divorce. Recently, the New York appeals court concluded that Clyde retains the right to initiate the sale of their co-owned property, dismissing Verna's claims that his rights were nullified by their divorce.

stories.title: Michael Sheen-backed children's hospice appeal raises £264,695 in 56 hours
stories.summary: Tŷ Hafan, a remarkable children's hospice located in Wales, has triumphed by surpassing its fundraising goal during the Every Precious Life campaign. Over just two days, generous public donations and match funding totaled an impressive £264,695. The heartfelt appeal, inspired by the touching story of William Watkins, attracted support from various Welsh celebrities. These funds will significantly enhance the hospice's ability to support families facing life-limiting conditions.

stories.title: Glenvar Heights Record Sale: Mansion sells for $13.25 million; nearly doubles in value
stories.summary: In a noteworthy real estate transaction, a luxurious mansion in Glenvar Heights has been sold for an impressive $13.25 million, nearly doubling its original price. Jose Dans Jr. had acquired the property for $7.3 million just in 2024, transforming it into a lavish estate complete with a main house, guesthouse, and cabana.

stories.title: NASA is offering $1 million to anyone who can solve one big problem standing in the way of building a human settlement on the Moon
stories.summary: NASA has launched the Moon Base Challenge, encouraging students to develop solutions for lunar habitation. The initiative offers $1 million in prizes to student teams from high schools and universities. Teams will focus on areas like power generation, life-support systems, and astronaut safety to address the complexities of lunar living. Registration for the competition is open until January 25, 2027, to eligible educational institutions.

stories.title: Humayun, Sher Shah and ‘one fort’: Pakistan minister highlights Purana Quila’s layered history at SCO forum
stories.summary: At the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, hosted at Delhi's Purana Quila, Pakistan's minister Musadik Malik elaborated on the site's historical relevance, paying tribute to Mughal emperor Humayun and Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri. He emphasized the necessity of dialogue among various cultures. The forum, which was kicked off by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, seeks to illuminate India's diverse civilizational heritage via displays and archaeological findings.

stories.title: UK councillor stabbed while protecting council staff member during community work; 32-year-old charged with attempted murder
US man sentenced to life for murdering British woman he groomed online and lured to America
'It changes your body': UK's Princess Catherine opens up about cancer journey for first time
Cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal joins BJP, gets role in OBC morcha executive committee
'Not about food': Owaisi's response to Azam Khan's 'Hyderabadi biryani' jibe
'Don't dislike BJP': Shehzad Poonawalla on quitting politics; calls rift with brother ideological
stories.summary: Shehzad Poonawalla clarified that his exit from active politics is not due to dislike for the BJP. He expressed his ongoing support for Prime Minister Narendra Modi and other BJP leaders. Differences with his brother Tehseen Poonawalla were framed as a clash of principles rather than personal issues. Shehzad emphasized that every person in India should identify as Hindu.

stories.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to reach Delhi on Sunday for his first foreign bilateral trip - what's on agenda
Judge blocks Trump's 250-foot arch near Arlington over lack of congressional approval
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, a federal judge has barred the construction of a controversial monument near Arlington National Cemetery. This decision follows an earlier temporary injunction from another judge, with local government and community members expressing strong concerns regarding the monument's potential effects. The Trump administration aims to appeal this ruling, defending their vision for the monument amidst ongoing debates over presidential authority regarding national landmarks.

stories.title: 94 acres in Massachusetts approved for 26 homes may become a $2 million wildlife conservation area
stories.summary: In Gloucester, Massachusetts, a 26-home housing initiative is meeting resistance from environmental groups. The Essex County Greenbelt intends to purchase the 94-acre woodland to preserve the area's natural environment. Future objectives include establishing walking trails to connect this space with adjacent conservation properties. Though most funding is secured, necessary approvals from the local council are still pending, alongside the open wetlands application by the Conservation Commission.

stories.title: Hilma af Klint painting expected to fetch SEK 8m sells for record SEK 128.9m
stories.summary: A rare painting by Hilma af Klint just sold for a jaw-dropping 128.9 million Swedish kronor at auction! It blew past its original estimate of 6 to 8 million kronor. Painted in 1920 and titled Ser III No. 5, this piece had been with a family for over 30 years and shows off af Klint's unique style and spirituality.

stories.title: 'Goondaism isn't a bug': BJP, BRS attack Congress over Meta office vandalism
stories.summary: Youth Congress workers caused a commotion at the Meta office in Hyderabad, protesting account suspensions affecting their leaders. This vandalism was denounced by leaders from both the BJP and BRS, who claimed it jeopardized the city's business-friendly image. N Ramchander Rao, president of Telangana BJP, criticized Congress for promoting such destructive behavior. Meanwhile, K T Rama Rao of BRS articulated that such incidents erode trust in companies like Meta.

US judge blocks Trump's bid to redirect $1.3 billion in homelessness funding to temporary housing
stories.summary: A federal judge ruled against the Trump administration's plan to change homelessness funding priorities. The judge determined the changes exceeded the authority granted to the Department of Housing and Urban Development. Additionally, the ruling requires the agency to reopen grant applications for organizations seeking funding support. HUD Secretary Scott Turner expressed dissatisfaction with the decision, citing potential disruptions to funding processes.

stories.title: Arizona parents win appeal after HOA blocks gate change for disabled son's golf cart access
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, an Arizona couple, Kevin and Jennifer LoPresto, sought to replace their single gate with a wider double gate to accommodate their disabled son's golf cart. The Wigwam Creek South Community Association rejected their request and pushed for arbitration. However, an appeals court sided with the LoPrestos, allowing their lawsuit against the HOA to continue and awarding them reasonable legal fees for the appeals process.

stories.title: 'Working to suppress India’s rise': US panel report flags China's support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor
stories.summary: In May 2025, China's military support for Pakistan intensified India's security dilemmas. This report reveals Beijing's ongoing strategies aimed at stifling India's strategic advancements through both military and economic tactics. With Pakistan receiving advanced weaponry, India's concerns over a dual-threat scenario have been amplified. The evolving military alliance between China and Pakistan poses greater risks for India moving forward, showcasing a troubling shift in regional security dynamics.

stories.title: 'When you promote rakshasas': BJP MP Nishikant Dubey takes swipe at Meta amid youth Congress protests
'Country's character remains the same': PM Modi praises people for heeding call to not buy gold
MEA clears Taj Mahal visit for Pakistan delegation, no nod for Nizamuddin dargah
stories.summary: A Pakistani delegation, led by Musadik Masood Malik, is in India for the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum. They have been permitted to visit the Taj Mahal, Humayun's Tomb, and Dilli Haat. However, their visit to Nizamuddin dargah has not been security cleared. This visit marks the first by a Pakistani minister to India in three years. The programme emphasizes shared civilizational heritage and cross-cultural engagement among SCO member countries.

stories.title: 'India not a rogue state': Wangchuk claims police deployment withdrawn after court hearing
stories.summary: Sonam Wangchuk accused the Ladakh administration of effectively placing him under house arrest since November 11. He appealed to President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi to uphold constitutional values. Wangchuk expressed concerns about government misuse of police for actions that compromise their duties. He opposed the timing of Hill Council elections, arguing that many residents would be unable to participate.

stories.title: 'Census-related delimitation should be put on hold for 25 years': CPM general secretary MA Baby
'Voices carry no weight': Wangchuk warns Ladakh's alienation could hurt national security during war
Evening newswrap: BJP targets Rahul as Trump hails India's GDP growth; PM Modi recreates 'gamcha' wave in Bihar and more
stories.summary: Donald Trump lauded India's remarkable 7 percent GDP growth recently, allowing the BJP to take jabs at Rahul Gandhi. Meanwhile, PM Narendra Modi unveiled the Nitish Setu in Bihar, evoking memories of past election celebrations. On the global stage, Mexican authorities arrested Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, an FBI's most-wanted fugitive, amid escalating clashes.

stories.title: ‘Thank you Singh Sb’: Sonia Gandhi acknowledges Sikh man's effort to preserve her childhood home
stories.summary: Acquiring Sonia Gandhi's old home in Italy, Sukhdev Singh Kang aspires to establish a museum in her honor. He received public acknowledgment from Sonia Gandhi on social media, expressing his gratitude. The post sparked varied responses, blending admiration with light political humor, and highlighted the Sikh community's fondness for her. Kang considers her recognition of his efforts deeply meaningful and transformative.

stories.title: 'Third contender has arrived': Owaisi says new UP alliance has unsettled Yogi, Akhilesh
stories.summary: Asaduddin Owaisi expressed that the emergence of the 'Samajik Parivartan Morcha' has notably unsettled both Yogi Adityanath and Akhilesh Yadav. With a strategy to become a formidable alternative for the upcoming 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, Owaisi challenged the assertions of vote-splitting, highlighting the Samajwadi Party's mixed performance across different states.

stories.title: Italy's ex-police chief dies amid probe into mafia case cover-up; suicide suspected
'Judgment will create confusion': TN consulting legal experts on SC ruling in Karthigai Deepam row
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government is currently consulting legal experts about the Supreme Court's recent ruling. The judgment allows a one-time lighting of a lamp atop Thirupparankundram hill during Karthigai Deepam. Officials are deliberating on whether to comply with this ruling or challenge it legally. Social justice minister Vanni Arasu has expressed strong opposition to the judgment.

stories.title: PM Modi launches projects worth Rs 34,000cr in Bihar; says state now known for development, not scams
Prove you're alive with a selfie: What pensioners need to know about Jeevan Pramaan
stories.summary: The Digital Life Certificate system in India provides a hassle-free way for pensioners to verify their identities annually through a simple selfie. Utilizing Aadhaar authentication via the Jeevan Pramaan and UIDAI’s AadhaarFaceRD apps, this initiative especially helps elderly and physically challenged individuals avoid travel difficulties. As part of a broader campaign to promote this service among pensioners, they must verify their information's accuracy before submission.

stories.title: NY woman’s 20-year apartment fight continues after court rejects landlord’s commercial lease claim
stories.summary: A landlord's attempts to reclaim a Manhattan apartment are hindered due to ongoing claims about rent stabilization. E. Terese Carpenter has resided in the unit for over 20 years, despite the existence of a commercial lease. The appeals court identified unresolved issues regarding the actual use of the apartment and the landlord's awareness of the situation.

stories.title: 'First violence, now poisonous liquor': Rahul Gandhi accuses Manipur BJP govt of negligence over spurious alcohol deaths
HC pulls up UP govt over registration of FIRs under law declared 'stillborn' by SC
Trump, Xi, Putin agree on UN reforms: What it means for India's permanent UNSC seat bid
Bangladesh wage protests: Clashes erupt between garment workers and police, dozens of factories shut
stories.summary: Tensions soared in Ashulia as garment workers rallied for higher wages, leading to confrontations with law enforcement. To maintain control, the police deployed tear gas to break up the protest after production was halted. Reports revealed that more than 50 factories chose to close temporarily amid the unrest, with indefinite shutdowns and sit-ins occurring in various industrial areas. This turmoil highlights the ongoing struggle for improved pay and working conditions.

stories.title: Pennsylvania county sold home for $109,000 after notices went to dead owner; court sets sale aside
stories.summary: A Pennsylvania appeals court recently ruled to cancel a tax sale of a home in Garnet Valley. The tax sale occurred due to the county's failure to notify the correct property owner about unpaid taxes. Bonnie Wilson's home was sold despite her and her son Kevin both being deceased. The appeals court emphasized the need for tax bureaus to investigate further when notices are returned.

stories.title: China-Pakistan ties raise two-front conflict risk for India: US report
stories.summary: A US congressional commission has warned that China's growing military support for Pakistan could heighten the risk of a two-front conflict for India. In its report, it urged Washington to deepen defence cooperation with New Delhi, particularly in the Indian Ocean, including intelligence sharing and joint tracking of Chinese naval and submarine movements. It also flagged Beijing's expanding strategic presence in the region.

stories.title: 'Nitish conceived the project': Prashant Kishor's rare praise for former Bihar CM with a jibe at BJP, RJD
Ex-Trump press secretary Katie Zacharia under probe for posing as lawyer without passing bar
'Will find way forward through dialogue': Amit Shah assures Arunachal locals amid Siang dam protests
7 killed as tribal feud over forest ownership triggers gunfight in Pakistan
stories.summary: Seven people were killed in a gunfight between the Gilal and Kaloch tribes over a decades-old forest ownership dispute in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, PTI reported, quoting police. The clash took place in Battagram district on Thursday night, leaving four members of the Gilal tribe and three from the Kaloch tribe dead. Repeated efforts to resolve the dispute have failed.

stories.title: Congress vs Congress over Siraj: Party MP tells Imran Masood to 'not interfere'
stories.summary: Congress MP Ranjeet Ranjan advised fellow MP Imran Masood to keep politics and sports separate. Masood had criticized the selection process after Mohammed Siraj was excluded from the Test squad. Siraj, India's top wicket-taker in the current World Test Championship cycle, was notable for his performance.

stories.title: Bangladesh violence: Fresh arson attacks reported as unrest continues amid Sheikh Hasina's return plans
stories.summary: Tensions continue to rise in Bangladesh as fresh arson attacks erupt in response to Sheikh Hasina's anticipated return. In an effort to restore peace following violent incidents that claimed multiple lives, paramilitary forces have been mobilized. Communication services in her hometown have resumed after disruptions caused by the unrest, while over a hundred Awami League members have been arrested in Dhaka.

stories.title: PM Modi inaugurates Nitish Setu in Bihar, recreates 'poll victory' moment with 'gamcha' wave
More than 100,000 strangers have shared handwritten stories anonymously
stories.summary: More than 100,000 anonymous handwritten stories have been shared in The Strangers Project since its inception. Individuals recount personal experiences centered on themes such as love, loss, and hope. Brandon Doman founded the project in 2009 to create a space for these shared experiences. The Strangers Project is currently located at the World Trade Center Oculus in New York City.

stories.title: NJ appeals $11.25M verdict for woman handcuffed during stroke by trooper
stories.summary: In a tragic turn of events, Cheryl Lynn Rhines suffered a severe stroke while driving and was mistakenly arrested for intoxication. The responding trooper overlooked the critical nature of her medical emergency, causing significant delays in her treatment. This negligence resulted in lasting brain injuries and communication issues for Rhines.

stories.title: CBI Recovers Cash and jewellery from CGST Superintendent home
Balochistan shutdown: Markets shut across Quetta as alliance protests rising inflation, insecurity
stories.summary: A significant shutdown swept across Quetta and several districts in Balochistan on Thursday, driven by widespread protests led by the All Parties Alliance. The strike aimed to highlight urgent issues such as deteriorating law and order, soaring unemployment rates, and rampant inflation. Major commercial hubs faced complete shutdowns, resulting in major disruptions.

stories.title: Taj Mahal, Humayun's Tomb on wish list as Pakistan minister visits India; what Centre said on travel curbs
stories.summary: Pakistan minister Musadik Malik, in India for the SCO meeting, expressed a desire to visit the Taj Mahal and other historic landmarks. The Centre clarified that visiting ministers faced no travel restrictions. Malik also stressed the importance of cultural exchanges and dialogue in improving regional ties amid strained India-Pakistan relations following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.

stories.title: 'Look beyond what an image shows': Hindu seer's open letter to Rahul, Priyanka over Shiva-Parvati post
Army jawan found dead near Jammu bus stand under suspicious circumstances; probe launched
Florida battles historic flooding as storms move further north
stories.summary: In Central Florida, residents face rising water levels from recent heavy rain, prompting evacuation alerts. Authorities urge those living by the St. Johns River to brace for potential evacuations as flooding disrupts Thanksgiving festivities. Emergency responders are tirelessly aiding those stranded in waterlogged neighborhoods, while meteorologists predict that both heavy rainfall and flooding risks will persist for the foreseeable future.

'Main chunauti ko chunauti diye bina reh nahi sakta’: PM Modi at IIT Kharagpur’s 75th anniversary
'PM-HM jodi still searching for majority': Congress takes dig at Centre over delimitation bill
Pregnant at 34 weeks, New York nurse completes all seven major marathons
stories.summary: Deirdre Keane, an inspiring nurse practitioner from New York, achieved a remarkable feat in 2026 by completing all seven World Marathon Majors while pregnant. Approaching her training thoughtfully after learning about her pregnancy, she ran the New York City Marathon at 34 weeks, pushing boundaries she once thought were fixed.

stories.title: Mexican cartel leaders, 19 others indicted in US over drug and arms trafficking
stories.summary: In a significant legal move, a federal grand jury has charged leaders of the La Nueva Familia Michoacana cartel along with 19 associates. Key allegations against them include drug trafficking and weapons smuggling. Prominent figures Johnny Hurtado Olascoaga and Jose Alfredo Hurtado Olascoaga are on the run, purportedly using violence and bribery to grow their criminal empire and engage in human smuggling.

stories.title: After his wife Susan died, Warren Lewis learned her body cannot be donated to science because of this
stories.summary: Susan Lewis's noble desire to donate her body to science was thwarted by a miscommunication. After her passing, her husband, Warren Lewis, tirelessly advocated for revisions to the university's body donation policy. This advocacy birthed a collaboration with Macquarie University, enabling weekend donations and ensuring that future donors' wishes are honored, despite bureaucratic hurdles. Susan's journey underscores the complexities surrounding body donations in Australia.

stories.title: Federal Lawsuit: Maine family challenges rooster fines; alleges free-speech violations
stories.summary: David and Sara LeBlanc have taken legal action against Ogunquit, Maine, after being penalized for setting up rooster sculptures outside their home. These sculptures symbolize support for their daughter Pyper, who is autistic and adores roosters. The town has classified the sculptures as commercial advertising for their restaurant, Omelette Factory, and although the couple has removed them, local residents have rallied to display the sculptures in unity.

stories.title: Air Niugini plane makes emergency landing in Philippines, all 146 safe
stories.summary: An incident occurred involving an Air Niugini aircraft with 146 individuals on board that indicated possible engine fire. The flight performed an emergency landing at Davao International Airport shortly after midnight. Passengers and crew were safely evacuated via emergency slides, with no injuries reported. Other flights at the airport were briefly suspended for safety checks and to assist those on the aircraft.

stories.title: Negligence Lawsuit: Mother seeks $8.7 million after son loses eye; Oregon age rules face scrutiny
stories.summary: A negligence lawsuit has emerged following a tragic e-bike accident involving a 14-year-old boy during a birthday sleepover hosted by Tessa and Matthew Cohen. The allegations claim that the Cohens provided electric bikes without adequate supervision or safety protocols. As a result, the boy sustained life-altering injuries, requiring significant medical attention. The lawsuit demands $8.7 million in damages to address his painful recovery and its long-term consequences.

stories.title: 'Apologise for 1962 humiliation': Rijiju fires 4 questions at Rahul over 'compromised PM' jibe
Himalayan marmot droppings could help track climate change
Illinois couple loses appeal over fence installed after trespassing and car theft
NMC hikes appeal fee for medical colleges up to six-fold; private institutions to pay Rs 3.54 lakh
stories.summary: Medical colleges in India will face significantly higher appeal fees to challenge National Medical Commission's decisions. Government institutions must now pay Rs 1.77 lakh for appeals, while private institutions will pay Rs 3.54 lakh. The new fee structure is effective for appeals relating to the 2026-27 academic year onwards. The previous uniform fee of Rs 59,000 has been revised to these new amounts.

stories.title: NMC plans to simplify rules for Indians who study medicine abroad
India, France condemn Pahalgam, Red Fort terror attacks at counter-terror meet
Amit Shah: PM used govt instruments to improve lives
Pakistan attending SCO event won't dilute IWT stand: Govt

No China input yet on GoPro cam used during Pahalgam attack: NIA
stories.summary: NIA director general Rakesh Aggarwal reported that a GoPro camera linked to the Pahalgam attack, which resulted in 26 fatalities including 25 tourists, remains unclaimed by China. This camera was lost in July 2025 when authorities neutralized the terrorists. Meanwhile, allegations by Mathew VanDyke regarding his treatment in custody haven’t been addressed in court. The investigation into the camera's origins continues as officials await China's response.

stories.title: PM Modi’s remark on jobs & wages a confession: Congress
North Carolina couple noticed kitchen floor dipping weeks after moving in; court rejects their claims
stories.summary: After moving into their new home, Nate and Christine Holton noticed troubling dips in their kitchen floor. Despite reaching out to the builder, concerns about their foundation emerged again over time. In January 2025, they pursued a lawsuit claiming construction defects, but the court deemed their claims time-barred. Ultimately, their assertions of negligence and deceit went unproven, as they couldn't establish additional financial harm.

stories.summary: India Announces 1st Official Trip To Start Tomorrow

UK retailer fined £720,000, ordered to refund 40,000 shoppers over charge
ED challenge to bail doesn't get listed for 3 years, SC smells a rat

stories.title: Louisiana farmer wins 13-year land dispute after neighbours clear trees; court awards him $59,966
stories.summary: In a landmark ruling, Louisiana farmer Benjamin Lee Bird emerged victorious in a lengthy 13-year battle over a disputed land strip. The court upheld his ownership, leading to a damages award against his neighbours for their actions, which included tree removal and altering drainage systems on Bird's land. The appeals court confirmed his rights, adjusting the compensation to $59,966.

stories.title: Indian Team leaves for Bangladesh for talks on Ganga water
Streamer Completion Race: Two creators finish GTA 6; marathon ending draws spoiler criticism
stories.summary: BrycexD became the first streamer to complete GTA 6 in 39 hours and 38 minutes, with iShowSpeed finishing second after a 52-hour marathon. Both pushed through without sleep, but their experiences differed. While BrycexD planned to replay the game, iShowSpeed was left emotional after receiving an ending that disappointed him.
