NIA seeks UAE's cooperation in probe of attack on Indian flydubai pilot Machchhar
SC allows lighting of lamp at Deepathoon as one-time measure
Melania Trump on life as first lady, White House renovations, marriage to Donald Trump and son Barron
stories.summary: Melania Trump opens up about her life as first lady in a new docuseries, discussing White House renovations, her passion for interior design and the responsibilities of managing the presidential residence. She also speaks about her marriage to Donald Trump, how they respect each other’s individuality and her approach to raising their son, Barron.

stories.title: Louisiana couple's $429,000 home defects case revived against property brokerage by appeals court
stories.summary: A couple in Louisiana filed a lawsuit against the sellers and brokerage after discovering defects post-purchase. They claimed that significant issues, such as a rotted air pipe and rodent remains, were concealed. The court ruled that the relationship between the agent and brokerage required further examination. While the jury dismissed some claims, questions about the agent's status remain unresolved.

stories.title: Fake university list grows from 20 to 32 in 3 years, 18 old names still on it
A Virginia woman who looks after 27 nest boxes near her home has helped 1,674 baby bluebirds take flight since 2006, checking every box each week from April to July and logging every single egg
stories.summary: Cathi Morrison has dedicated her efforts to monitoring 27 bluebird nesting boxes since 2006. She documents every nesting attempt, egg, and fledgling, contributing valuable data to conservation organizations. Morrison highlights the challenges young bluebirds face, including predators and extreme weather conditions. She emphasizes the importance of maintaining an environment that supports insect populations necessary for bluebird survival. Morrison encourages community involvement in supporting local bird populations and creating healthier ecosystems.

stories.title: Empires changed maps, but dialogues changed world: PM Modi at SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum
Consider law to curb marriage between relatives: SC to government
Platte County treasurer faces lawsuit over alleged $1.3 million bank transaction
stories.summary: Kimberlie Miller has initiated legal action against Treasurer Chris Kendall and Platte County following her dismissal. She asserts that her firing occurred after she flagged a suspicious transaction linked to a $1.3 million cheque directed to an unauthorized account. Miller's lawsuit encompasses various claims, including discrimination and wage discrepancies, with a hearing set for February 2027.

stories.title: Kansas family harvesting crops 13 miles north of Syracuse filmed a rare piebald black bear with patchy light and dark fur, the first a state wildlife biologist says he has ever seen in Kansas.
stories.summary: A family in Kansas spotted a rare piebald black bear while harvesting crops in their field. The unusual bear had distinct patches of light and dark fur, surprising wildlife experts. Typically, black bears in the region are known to have cinnamon-colored fur. Wildlife biologists explained that young bears often disperse in search of food and territory.

stories.title: Brazil's imprisoned ex-president Jair Bolsonaro taken to hospital with 'severe abdominal pain'
stories.summary: Jair Bolsonaro has been hospitalized due to intense abdominal pain linked to his declining health condition. Concerned for his father’s well-being, Carlos Bolsonaro has voiced worries over the treatment and persistent psychological pressure. After sustaining multiple stab wounds, Bolsonaro is serving a lengthy prison sentence for alleged coup attempts. In a related note, his eldest son Flavio faced electoral defeat and subsequently relocated to the United States with his family.

stories.title: First regular India-Nepal passenger train to link birthplaces of Lord Ram and Mata Sita
stories.summary: Indian railways is set to launch a direct passenger train service between Ayodhya and Janakpur after two years. This new connection will promote religious tourism by linking Lord Ram's and Mata Sita's birthplaces. The inaugural run is scheduled for November 23, with the train operating weekly. Passengers will travel around 604 kilometers in approximately 19 hours with customs clearance aboard.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Michael Jackson: "You never know how long you have with someone, so don't..."
Australian data centre with Anthropic faces 595 objections over power, water, traffic and noise
stories.summary: Residents of Queensland are raising alarms over a proposed data centre that may significantly impact their community. Concerns have been voiced regarding heightened water usage, the strain on electricity supply, increased noise levels, and road infrastructure challenges. Zerra DC, the developer, is committed to engaging with locals and addressing their issues. The ambitious plan to establish one of Australia's largest computing facilities is now pending necessary planning and regulatory approvals.

stories.title: 'Look at India', 'country of 2nd chances': 10 takeaways from Trump's White House presser
stories.summary: Donald Trump championed his administration's initiatives and signaled a willingness to partner with Democrats on key issues. He lauded the economic prospects of the Quad alliance, particularly India's remarkable growth figures. Discussing Iran, Trump called for clear and acceptable terms in any agreements. Supporting former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, he recommended enforcing a tax on offshore data centers.

stories.title: Florida couple find 15-foot, 134-pound python during late-night dog walk
stories.summary: Late one night, while taking their dog for a stroll in Chase Preserve, Florida, a couple stumbled upon a massive Burmese python. Residents soon gathered, alarmed by the sight of the snake lurking in the bushes, prompting a call for assistance. A local trapper swiftly captured the hefty 134-pound female python in only three minutes.

stories.title: Ed Sheeran's former Brooklyn Heights rental hits market for $12.5 million
US feels like a golden prison: Google engineer on H-1B visa says he's moving to the UK without a job, says he hasn't traveled outside US for 18 months out of fear
Tech millionaire spends $14,400 to hire 30 protesters to picket Saks after his mother was fired from the store five days after a customer allegedly punched and kicked her
Eric Schmidt lists Malibu beachfront home for $37.5M alongside second Google listing
Amazon communities have a complicated relationship with giant anacondas; a 2025 study explores why some people fear them while others live alongside them
stories.summary: Communities in the Lower Amazon have a multifaceted relationship with giant anacondas, dealing with folklore and livestock concerns. The presence of these snakes is often rooted in local myths, but practical encounters create conflicts. Killing anacondas frequently stems from protecting domestic animals rather than pure fear. Researchers indicate that the people's perceptions of the snakes have altered due to economic considerations.

stories.title: FBI's Winter SHIELD and Riptide: Kash Patel says 750 companies contacted, 200 cybercriminals arrested as US steps up cyber defence
Quote of the day by Princess Diana: "People think that at the end of the day a man is the only..."
Denver detective accused of DUI, fleeing crash in city SUV; deputies stop, identify her at gunpoint
stories.summary: A Denver police detective has been charged with DUI and hit-and-run after allegedly crashing a city-provided SUV into a parked car in an Arapahoe County neighbourhood and fleeing. Deputies stopped the damaged vehicle at gunpoint after it travelled nearly a mile on three tyres and a rim. The detective later resigned from the department.

stories.title: Sara Bareilles helps raise $1.8m for New York public radio at gala
stories.summary: Sara Bareilles graced the stage at a New York City gala, successfully raising over $1.8 million for New York Public Radio. The event gathered more than 500 attendees to emphasize the vital role of independent journalism and cultural initiatives. This yearly gala underscores the community's commitment to maintaining strong public broadcasting, with funds aimed at bolstering NYPR's diverse offerings, including news coverage and classical music shows.

stories.title: US postal inspector jailed for 40 months after stealing $340,000 from elderly scam victims
stories.summary: Scott Steven Kelley, a former US Postal Inspector, received a 40-month prison sentence for stealing money from elderly victims. He embezzled over $340,000 by intercepting postal packages meant for fraud victims. The money was used for personal expenses, including home improvements and family vacations. Federal authorities have worked to identify the victims and ensure restitution.

stories.title: 'Don't reduce it to bilateral': Pakistan minister in Delhi for SCO ducks question on terror
stories.summary: Musadik Masood Malik, the Pakistani minister, participated in the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. He acknowledged India's suffering from terror attacks while avoiding direct questions about terror networks in Pakistan. Malik emphasized the importance of an evidence-based mechanism to address terrorism and restore trust between the countries. He advocated for regional cooperation rather than focusing solely on bilateral disputes between India and Pakistan.

stories.title: NIA probes 'Indian footprint' in flydubai pilot stabbing case, seeks UAE assistance
stories.summary: The National Investigation Agency is currently probing the shocking mid-air stabbing of Captain Smit Machchhar, where an Omani first officer allegedly attempted to hijack a flydubai flight. Authorities are now exploring any possible Indian links to the suspect. Additionally, they've sent a request for legal assistance to the UAE to secure important documents while delving into the deeper conspiracy surrounding this alarming incident.

stories.title: 'Voice of every village': Rahul attacks BJP after Congress's Rajasthan panchayat poll gains
North Carolina owner wins appeal over city's immunity defence in 361-home flooding dispute
stories.summary: A North Carolina property owner has won a significant legal victory against the City of Concord in her lawsuit. This case involves stormwater flooding allegedly caused by a nearby residential development, leading to property damage. The North Carolina Court of Appeals ruled that the city cannot claim governmental immunity at this stage. The decision allows the property owner to continue her claims of negligence, trespass, and nuisance.

stories.title: A retired architect in Dicmo, Croatia, spent nearly 50 years collecting carved stones from his family’s land, and archaeologists now say they belonged to a lost 1,900-year-old Roman arch built for Trajan
stories.summary: Archaeological excavations in Dicmo, Croatia, have revealed a stunning Roman triumphal arch dedicated to Emperor Trajan, believed to have stood for nearly 1,900 years. Božo Kokan's efforts in gathering stones from his relatives' land played a pivotal role in identifying this significant find. The site boasts intricate Roman architectural features and elements like the imperial eagle, along with signs of a larger Roman community, underscoring the area’s extensive historical narrative.

stories.title: Rao and Patil: The two desis behind Anthropic's bang and buck
At least 36 trains robbed; 14 accused in $22.5 million Nike cargo theft racket in US
stories.summary: Fourteen people have been indicted in the US for allegedly stealing over $22.5 million worth of cargo from at least 36 freight trains in Southern California. The stolen goods included Nike sneakers and Milwaukee tools, which were allegedly resold on the black market. Investigators claim the gang used social media to coordinate thefts and sales.

stories.title: Ex-IAF vice-chief slams UK report claiming India has 32 Rafales instead of 36 as 'patently false'
Government hails growing trust as US navy vessel undergoes repair in India
Government avoids war of words, fears extradition push is a delaying tactic
stories.summary: Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has leveled serious allegations at India and the Awami League, previously led by Sheikh Hasina, suggesting they are stoking discord. The Indian government refrains from offering comments, emphasizing its commitment to fostering a positive relationship with Bangladesh. Furthermore, concerns arise over Hasina's passport application, which Dhaka rejected amid concerns regarding its authenticity.

stories.title: Begg Receives Tusk Honour: Begg becomes first woman to win; Niassa teams gain recognition
stories.summary: Dr. Colleen Begg has received the prestigious 2026 Prince William Award for Conservation in Africa, reflecting her commitment to safeguarding wildlife in Mozambique's Niassa Special Reserve. For over twenty years, she has worked alongside her husband to establish the Niassa Carnivore Project, focusing on large carnivore conservation through community engagement. This accolade underscores the vital role of sustainable practices and local leadership in conservation efforts.

stories.title: California 'lost shark guy', 68, names 56 species, hunts fish unseen since 1926
stories.summary: For decades, marine biologist David Ebert has journeyed to fish markets worldwide, uncovering the mysteries of sharks and rays. His remarkable contributions include documenting 56 new species, revealing the astonishing diversity of marine life. Ebert passionately advocates for recognizing the neglected shark species, underlining the integral role they play in maintaining healthy ocean ecosystems and the threats they face from human activities.

stories.title: Jensen Huang told one employee his mother should have aborted him; yelled at another that he would remove the top of their head and urinate on their brain: NYT investigation
stories.summary: Jensen Huang believed that his bullying had entertainmet value and it was practice inflicted on newcomers to test their resilience as to whether they could withstand Huang's episodes of public humiliation. Huang dismissed all HR complaints and said that his employees became so rich that money was no more a motivating factor for them and that's why he had to resort to bullying to push them towards more efficiency.

stories.title: Pahalgam attack: Beijing yet to share info on how GoPro camera US supplied to China was found on terrorists
'No complaint in Tihar': NIA chief rejects US citizen VanDyke's claim of torture in jail
stories.summary: Mathew VanDyke, an American citizen, has accused Indian authorities of custodial torture during his time in Tihar jail. Despite the National Investigation Agency (NIA) chief asserting that VanDyke did not report any mistreatment while in judicial custody, he was arrested alongside six Ukrainians for allegedly training insurgents in Myanmar and unlawfully entering India.

stories.title: Newly released emails show how Trump lawyer urged DOJ to pardon 2020 fake electors before trials; state charges unaffected
'Compromised' PM remark: BJP hits back at Rahul Gandhi with AI image of LoP serving water to Trump
stories.summary: Amidst the backdrop of political tensions, BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia fired back at Rahul Gandhi's criticisms about India's lack of representation at the SCO summit with an AI-generated image. Gandhi's remarks targeted Prime Minister Modi's absence, leading BJP officials to highlight India's proactive engagement in international gatherings like BRICS and G20, while scrutinizing the previous Congress-led government's foreign relations strategy.

stories.title: 'Partnership will define 21st century': US ambassador Sergio Gor
stories.summary: During his recent visit to the USS George Washington, US Ambassador Sergio Gor emphasized the crucial defense partnership between India and the US, predicting it will shape the 21st century for both nations. Highlighting President Donald Trump's commitment, Gor pointed to advancements in technology access and military training for India, alongside joint military exercises that showcase increasing interoperability and strategic ties.

stories.title: Russia's war spills into Poland as missile crashes near Ukraine border
'Fatal Attraction' feud: Former Columbia professor seeks $10 million from ex-lover who accuses him of rape
US Senate passes energy bill requiring AI data centres to pay more for grid upgrades
stories.summary: The US Senate has passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, designed to bolster energy infrastructure significantly. This new law mandates that large AI data centers play a larger role in funding electricity grid improvements. Environmental advocates raise alarms over potential threats to regulatory controls and tribal rights.

stories.title: Dog helps find missing owner, alerts lodge staff; rescuers find 69-year-old alive after freezing night
stories.summary: Becky, the brave Basset hound, made her unexpected debut at a mountain lodge, alone and worried. Staff were quick to act, involving rescue teams equipped with drones and bloodhounds in the search for her missing owner. After enduring a frostbite-inducing night in the wilderness, he was located thanks to his loyal companion's timely arrival. Without Becky leading the way, the outcome could have been much grimmer for him.

stories.title: Teen Michigan student develops microplastics removal system that is 90% cheaper
Rajasthan panchayat election results 2026: 5 takeaways as Congress beats BJP; RLP makes big gains
stories.summary: In the 2026 Rajasthan panchayat elections, Congress emerged victorious, securing thousands of seats and highlighting its political strength. The BJP, on the other hand, faced significant setbacks in key regions, raising questions about its grassroots appeal. Additionally, the Rashtriya Loktantrik Party's gains signify a shifting political landscape, while independent candidates' wins hint at emerging local dynamics. Overall, the results pose serious challenges for the BJP as assembly elections approach.

stories.title: 'Will put him out of circulation': NIA chief welcomes Canada naming Goldy Brar most-wanted criminal
stories.summary: The Canadian government has put a $250,000 bounty on gangster Satinderjeet Singh, known as Goldy Brar, who is wanted for first-degree murder connected to a recent homicide in Winnipeg. Brar, who is also on the FBI's Top 10 Most Wanted list with a whopping $1 million reward, poses a serious threat as he is armed and dangerous. His capture would significantly aid ongoing investigations into organized crime activities.

stories.title: 'Need to treasure those': SC refers 135-year-old library relocation case to CJI; no shifting of books for now
'Daddy, please don’t shoot me': US man kills wife, three young children before shooting self
‘Dialogue on civilisation, not war’: PM Modi's message at SCO summit - top quotes
India unveils first indigenous H5N1 vaccine to protect chickens from bird flu
Ohio court overturns divorce deal after husband alleges wife hid $443,000 in personal spending
stories.summary: An Ohio businessman, Jason G. Jardine, successfully appealed a divorce settlement ruling due to undisclosed expenditures by his ex-wife, Crystal T. Jardine. The Ohio Court of Appeals determined that the original decision lacked a hearing concerning fraud allegations. Jason claimed Crystal obtained significant undocumented funds during their divorce, complicating their dispute over funeral home management and associated receiver fees. The court has mandated further hearings to address these financial matters.

stories.title: Arizona toddler, 2, wanders into desert wearing only a diaper; volunteer finds her alive under bush
stories.summary: A two-year-old girl named Vella Campillo vanished from her home in Eloy, Arizona, prompting an extensive search by volunteers and officials in the chilly desert for several hours. After more than five hours of searching, neighbor Jay Stewart found her hiding under a bush. Emergency responders ensured the girl's safety and promptly took her to a hospital for evaluation. Authorities classified this incident as a case of a wandering child.

stories.title: Florida mom buys 480 toilet paper rolls, earns miles for daughter's flight home
stories.summary: In an effort to minimize travel costs, Florida resident Michelle Jolene bought toilet paper through an airline shopping website, amassing 8,500 airline miles. These miles allowed her daughter to fly home for Thanksgiving from Washington, D.C. As airfares continue to climb, families face challenges with ticket prices and possible cancellations during the holiday rush. Michelle's inventive method showcases the potential for everyday spending to alleviate travel expenses.

stories.title: Mississippi politician's Nike sneaker idea expands nationwide for 2027 high school valedictorians
stories.summary: Nike has announced plans to reward high school valedictorians with custom Air Force 1 sneakers across the United States. This initiative originated from a request by incoming Mississippi senator Scott Colom to honor state valedictorians. Following Colom's appeal, Nike decided to expand the program to include all eligible students nationwide. Colom also suggested that the sneakers could feature historical figure Hiram Revels to connect education and Mississippi's history.

stories.title: No proof that assault was motivated by bias: Indian-origin Samit Apurva Patel, who attacked Somali-American Uber driver, released from jail; placed on electronic home monitoring
Owaisi-Azad alliance looks strong on paper, but Akhilesh Yadav has little to fear: 5 reasons why SP may not be worried
stories.summary: The Owaisi-Chandrashekhar Azad alliance may look like a major threat to Akhilesh Yadav's PDA formula, but the reality in Uttar Pradesh tells a different story. From Akhilesh's efforts to broaden the SP's support base to Azad's challenge from Mayawati and Owaisi's limited success in UP, we examine five reasons why the new Dalit-Muslim alliance may not be as big a worry for the SP chief as it appears.

stories.title: Evening Newswrap: Congress hits back at PM Modi's 'hunger' jibe; NCB busts US-bound opioid pipeline & more
Mamdani unveils $290m plan to close Rikers Island by 2032, five years past legal deadline
stories.summary: In a bold move, New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has unveiled a strategic initiative aimed at closing Rikers Island jail by 2032. The plan emphasizes the establishment of four smaller jails across various boroughs, with a focus on slashing the jail population. Key investments in mental health services and job training are central to this effort, as the city seeks to reform the beleaguered jail system.

stories.title: Another Parliament showdown loading over delimitation bill? Congress says INDIA bloc, including DMK, NCP-SP, united
stories.summary: The Congress party is voicing concerns about the government's insufficient communication about the upcoming delimitation exercise. In a show of solidarity, leaders from the INDIA coalition, including DMK and NCP-SP, have come together on vital demands for transparent consultations. Congress emphasizes the importance of maintaining existing Lok Sabha seats and ensuring an equitable distribution among states during the process.

stories.title: 'Clueless on geopolitics': BJP hits back at Rahul Gandhi over 'compromised PM' charge
‘All our relationships will improve’: Pakistan minister in Delhi for SCO summit
'Baseless lawsuits': MEA rejects US court summonses to NSA Ajit Doval
stories.summary: The ministry of external affairs has dismissed US court summonses aimed at Ajit Doval and Samant Goel, linked to a civil lawsuit by the pro-Khalistan group Sikhs for Justice. Although a US district court sought to serve these summonses, they had to resort to alternative methods after the initial refusal.

stories.title: SpiceJet cash crunch hits flight operations; Delhi airport issues advisory for flyers
Why can people with low bad cholesterol still have heart attacks?
stories.summary: A study has uncovered a concerning relationship between lipoproteins, particularly triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and lipoprotein(a), and the risk of developing coronary artery disease. Analyzing nearly 3,000 blood proteins, it revealed key differences in protein patterns compared to LDL cholesterol. The results underscore the importance of inflammation and vascular changes in coronary artery disease progression, indicating the necessity for additional research to better understand these proteins' influence on cardiovascular health.

stories.title: Centre moves to tighten controls on antibiotic manufacturing, bulk drug trade
stories.summary: The Centre plans to introduce stringent regulations on antibiotic manufacturing and distribution as a strategy to counteract antimicrobial resistance. Newly proposed measures require manufacturers to secure central approval for antimicrobial licenses, coupled with enhanced quality assessments. Wholesalers will also need distinct licenses for bulk drugs, promoting improved monitoring. Stakeholders are encouraged to provide public comments on these draft amendments prior to their finalization.

stories.title: Medicines may face tighter checks from factory to pharmacy under new Centre proposal
stories.summary: The Centre is proposing to enhance quality checks for medicines throughout their distribution chain. Good Storage and Distribution Practices are to be integrated into the existing Drugs Rules to ensure safety. This initiative aims to address risks associated with the supply chain, including contamination and unauthorized distribution. Stakeholders have been invited to submit their objections and suggestions to the proposed guidelines.

stories.title: Christie’s Auction Withdrawal: Christie’s pulled Kahlo painting; 1953 return complicates export claims
stories.summary: In a surprising turn of events, a rare Frida Kahlo painting was pulled from a New York auction at Christie’s. The auction house raised concerns over the artwork's ownership provenance, especially its ties to Kahlo's iconic Casa Azul. Mexican officials are now on the hunt for necessary documentation to verify its legal status, with Christie’s optimistic about reintroducing the piece after thorough investigations.

stories.title: Nepal PM Balen Shah's first India visit on November 23, talks with PM Modi on agenda

Bristol's 600-year-old Ashton Court Mansion could finally be restored after councillors backed a 125-year lease to a community trust, but the group has raised only £125,000 toward its early funding target
stories.summary: Ashton Court Mansion, a historic building in Bristol, has been neglected and is in poor condition. The Bristol City Council has approved a 125-year lease for the Ashton Court Mansion Trust. The trust aims to restore the mansion and enhance community access, with a financial target of £480,000. They have raised £125,000 through a community share offer, showcasing public interest in the project.

stories.title: Supreme Court refuses separate listing of plea challenging split verdict on EC law
Florida student meets 7-year-old boy whose life she saved
Canadian man discovers long-lost half-brother in Netherlands after 80 years
'Impossible for us to accept': Rahul Gandhi's response to question on Pakistan talks
Rahul Gandhi calls India a ‘side player’ in geopolitics; BJP hits back with ‘Pak fanboy’ jibe
Prosecution Withdrawal: Powys Council drops case; renovation approval remains unconfirmed
stories.summary: A group of four friends took on a challenging planning dispute with Powys County Council after acquiring Llanerchydol Hall. Their efforts, including an investment of £700,000, led to the withdrawal of the council's case just before trial. This historic mansion, built in 1776, boasts rich heritage, and the owners' goal is to create a sustainable business by welcoming guests into completed rooms. However, the comprehensive restoration remains an ongoing project.

stories.title: America’s rarest fish is bouncing back: Biologists diving into Nevada’s Devils Hole counted 137 pupfish this fall, nearly double the 69 found a year earlier in the only place the species lives in the wild
stories.summary: Devils Hole pupfish, a rare species, has seen population numbers increase significantly after a near extinction event. Recent surveys indicated 137 individual fish, more than doubling from previous counts. Conservation efforts, including releasing captive-raised fish, have contributed to the recovery of their population. Despite positive signs, challenges such as environmental disturbances and habitat vulnerability remain a concern for their future.

stories.title: Supreme Court declines Tamil Nadu's plea seeking 11 TMC Cauvery water from Karnataka
Saskatoon turned 10,000 pounds of plastic waste into three giant sculptures
‘Kashmir free of local terrorists after 35 years’: Amit Shah calls for stronger anti-terror strategy
A black briefcase, a nuclear arsenal: What Putin's Cheget can actually do
Trump's $48.3b Iran war bill excludes damaged US bases; Democrats press for tally
stories.summary: The financial cost of the US war against Iran has reached an estimated $48.3 billion. Lawmakers are urging the Pentagon to provide assessments of damages to military bases. Democratic senator Richard Blumenthal pressed for damage estimates during a Senate Armed Services Committee meeting. According to reports, Iranian attacks have resulted in billions of dollars in losses, including damage to key facilities.

stories.title: Opposition MPs question FCRA panel methods
French woman’s €20 flea market find fetches €251,000
stories.summary: A woman from France stumbled upon a remarkable black ceramic lamp at a local brocante for only €20. Months later, her daughter discovered an inscription revealing the lamp was crafted by Georges Jouve. They reached out to a Paris auction house, which confirmed its authenticity. This led to a stunning auction result of €251,000, setting a record for a Jouve lamp.

stories.title: 'I call for Imran Khan's release': UN rights chief raises alarm over jail conditions
A nuclear blast might be humanity’s best shot at nudging a killer asteroid off course
stories.summary: In an intriguing twist of space science, researchers are exploring nuclear explosions as a potential solution to divert asteroids threatening Earth. Their latest simulations reveal that the angle of X-ray emissions plays a crucial role in determining how effective these deflections may be. With diverse asteroid shapes adding complexity to the challenge, the developing model aims to offer improved predictions of how asteroids will respond to such drastic measures.

stories.title: Illinois man Alexandros Paporakis pleads not guilty to charges over foiled shooting at Hindu temple
Newer BS-VI vehicles get 3-year PUC validity, older vehicles face more frequent tests
stories.summary: The government has announced a three-year extension for Pollution Under Control Certificates for private BS-VI vehicles. Owners of BS-IV vehicles must now renew their certificates every six months, tightening existing norms. For BS-I to BS-III vehicles, the renewal interval has changed to three months. Additionally, different schedules are prescribed for commercial BS-VI vehicles based on their age.

stories.title: Who is Kirsten Davies? White House names new US cyber chief after Cairncross exit
Resignation not admission of wrongdoing, I am innocent: Justice Yashwant Varma to Parliament
'Compromised PM can never sit at this table': Rahul Gandhi shares 'G3' leaders' picture, targets Modi
Fiona the hippo dies after visitor’s hat triggers fatal medical emergency at Cincinnati Zoo
'Everybody's got an opinion': Rahul Gandhi explains why he is called a youth leader at 56
Hello, Earth! Nasa's Voyager 1 phones home from beyond 16 billion miles
US prosecutor declines charges against white cop who killed Black man
stories.summary: A police officer in Wisconsin will not be charged for fatally shooting a Black man in July. Prosecutor Ismael Ozanne concluded that the officer acted reasonably in the situation involving Corey Ruiz. Ruiz allegedly resisted arrest, brandished a knife, and was unaffected by Tasers before he was shot. Family members of Ruiz criticized the decision and claimed excessive force was used in the incident.

stories.title: SC allows German mother to take child to Singapore, grants dad visitation rights
SC nixes ED plea, upholds interim bail to Azam Khan
ED didn't follow norms, says court, gives relief to businessman in AJL case
Women should get 33% quota in legal profession, says SC judge
BJP cites Moily remark to claim Congress tried to 'frame' PM Modi
stories.summary: M Veerappa Moily criticized the disruption of an investigation into Prime Minister Narendra Modi by certain Congress members, clarifying that former PM Manmohan Singh was not involved. BJP officials viewed Moily's claims as a display of political vendetta against Modi. Furthermore, Moily linked Amit Shah’s past legal issues with political motivations, prompting the BJP to seek an explanation from Congress regarding these serious allegations.
